stories.title: Married couple kidnapped at midnight in Prayagraj:3 men held after allegedly molesting woman, looting 2 iPhones
stories.summary: A married couple who had arrived in Prayagraj from Mumbai was allegedly kidnapped at midnight in Kareli. The couple was travelling in an auto-rickshaw when three men in a Maruti Suzuki Dzire allegedly intercepted them, dragged them into their car and fled. The accused allegedly sexually harassed the woman during the journey and robbed the couple of two iPhones. After the couple raised an alarm, passersby alerted the police. Officers chased the accused for around 3.5 km and eventually intercepted their car in Shahganj, rescuing the couple. The incident took place at around 2:40 am on Tuesday. The three accused were sent to jail at around 4 pm on Wednesday. Police also recovered the car allegedly used in the crime. The accused had the words "Government of India" written on the vehicle. Couple had arrived from Mumbai on July 27 The 21-year-old man, a resident of Bakshi Bazaar in Khuldabad, works for an IT company in Mumbai. He told police that he had married his friend, who also works in Mumbai, about a week earlier. The couple arrived in Prayagraj by flight on July 27 and checked into the Urban Residency Hotel near Prayagraj railway station. At around 1:30 am, the man's wife suddenly developed a severe cough. He went around the railway station looking for medicine but found that the medical stores were closed. Couple was heading to Apollo Pharmacy The man told police that an auto-rickshaw driver informed him that an Apollo Pharmacy remained open throughout the night. He then took his wife in an auto-rickshaw to get medicine. According to his complaint, a Swift Dzire approached them from behind. The vehicle had "Government of India" written on its front, and the occupants began following them. At around 2:40 am, when the couple reached between Pahalwan Chauraha and Labour Chauraha in GTB Nagar, Kareli, the car overtook and stopped their auto. Before the couple could understand what was happening, the three men allegedly got out of the car and dragged both of them inside. The accused then drove away. The man alleged that he was beaten when he resisted and that his wife was sexually harassed. The accused also allegedly took both their iPhones. Accused allegedly discussed taking couple to a hideout According to the man, the three accused kept discussing where to take the couple, allegedly referring to two possible hideouts. He said they appeared to be discussing harming the couple and disposing of them after reaching the location. The couple continued shouting for help, following which a passerby alerted the police. Police then began chasing the car. The accused allegedly drove around for nearly 15 minutes in an attempt to escape. After a chase of around 3.5 km, police stopped the vehicle in Shahganj and rescued the couple. Accused allegedly targeted passengers at night During interrogation, the accused identified themselves as Suraj Singh, Ashish Singh and Sunil. Police said Suraj is originally from Holagarh and had been staying in Panchsheel Colony in Civil Lines. Ashish is from Kunda in Pratapgarh, while another accused, Suraj, is from Vigahra in Kaushambi, according to the police account. The accused allegedly told police that they would drive around the area near the railway junction at night and target passengers for robbery. They allegedly assaulted and robbed people travelling alone whenever they spotted them on the road. Three accused sent to jail DCP Manish Kumar Shandilya said the three accused were produced before a court and subsequently sent to jail. "The couple's mobile phones and the car used in the incident have been recovered from them," he said.

stories.title: Class 5 student dies after clash with fellow student:Principal, entire staff suspended; father alleges son was strangled
stories.summary: A Class 5 student died after allegedly being attacked by another student at a government school in Uttar Pradesh's Kaushambi. The boy's father alleged that the accused student strangled his son and that teachers failed to intervene during the fight. The 13-year-old student, Vihan, died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Prayagraj at around 9 am on Wednesday. Following his death, angry family members and villagers brought his body to the school and staged a protest. As the situation escalated, the school staff reportedly fled the premises. ASP Amita Singh and CO Chail Shivank Singh reached the spot with police forces and tried to pacify the protesters. However, the family remained firm on its demand for action against the school staff. Following the incident, Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Kamalendra Kushwaha suspended the principal, Yogesh Singh, and six other staff members. Boy complained of throat pain after returning from school Vihan, a Class 5 student at a primary school in the Charwa police station area, was the son of Biru Rathore, an auto-rickshaw driver from Paharpur Sudhwar village. According to the family, Vihan returned home after school on Thursday. While eating, he complained of pain and difficulty in his throat. When his mother asked what had happened, he reportedly told her that another student had strangled him at school. The boy allegedly said he was experiencing severe pain and difficulty breathing. He also reportedly told his family that he had informed the principal and class teacher about the incident, but no one paid attention. The family initially believed that the injury was minor and that he would recover. First, see 2 pictures Condition deteriorated, student dies during treatment When Vihan's condition worsened on Friday, his family took him to the district hospital. He was subsequently shifted to a private hospital in Prayagraj. As his condition failed to improve, he was later admitted to Arogyavaram Hospital in Prayagraj. His condition continued to deteriorate and he died at around 9 am on Wednesday. Family reaches school with body, villagers protest After Vihan's death, his family took his body directly to the school. By then, the entire school staff had reportedly left the premises. Around 150 villagers gathered at the school and began protesting. CO Chail Shivank Singh reached the spot with police personnel from two police stations. Police tried to pacify the protesters, but Vihan's father alleged that the students had been fighting for a considerable time and that teachers failed to intervene despite witnessing the incident. He said the family would not leave until action was taken against the teachers. As the protest intensified, the CO informed senior officials. ASP Amita Singh subsequently arrived with additional police personnel and assured the family of action. She also informed Kaushambi District Magistrate Dr Amit Pal about the situation. On the DM's directions, BSA Kamalendra Kushwaha suspended principal Yogesh Singh and all other staff members. The family subsequently agreed to take the body for the last rites. Villagers allege teachers spend time on phones Villagers said they send their children to the school trusting the teachers. Around 150 students from Classes 1 to 5 study there, with seven teachers, including a Shiksha Mitra. They questioned why the teachers did not intervene if a fight had broken out between the students. Villagers also alleged that teachers often remain busy using their mobile phones instead of teaching the children. Police register case, await post-mortem report ASP Amita Singh said the family had reported that the child died following a dispute between students. "A case has been registered based on their complaint. The family has been assured of action, and the body is being sent for post-mortem," she said. Police will also question students at the school. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and the findings of the investigation

stories.title: Man shoots girlfriend three times, then dies by suicide:Couple had argument on road; woman in critical condition
stories.summary: In Meerut, on Wednesday evening, a history-sheeter first shot his girlfriend, then shot himself to death. The young man was shot in the chest, while the young woman was shot twice in the stomach and once in the head. Upon reaching the hospital, doctors declared the young man dead, while the young woman's condition remains critical. The incident occurred around 4:30 PM at zonal park in Defense Enclave Colony, Kanker Khera. According to eyewitnesses, the young man arrived on a Pulsar and the young woman arrived on a scooter. They stood near the park talking for some time. Soon an argument broke out between the two. The young man pulled out a country-made pistol and shot the young woman three times. The young woman fell to the ground, writhing in pain. When people nearby rushed over, the young man immediately placed the pistol to his own chest and shot himself. When the police arrived, they called an ambulance and took both to Kailash Hospital, from where they were referred to Subharti Medical College. Both are residents of Kankarkheda According to the police, the injured girl has been identified as Anushka (23), a resident of Govindpuri, Kankarkheda, and the deceased youth as Aditya (26), a resident of Shivlok Pura Colony, Kankarkheda. Aditya is an ITI graduate and also a history-sheeter of Kankarkheda police station. Kankarkheda police station officials and a forensic team reached the spot. They collected evidence from the scene and also recovered a pistol. Police are also scanning nearby CCTVs to ascertain activities before and after the incident. Police are questioning the families of both SP City Vinayak Bhosale said, “In the CCTV footage, there was an argument between the young man and the young woman. After this, the young man shot her. The families of both are being questioned. After this, further action will be taken.”

stories.title: Five cyber criminals held for siphoning crores from poor people:Police seize 43 ATM cards and 12 passbooks
stories.summary: The Cyber Crime Police of Varanasi Commissionerate has busted an interstate gang involved in cyber fraud. The gang used mule bank accounts and APK files to defraud unsuspecting people. Five gang members have been arrested. Police recovered 15 Android mobiles, three iPhones, 43 ATM cards, 12 passbooks, 10 chequebooks, 11 QR codes, 12 SIM cards, one laptop, one diary, two four-wheelers (Mahindra Thar and Hyundai i-20), and ₹12,060 cash from the possession of the accused. During interrogation, it was revealed that the gang used to open bank accounts in the name of poor and needy people and take possession of their ATM cards, passbooks, and internet banking details. These accounts were used for transactions of money obtained through cyber fraud across the country. Police have registered a case and started investigating the criminal history of the accused. On Wednesday, DCP Crime Neetu Kadyan revealed the arrest of a gang of cyber criminals in the Police Line Auditorium. The DCP informed that the team has apprehended five notorious criminals of an interstate cyber gang. The investigation into the complaint of fraud from a businessman's account revealed links to a gang of cyber criminals. With the help of preliminary investigation and the surveillance team, one was apprehended. The arrested accused revealed that they formed cyber gangs and provided mule bank accounts to active cyber criminals across the country. The gang used to lure innocent and economically weak individuals with money and open accounts in various banks in their names. ATM cards, passbooks, checkbooks, SIM cards, internet banking IDs, passwords, and other banking documents were taken from the account holders, thereby gaining complete control of the accounts. The accused would then make these accounts available to their other cyber criminal associates and foreign cyber criminals. By obtaining transaction APK files from foreign cyber criminal associates, installing them on devices with mobile numbers linked to the accounts, and providing access, money obtained through cyber fraud is transferred into these accounts. This money is then subsequently transferred to other accounts at various levels, thereby committing cyber fraud. 8 to 15 per cent commission During interrogation, it was revealed that the gang members took 8 to 15 per cent commission on the money extracted from cybercrime. The gang members would then distribute it among themselves. It has been learned that the accused purchased Mahindra Thar and Hyundai i-20 cars with the money earned from cybercrime, and their EMIs were also paid from this illegal money. During the investigation, important digital evidence related to bank accounts, cyber transactions, suspicious chats, Telegram communication, and cybercrime was obtained from the accused's mobile phones, laptops, and other digital devices. This evidence is currently undergoing scientific examination. Arrested members of the gang: 1. Adarsh Chaubey son of Mithilesh Chaubey, resident of Ramgarh, Police Station Chunar, District Mirzapur (Current address - Varuna Enclave, Police Station Cantt, Varanasi) 2. Ashish Yadav son of Omkar Yadav, resident of Tofapur Bindwal, Police Station Bilariaganj, District Azamgarh (Current address - Varuna Enclave, Police Station Cantt, Varanasi) 3. Sujal Singh son of Vijay Singh, resident of Kawal, Police Station Jansath, District Muzaffarnagar (Current address - Ganpati Enclave Sunderpur, Varanasi) 4. Piyush Singh son of Ramkuwar Singh, resident of Bhikampur, Police Station Ghosi, District Mau (Current address - Kabir Nagar, Bhelupur Varanasi) 5. Yuvraj Verma son of Ashish Verma, resident of Gandhi Nagar, Naria, Police Station Lanka, Varanasi Recoveries from the Accused 15 Android mobile phones 3 iPhones 43 ATM cards 10 Passbooks 8 Chequebooks 11 QR codes

stories.title: Boating at Ramgarh Tal may resume this weekend:AI cameras and geo-fencing to be introduced before operations restart
stories.summary: Boating is likely to resume in Gorakhpur's Ramgarhtal from the coming Saturday. Boating had stopped at the lake after last Sunday's boating accident in which one person lost his life. Initially, preparations are being made to allow boating only from platforms number 1 and 6. The security arrangements of platforms number 4 and 5 are being investigated by separate committees of the district administration and Gorakhpur Development Authority (GDA). The reports from both committees are expected to be submitted by Friday. Strictness on speed boats, new system to be implemented GDA plans to implement several new rules keeping security in focus. Now, after sunset, speed boats will not be able to operate from any platform. Meanwhile, ordinary motor boats will only be able to operate till 9 PM. AI-based speed cameras will be installed on every platform, which will monitor the speed of the boats. If the speed exceeds the prescribed limit, the license of the concerned operator will be revoked and a fine will also be imposed on them. Route will be determined by geo-fencing and blinking lights Geo-fencing will be done in the lake so that boats from every platform operate only on their designated routes. For this, blinking lights will be installed in the water, so that boat operators can clearly see their path even at night and the possibility of accidents is reduced. In addition, AI cameras will also monitor whether any boat is going off its designated path or entering a restricted area. In the future, there are also plans to establish a water police outpost at Ramgarhtal to further improve patrolling and rescue operations. Two committees are investigating the accident A three-member committee constituted by District Magistrate Deepak Meena and a four-member committee of GDA are investigating the accident. Both committees are investigating security arrangements, boat drivers' licences, compliance with contract terms, and the causes of the accident. The GDA Vice Chairman stated that if the investigation report is satisfactory, boating will be resumed by the end of this week with some conditions. Based on the report, administrative and legal action will also be taken against the culprits.

stories.title: After Gen Z, Gen Alpha children protest in UP school:Demand clean water, electricity, toilets
stories.summary: After the Gen Z protest at Jantar Mantar, a video of a Gen Alpha children's movement from Uttar Pradesh has now surfaced. In the video, schoolchildren can be seen protesting to have their basic demands met. This incident is from Sarvodaya Inter College in Kishanpur, Fatehpur district. Children can be seen raising slogans against the school. A boy present at the protest is heard saying in the video that the school toilets are not clean. Children who are still inside the school and want to come out to join the protest against the management are also reportedly not being allowed to leave. The banner in the children's hands reads: "Improve the college system, build the children's future." The students claim that if they raise their voice against the principal of Sarvodaya Inter College, they are also threatened with being failed. The students' protest began at 7 am, once the school gate opened. They were raising their voices against the school's dilapidated buildings, contaminated water, and the principal's poor behaviour towards students. Students stated during the protest that the school toilets are dirty, there is no electricity, and the fans are broken. In addition, there are no facilities for a computer lab, library, or sports. The condition of the school's fans is reportedly so poor that some children have already received electric shocks. The school administration allegedly charges fees from children arbitrarily in the name of admission, and similarly, money is said to be demanded when students ask for mark sheets and other documents. Students remained firm on their demands Students from Classes 6 to 12 took part in the protest. Principal Lal Bahadur Singh and Station House Officer (Kishanpur) Manish Singh initially tried to persuade the students to end the protest, but they refused and remained firm on their demands. The protest continued into the afternoon until District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) Rakesh Kumar arrived at the campus. Kumar spoke with the students and assured them that their demands would be met within 24 hours. Following the protest, the school was closed for the day. After videos of the children's protest circulated, the DIOS confirmed that the students' demands had been accepted. Four fans will now be installed in every classroom by the next day, and the wiring will be fixed. Desks and benches will be provided within a month, and one RO water cooler will be installed. Students' demands accepted Rakesh Kumar told the students that arrangements for clean drinking water at the school would be made immediately. Toilets will be kept clean, and a computer laboratory, library, and sports facilities will also be provided with immediate effect. If illegal fees are being collected from students, this will be investigated, and strict action will be taken against those responsible. Who are Generation Alpha? Generation Alpha includes children born between 2010 and 2024. They follow Generation Z, whose members were born between 1997 and 2012.

stories.title: Student hacks IIT Kanpur website after missing admission:Says 'I just need one chance', director offers a fresh test after seeing his talent
stories.summary: A student hacked the website of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kanpur after failing to secure admission. He had applied for the Bachelor's in Cyber Security programme. On Tuesday, he breached the institute's high-security website and posted the message: "I just need one chance." The student also shared screenshots of the hack on social media platforms X and Reddit, taking responsibility for the breach. The incident caused a stir within IIT, and the matter reached the institute's director. The administration initially considered filing an FIR but later changed its decision, taking the student's future into account. IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal said that if the student genuinely possesses strong cyber security skills, he will be invited back for a fresh test. However, he stressed that illegally breaking into a cyber system is not the right way to demonstrate cyber security expertise. For now, the institute has not disclosed any information that could identify the student, citing concern for his future. Student wrote on hacked website: 'Give me a chance to prove myself' After hacking the website, the student posted the following message: "I completed the entire IIT admission process properly. I submitted my application, paid the fee, uploaded all the required documents, and even provided proof of my work in cyber security. All I want is one opportunity for my abilities to be recognised. I want my skills to be evaluated. My intention was never to harm anyone. I hacked the website only to draw the attention of the institute's cyber security professors. Users can continue using the website by clicking the button below. If you are part of the IIT administration or the cyber security team, I request you to understand my side of the story. I want to explain my situation as a hacker and why I felt compelled to take this step. I have the capability to damage the website, but I was not considered worthy of selection for the B.Cyber programme." Director says student will be invited for a fresh test IIT Kanpur Director Prof. Manindra Agrawal said, "Applications for the four-year Bachelor's in Cyber Security (B.Cyber) programme were accepted from 15 to 25 June this year. A hackathon was held on 5 July as part of the selection process, giving applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. At that stage, this student was unable to prove his capabilities. "Now, to verify his claims, we will invite him to the institute for a fresh test. IIT Kanpur has previously given opportunities to talented young people in cyber security. Recently, a youth who identified a vulnerability in the CBSE online portal was offered a job at the institute's C3iHub." How admission to the B.Cyber programme works Admission to IIT Kanpur's Bachelor's in Cyber Security (B.Cyber) programme is not based solely on JEE Main scores. Students must have completed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM). The selection process begins with an assessment of the candidate's JEE Main performance. The institute also evaluates prior work in cyber security, such as bug bounty programmes, Capture the Flag (CTF) competitions, open-source projects, or other cyber security projects. Shortlisted candidates are then invited to IIT Kanpur, where they undergo a technical assessment and a hackathon to evaluate their practical skills. Final admission is based on a combination of JEE Main scores, cyber security expertise and hackathon performance. Four-year programme The B.Cyber programme spans four years. During the first two years, students study on the IIT Kanpur campus, receiving both classroom instruction and hands-on laboratory training. In the final two years, students undertake internships with government security organisations across India. During these placements, they work on real-world projects involving cyber defence, preventing hacking, and securing government systems.

stories.title: 'Ram Mandir donation thieves, step down':Akhilesh raises slogans outside Parliament; Dimple arrives with donation box to mock govt
stories.summary: SP MPs staged a noisy protest outside Parliament on Wednesday over the alleged theft of Ram Mandir donations. Dimple Yadav arrived carrying a donation box and asked SP MPs and journalists to put money into it. Several SP MPs dropped cash into the box, followed later by Akhilesh Yadav. During the protest, SP MPs raised slogans of, 'Donation thief, step down from the throne'. Dimple Yadav alleged that BJP leaders had "swallowed" public donations. "Such a major incident has taken place in Ayodhya. It is the Chief Minister's responsibility to explain how this scam happened. SITs are formed merely as a formality to divert public attention," she said. Akhilesh Yadav said, "Those who could not even protect a donation box cannot be trusted with anything. The message is clear: if they can play with people's faith, they can also play with the future of our youth." Proceedings in the Lok Sabha were disrupted as soon as the House convened at 11 am on Wednesday, with opposition MPs raising slogans. Amid the uproar, the House was adjourned till noon. After reconvening, discussion resumed on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, related to paper leaks. The House continued the debate for a second consecutive day after a nine-hour discussion on Tuesday. Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad says government is protecting 'big fish' Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad said, "It is unfortunate that the BJP and its government are protecting the big fish. This government came to power because of Ayodhya, and it will fall because of Ayodhya. That process has already begun. The BJP will not win even 50 seats. This is not Awadhesh Prasad speaking; it is the will of the Lord."

stories.title: Former minister's wife faints as funeral procession begins:Brother accuses MLA's caretaker of murder, complains to Lucknow Police
stories.summary: A new twist has emerged in the death case of Nanakdeen Bhurji, the State General Secretary of BJP's Backward Class Morcha and a former State Minister. Nanakdeen's younger brother has filed a complaint at Hazratganj Kotwali, accusing Muhammad Arif, the caretaker of Ballia's Belthara Road MLA Hansuram, of murder. However, the police say that the investigation so far and the evidence found at the scene point towards suicide. Investigation is ongoing, keeping both aspects of the case in mind. Nanakdeen's last rites will be performed on Wednesday at Bhaisakund. Nanakdeen's final journey began on Wednesday morning from his residence in Khadra, Madeganj. During this, his wife Manju Devi fainted. Nanakdeen Bhurji died on Tuesday, 28 July, after falling from the seventh floor of the new MLA residence in Darulshafa. Nanakdeen reached the MLA's residence at 2 PM According to the police, on Tuesday afternoon around 2 PM, Nanakdeen Bhurji reached the new MLA residence of BJP MLA Hansuram from Belthara Road. The MLA was not present at that time. Nanakdeen asked the helper present there to bring coffee and sat in the room. Helper returned with coffee to find the chair empty According to the police, when the helper returned with coffee, Nanakdeen was not in the room. Meanwhile, noise was heard outside. People went downstairs and found Nanakdeen Bhurji lying on the ground in serious condition. Police, who arrived on information, immediately took him to the civil hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Brother accused of murder After the incident, Pradeep Kumar Gupta, the younger brother of the deceased, filed a complaint with the Hazratganj police, accusing Mohammad Arif, caretaker of MLA Hansuram, of murder. He has demanded an impartial investigation and action in the matter. The police conducted a post-mortem of the body and handed it over to the family. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and other evidence. According to family members, Nanakdeen Bhurji's last rites will be performed on Wednesday. Police say that every aspect of the case is being thoroughly investigated.

stories.title: Religious conversions carried out in Lucknow for 20 years:Locals say children cover their ears at the sound of bhajans
stories.summary: An organised network of religious conversion was operating in the Mohanlalganj (about 21 km from Lucknow) for about 20 years under the guise of prayer meetings. The gang first identified people in villages who were sick, childless, poor, and struggling with family problems. After this, they were invited to prayer meetings with temptations such as curing illness, having children, getting jobs, and arranging marriages. The newly converted were given ₹1 lakh to ₹3 lakh and a job based on their caste. After changing their religion, these same people trapped other people they know through the same temptations. Children are taught to stay away from the worship of Hindu deities and prasad. Children in the newly converted families would cover their ears as soon as they heard the sound of bhajans and kirtans. This network was spread not only in Mohanlalganj but also in surrounding villages and up to the border of Rae Bareli district. After the revelation of the conversion gang, a Dainik Bhaskar team reached Devaria Bharsawan in Mohanlalganj and found surprising information. The villagers said that those who have converted from Hinduism to Christianity are annoyed by devotional songs (bhajan-kirtan) and worship. Even the children in their homes cover their ears as soon as they hear the sound of bhajan-kirtan. 'Threatened for opposing conversion to Christianity' Amit Kumar, a resident of Devariya Bharsawan village in Mohanlalganj, alleges that Chandrabhan, his wife Aarti, Seema, Subala, Daniel, Sheela, and Ajay Rawat from the same village had been pressuring him for a long time to convert to Christianity. He states that the accused had told him that if he started going to church and accepted Christianity, he would have children at home. When he resisted, the accused said, "Do whatever you want; we are not afraid of anyone. We will continue to convert people." Gang apprehended on 22 July According to Amit, on 22 July, all the accused again reached Devariya Bharsawan village. He asked them not to come to the village with the intention of religious conversion, but they did not comply. After this, at around 8:15 PM, Amit informed the police on Dial-112. It is alleged that as soon as the accused learned about the police being informed, they started verbally abusing. Amit tried to stop them there until the police arrived. During this, when he tried to stop their Bolero vehicle, Chandrabhan threatened to run him over. Meanwhile, the police, who arrived on receiving the information, took all seven accused into custody from the spot. After this, Amit Kumar gave a written complaint of the entire incident to the police. Based on the complaint, a case was registered and all seven accused were arrested and sent to jail. Police say that during the investigation, some evidence related to religious conversion has also been found and the entire network is being investigated. Became a target for the gang due to not having children Amit works as a caterer. Amit said that he got married about 10 years ago. He does not have any children. Chandrabhan Rawat was aware of this. Chandrabhan repeatedly spoke of coming to God's refuge and said that they would have children. He used to ask him to come with him to the prayer place. Upon this, he agreed to go, but he said that he would not take any water or medicine there. “Give this in writing on a stamp paper so that no pressure will be put there, because of this, Amit's conversation with Chandrabhan stopped,” Amit recalled. Some time ago he had gone to work. Then Chandrabhan's wife Seema came home and started telling his wife that ‘if God wills, your lap will be filled’. For this, she started asking her to come to the prayer place daily. Similarly, she started luring Jai Prakash of the village as well. Jai Prakash has daughters, whose marriage Seema used to talk about arranging. Said in the video, ‘Let us pray to our God’ On the night of the incident, Amit informed the police and also made a video of the scene. In it, everyone is seen threatening Amit. Chandrabhan's wife Seema is saying, "You worship your God. We will worship our God. No one will be able to do anything." Ram Lal's nephew went to jail a year ago Villagers said that Ram Lal, Chandra Bhan, and Manoj Pasi of the village have converted their religion. Manoj's in-laws live in Mati Alinagar. They have also converted. Since then, every poor and weaker section of the village is being targeted. Ram Lal's nephew Malkhan, a resident of Baktaurikheda, has gone to Kanakaha Jail. After he went to jail, everything remained quiet for a few days, but after some time, everyone again got involved in the work of religious conversion. They would also pressure many people to convert by threatening them. They did not listen to bhajans and kirtans Kaushalya, a resident of the village, said that a Bolero car would come and park in front of her house, in which all the church people would arrive. They would take them home, introducing them as relatives. Everyone wore white clothes and there were also three or four women with them. Everyone would arrive at 8 PM and leave between 11 PM and 12 PM. Chandrabhan, Aarti, Seema, Manoj, and people from Manoj's in-laws' house in Alinagar also used to come. These people would come to see them off. Malkhan, who is Seema's paternal aunt's son-in-law, started it here. He went to jail a year ago. A lot of money comes from religious conversion, and everything was done by luring people with that money. If there was any bhajan-kirtan (devotional singing) in the village, the children from their house would cover their ears. When asked why, the children would say that their family members had told them not to take prasad (offerings) if there was any worship. Devils reside in gods and goddesses; sing the praises of your Lord. Poor families were targeted Poor families were often the target of this gang. Besides Bharsawa village, the accused also converted people from Phulwaria, Jyoti Nagar, and Gaura. Currently, their number has reached close to four thousand. The gang had fixed rates according to caste. They were guided by a church in Kanyakumari. The rates for Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Sheikhs, Sayyads, and Pathans were different. Used to give ₹3 lakh to upper castes and ₹2 lakh to backward castes Upon religious conversion, upper castes were given ₹3 lakh and backward castes ₹2 lakh. They promised to arrange marriages for unmarried men with girls who had already converted. Dalits received a proposal of ₹1 lakh, a job, and marriage. Now, most of the poor families are falling for their deception. Gaurakshaks also arrived upon receiving information Vimlesh Sharma of Shri Ram Sanatan Sevak Team stated that many families in villages around Bharsawa village have also been converted. On the day of the incident, as soon as we received information, we also arrived. Even on that day, we warned them to leave from there, but everyone was bent on bullying. After this, the police were informed. This work of religious conversion had been going on for about 20 years. ADCP South Rallapalli Vasanth Kumar said- On the night of 22 July, information was received from a caller in Bharsawa village that approximately seven people arrived in a Bolero vehicle, threatening some villagers and offering various inducements, attempting to convert them to Christianity.Considering the seriousness of the matter, the police team reached the spot. All seven accused were arrested. The Bolero car was also seized. All the accused have been sent to jail. The network is being investigated.

stories.title: Businessman's grandson murdered for ₹1 crore ransom:Accused says he needed to repay a ₹36 lakh debt
stories.summary: “I had a debt of ₹36 lakh. My father used to taunt me every month for not depositing the instalment. He called me worthless. Disturbed by this, I planned to kidnap the son of a bullion trader. With the help of AI, I gathered information about the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. I understood how the gang operates and how they demand ransom. I bought a Cambodian mobile number for ₹199 from the internet and created a WhatsApp account on it.” “On Monday evening, I lured Vaibhav with a gift and took him with me. When he started screaming, I got angry. I pushed him to the ground, put my knee on his chest, and strangled him. I stuffed the body into a sack and hid it in the house's basement. After this, I made a WhatsApp call and demanded a ransom of ₹1 crore from Vaibhav's father. To avoid suspicion, I continued to pretend to search for Vaibhav with my family.” This is the confession of computer teacher Sarvesh, alias Bittu Bhatt, accused of murdering Vaibhav, the 10-year-old grandson of a jeweller in Gorakhpur. Police have taken seven people into custody, including Sarvesh's father, brother, and wife. Sarvesh had been imprisoned for 40 days in Prayagraj's Naini Jail in 2024 in connection with a paper leak case in Bihar. He got married a year ago. Today, Vaibhav's last rites will be performed in Ayodhya. Find out when Vaibhav went missing and how the accused was caught. Lakshmi Narayan Verma lives in Khajni town. He is among the big jewellery businessmen in the area. Vaibhav, the youngest son of Hanuman, Lakshmi Narayan's son, studied in the fourth grade at Navels Academy. The accused Sarvesh's house is 20 meters away at the end of the same lane where Vaibhav's house is. Sarvesh's father Harinarayan owns a cloth shop. His elder brother Satish is a lawyer. Sarvesh himself runs a computer coaching centre, where diploma courses and TET preparation are offered. On Monday at 1:30 PM, Vaibhav returned from school. After reaching home, he kept his bag, changed his uniform, and left the house with his bicycle. Thirty minutes later, a neighbour came home and informed that Vaibhav's bicycle was lying behind the house. His grandmother reached 50 meters from the house, but Vaibhav was not seen. She searched nearby, but she could not find Vaibhav. The grandmother informed the family. One of Vaibhav's slippers was found lying in an empty field 100 meters away from where the bicycle was found. The family suspected kidnapping. The police were immediately informed. SSP Dr Kaustubh immediately formed five teams. One team started scanning CCTV footage. In a CCTV footage, Vaibhav was seen going towards the field with his neighbour Sarvesh Bhatt. Police apprehended Sarvesh. During interrogation, he confessed to his crime. Vaibhav's body was sent for post-mortem examination by a panel of two doctors on Tuesday. Its videography was also done. The post-mortem report confirmed that Vaibhav was strangled to death. After the post-mortem, the child's body was sent home by ambulance. After the incident, an angry mob entered the police station. They tried to pull out the accused kept in the lockup. Police acted strictly and dispersed the crowd. Killed and hid the body in the house's basement Sarvesh told the police, 'He had taken a loan of ₹25 lakh from a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC). Its monthly installment of ₹28,700 had to be paid. Besides this, he had borrowed 11 lakh rupees from a friend. Thus, he had a total debt of 36 lakh rupees. To repay this debt, he planned Vaibhav's kidnapping. He said, "Vaibhav was passing in front of the house. I stopped him and said that I have a gift for you, come with me. He refused and said he would complain to his father. However, he later agreed. I took him to the field at the edge of the house and strangled him to death. After the murder, the body was put into a sack. In the afternoon, he reached home with the sack. At that time, his father, wife, and sister-in-law were in their respective rooms. He placed the sack containing the body among the grain sacks in the basement and covered it with a quilt and a mattress. SP South Dinesh Puri said, “When the police searched the accused's mobile phone, they found several AI-generated questions and their answers. These included information related to Lawrence Bishnoi gang's extortion methods and gang activities. Police also found a Cambodian SIM card with him. The accused had also prepared a mule (fake) bank account.” Notice pasted on the accused's under-construction building The District Panchayat has pasted a notice on the under-construction building of the accused's father, Harinarayan, located in Rudrapur. The District Panchayat states that the building's map has not been approved. The notice instructs to visit the office within three days to get the map approved. Failure to comply will result in action under the law.

stories.title: Yogi offers prayers at Gorakhnath Temple on Guru Purnima:Pays tributes to late Mahant Avaidyanath; feeds jaggery and gram to cows
stories.summary: On the occasion of Guru Purnima on Wednesday morning, Gorakshpeethadhishwar and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath performed special puja of Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath with due rituals at Gorakhnath Temple. After this, he paid tribute to the gurus of Nathpanth, including his guru Brahmaleen Mahant Avaidyanath and Dadasguru Mahant Digvijaynath. During the worship, CM Yogi also offered prayers at all the major deities and the samadhis of the Brahmaleen Mahants located in the temple complex. According to the tradition of Nathpanth, Mahaprasad of 'rot' (bread) was offered to Guru Gorakhnath. After this, the Chief Minister reached the temple's cowshed and fed jaggery and gram to the cows. After leaving the cowshed, the Chief Minister also offered prayers at the ancient Kali Mata Temple. After this, he reached the 'Janata Darshan' (public audience), where he listened to petitioners' grievances and instructed the officials to ensure their speedy resolution.

stories.title: CM Yogi hears 200 complainants on Guru Purnima:Orders officials to ensure every grievance is resolved
stories.summary: On the occasion of Guru Purnima, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath met with people who had come to Janta Darshan, organised outside the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan located within the Gorakhnath Temple complex. The CM listened to the problems of about 200 complainants. He assured everyone that their complaints would be resolved. The Chief Minister himself went among the people and listened to their problems one by one. He instructed the officials that every complaint should be resolved seriously, sensitively, and in a time-bound manner. There will be no shortage of money for the treatment of serious patients Many people arrived at Janta Darshan seeking financial assistance for the treatment of serious illnesses. The Chief Minister assured that no one's treatment would stop due to lack of money. He instructed officials to quickly prepare an estimate for the patients' treatment and send it to the government, so that financial assistance can be provided on time. Some people from Ghazipur and Deoria complained about not getting possession of their land. The Chief Minister instructed officials to coordinate with the officials of the concerned districts to investigate the matter and ensure that eligible people get possession of their land. Gave chocolates to children, inquired about their well-being In the Janta Darshan, the Chief Minister gave chocolates to the children who came. He inquired about the children's well-being and also spoke with their family members. Before the Janta Darshan, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath visited the cowshed in the Gorakhnath Temple complex. Here, he fed jaggery and bread to the cows. Taking stock of the cowshed's arrangements, he instructed the staff to maintain cleanliness and ensure better care for all cows.

stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Sambhal, trees swept away in Gonda:Floodwaters enter 50 temples in Varanasi, 100 families flee homes in Ballia
stories.summary: Rivers across Uttar Pradesh are in spate following heavy rainfall in the hills. In Ballia, floodwaters from the Saryu River have entered villages, forcing around 100 families to leave their homes. In Varanasi, the Ganga has inundated more than 50 small and large temples. In Gonda, the Ghaghara River is eroding its banks at a rapid pace. Several bighas of farmland and many trees have already been washed away. Fearing further erosion, residents are demolishing their homes and migrating to safer places. Sambhal received heavy rainfall at around 11 am on Wednesday, leaving roads waterlogged. A rain alert has been issued for 60 districts across the state today, with six districts under a heavy rainfall warning. On Tuesday, rain was recorded in 55 cities across Uttar Pradesh. In Noida, heavy evening showers left roads submerged in waist-deep water, with cars and motorcycles stranded underwater. Four children were swept away in rainwater drains in Shrawasti, Bareilly and Bulandshahr. In Shrawasti, two young children who were washed away died. An eight-year-old boy in Bareilly and an 11-year-old schoolgirl in Bulandshahr remain missing. Bulandshahr recorded the state's highest rainfall in the past 24 hours, receiving 44.9 mm rain. Since 1 June, Uttar Pradesh has recorded 25% below-normal rainfall. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon trough is once again shifting towards Uttar Pradesh, while the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is also strengthening. As a result, both eastern and western parts of the state are likely to receive widespread rainfall. Several districts may witness light to moderate rain, with heavy showers at isolated places, till 30 July. There is also a possibility of lightning in some areas."

stories.title: 122 UP MLAs are turncoats, what lies ahead till 2027?:Ministers and MPs are no different, 30% of BJP legislators switched from other parties; see list
stories.summary: The buzz about party switching in UP politics has intensified again. It is very difficult to say which leader will be in which party before the 2027 assembly elections. Opportunism exists in every state of the country, but UP's political leaders are at the forefront of it. Some leaders are such who joined every party when they got the opportunity. Some leaders came back, but when they got the chance, they left the party again. UP government minister Dara Singh Chauhan has changed parties 5 times. When Dainik Bhaskar scrutinized 15 years of records, the picture of UP regarding turncoat leaders turned out to be shocking. Out of UP's current 399 MLAs, 30% i.e., 122 MLAs are turncoats. MPs also did not lag behind in changing parties when they got the opportunity. First, let's talk about UP's MLAs 78 MLAs reached BJP after being in other parties Ministers who changed party once Every second of our MPs changed parties Leaders from other parties behind SP's good performance Uttar Pradesh has 80 MPs in the Lok Sabha. Among them, SP's MPs are the biggest defectors. Out of 37 MPs, 19 have changed parties and joined SP. This is approximately 51%. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP achieved its best performance in its history, securing 37 seats. Leaders who came from other parties made a significant contribution to the SP's success. BJP has 33 MPs from UP in the Lok Sabha. Among them, 15 have joined BJP from other parties. Thus, about 45% of the party's MPs are defectors. Only 18 MPs are from the BJP cadre. Among alliance partners, 50% of RLD's MPs fall into this category. Out of RLD's total 2 MPs, one has defected. In Congress too, 50% of MPs joined the party sensing a political opportunity. Out of Congress's 6 MPs, 3 are defectors. These include Imran Masood, Rakesh Rathore, and Ujjwal Raman Singh. While Rahul Gandhi, Kishori Lal Sharma, and Tanuj Punia are staunch Congress members. Ministers who changed party twice Prominent figures who changed parties twice BJP MP SP Singh Baghel from Agra has changed parties twice. Mulayam Singh Yadav brought him into politics. In 1998, he became an MP for the first time from Jalesar on a SP ticket. After differences with Ramgopal Yadav, he left SP. In 2010, he joined BSP and went to Rajya Sabha. Just before the 2014 elections, he joined BJP. Since then, he has continuously been an MP from Agra on a BJP ticket (2014, 2019, 2024). Ministers who changed party 3 times Sakshi Maharaj, who first became an MP from Mathura on a BJP ticket in 1991, was an MP from Farrukhabad in 1996 and 1998. When BJP denied him a ticket in 1999, he joined the Samajwadi Party. He was expelled from the Rajya Sabha in 2006 after his name surfaced in a sting operation related to the MP fund scam. In 2012, he returned to the BJP. He was then elected as an MP from Unnao three consecutive times in 2014, 2019, and 2024. MPs who changed parties Cabinet Minister Nand Gopal 'Nandi' in the Yogi government has been a part of 3 parties in his political career. In 2007, he was elected MLA for the first time from Allahabad City South on a BSP ticket. He became a minister in the Mayawati government. In 2014, he was expelled from BSP on charges of indiscipline. He joined Congress. In the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, he contested from the Allahabad seat on a Congress ticket, but lost. Just before the 2017 UP assembly elections, he joined BJP. MLAs who changed parties Cabinet Minister Rakesh Sachan changed parties twice. He became an MLA on a Samajwadi Party ticket in 1993 and 2002. In 2009, he was elected MP from Fatehpur Lok Sabha seat. Just before the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, he joined Congress. Before the 2022 assembly elections, he joined BJP. He won from Bhognipur assembly seat in Kanpur Dehat. He is a cabinet minister in the Yogi government. Leaders who never changed their party UP government ministers have also benefited from changing parties Dara Singh Chauhan is the minister who has changed parties the most in the UP cabinet. He has changed parties 5 times so far. There are also many ministers who have become MLA, MP and then minister by changing parties once, twice or thrice. Leaders who changed parties twice (with Year) Parties are also adept at changing alliances Parties here have also frequently changed alliances. Currently, the NDA government is in power in UP. It includes BJP along with Apna Dal (S), Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP), and Nishad Party. Among these, Apna Dal and Nishad Party have been with BJP from the beginning. However, RLD and SBSP have changed their political partners from time to time. RLD - Sometimes with BJP, sometimes with SP, sometimes with Congress Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) formed alliances with different parties in different elections. The party has been a part of grand alliances formed sometimes with BJP, sometimes with SP, sometimes with Congress and BSP. Most often, RLD has contested elections with BJP and SP. SBSP: Alliances kept changing over the years Om Prakash Rajbhar's SBSP has also changed its political partners many times.

stories.title: Railway officer's daughter becomes fraudster to get rich:Involves father, gets loans and embezzles the money herself; writes in diary, 'I will become a billionaire'
stories.summary: 'I, Garima Singh, will become a billionaire by April 2026. This is my goal. All my loans will be cleared from April to May. My target is to earn ₹100 crore from April to May. Garima Singh is a crorepati. Thank you, God.' These lines were written in a diary by Garima Singh, daughter of Gorakhpur's Station Superintendent. To fulfill her goal of becoming a crorepati, Garima defrauded more than 10 people of ₹1.67 crore in the name of arranging loans and getting them waived. On Monday, 3rd July, the police of Gorakhpur AIIMS station arrested Garima Singh and her father. The police have recovered a diary from Garima's possession. In it, she used to write daily about her goal of becoming a crorepati. Started fraud to fulfill the desire of becoming a millionaire Dhruv Narayan Singh, a resident of Mahadevi Jharkhandi Colony in AIIMS police station area, is a Railway Station Superintendent in Sahjanwan. He married his daughter Garima Singh to Bhanu Pratap Singh of Sukrauli, Kushinagar in the year 2020. Bhanu Pratap was a contractor. Garima has one son who is 3 years old and another who is 3 months old. When the contracting work weakened, Bhanu came to live with his wife at his father-in-law's house 2 years ago. Dhruv Narayan Singh said, " His daughter had a desire to become rich from the beginning. In this situation, she planned to commit fraud. For this, she read news articles, and read about people who commit fraud on the internet and YouTube. Then, she planned to commit fraud in the name of getting bank loans. She first made her own people victims. Then I also started helping my daughter. Those I knew in the railway, who had taken loans or who needed to take loans. I introduced all of them to my daughter.'' Police said that Garima Singh used to search for two types of people. First, those who needed loans. Second, those who had already taken loans. Garima Singh used to brainwash people to take loans. She would say, ‘You take the loan, I will pay the installments.' Whatever loan amount she got withdrawn from the bank, she would give 10-20 percent to the loan taker. She would get the remaining amount transferred to her own bank account. Now read how the case was uncovered On 1st August, Satyaprakash Singh, who works in the railway, reached AIIMS police station. He told the police that Dhruv Narayan Singh is a Station Superintendent like me. I had a car loan. Dhruv Narayan introduced me to his daughter, Garima. Garima told me that I would get your loan closed in a snap. For this, you will have to take a personal loan. That amount will have to be deposited in my account. I will pay its monthly EMI. Taking my documents, Garima got a total loan of ₹1.67 crore sanctioned from 6 banks - ICICI, HDFC, Yes Bank, SBI, SMFG and Bandhan Bank. She started saying that now I will repay the entire loan. I will also get your car loan waived. She sent about ₹10 lakh to my account as well. She said that this is your profit. Until your loan is not finished, I will keep paying the EMI. Paid EMI for 3 months, then backed out Satyaprakash said, ''Garima deposited the loan EMI for 3 months. Then I started getting calls from the bank. Then I contacted Garima. She would put me off every time. She said don't worry, everything will be done. When she didn't pay the EMI, then I filed a complaint against her.'' Police have registered a fraud case against Garima Singh, her father Dhruv Narayan Singh, husband Bhanu Pratap Singh, his associates Vishal Yadav, Rajendra Kumar, Chandraprakash, Dinkar Mani Tripathi and Sanjay Singh alias Jayprakash Singh. Police arrested father and daughter Garima Singh also defrauded railway employee Mohan Singh, Brahmanand Singh, Dr. Dilip Singh, Dr. Paramatma Singh, Sadhana Mall, Sugreev Singh and Sandeep Pandey. All of them have filed complaints at the CO office. AIIMS police station arrested a father and daughter on Monday. The police team is conducting raids in search of others. The police claim that the absconding accused will be arrested soon. SP City Nimish Patil said that complaints from more people are coming forward. In this case, the father and daughter have been arrested and sent to jail. Action will be taken after investigation in other cases as well.

stories.title: Ban on Kamil-Fazil degrees approved:Yogi cabinet clears proposal; Jewar airport to be linked with Ganga expressway
stories.summary: A cabinet meeting was held on Tuesday at Lok Bhawan under the chairmanship of CM Yogi Adityanath. Many major decisions were approved in it. 'Kamil' (graduate) and 'Fazil' (postgraduate) degrees will not be awarded in madrasas. A new expressway will be built to connect Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. Now, workers will have to be paid double overtime for working more than the stipulated time. Also, at least 50% of the employees' total salary will be basic salary. This will stop the system of paying salaries in the name of allowances. Deep Tech Hubs (U-Hubs) will be built in Lucknow and Noida. The crop insurance scheme for farmers will also continue next year. The government says that these decisions will benefit education, employment, technology, roads, and farmers. Key decisions of Yogi Cabinet- No graduate and postgraduate degrees to be awarded in madrasas The Cabinet has approved an amendment to the UP Madrasa Education Council Act, 2004. Following this, 'Kamil' (graduate) and 'Fazil' (postgraduate) degrees will not be awarded in madrasas. This change is being made in accordance with the Supreme Court's decision of November 5, 2024. The court had deemed the provisions related to these two degrees unconstitutional. U-hubs to be built in Lucknow and Noida The government will establish U-hubs (Deep Tech Hubs) in Lucknow and Noida. Here, research will be conducted on new technologies like AI, Quantum Technology, Semiconductors, and Biotech. Startups and investment will also be promoted. In the first phase, centers will be built in both cities across 25,000 square feet each. Double overtime for working beyond prescribed hours The Cabinet has approved the Uttar Pradesh Wage Rules-2026. Under this, laborers will receive double overtime for working beyond the prescribed hours. Additionally, it will be mandatory to keep 50% of employees' salaries as basic pay. This will provide laborers with greater benefits from PF and other facilities. New development authority for Prayagraj-Chitrakoot The government will establish a new regional development authority by combining Prayagraj, Chitrakoot, Fatehpur, Banda, Kaushambi, and Hamirpur. This aims to promote planned development, better roads, and new employment opportunities in these districts. Development board to be formed for nomadic communities The Uttar Pradesh Nomadic Development Board will be formed for the development of denotified, nomadic, and semi-nomadic communities. This board will survey these communities, prepare their records, and help them avail the benefits of government schemes. Scope of Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana expanded The government has added 14 new trades to the scheme. Now, a total of 25 trades will be included in the scheme. Those undergoing training will receive a loan of up to 10 lakh rupees, 15% subsidy, and a modern toolkit. There will be a provision to disburse the loan within 15 days of bank approval. New expressway to be built up to Jewar airport A 74.46 km long greenfield expressway will be built in Bulandshahr to connect Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. It will be six-lane, which can be expanded to eight lanes in the future. Approximately Rs 8,585 crore will be spent on this project. Agreement with HCL foundation for 5 more years The agreement with HCL Foundation for the 'Samuday' project running in Hardoi district has been extended for the next five years. Under this project, work related to education, health, agriculture, livelihood, and sanitation is being carried out. Crop insurance scheme to continue The government has decided to continue implementing the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Weather-Based Crop Insurance Scheme in the year 2026-27 as well. Farmers will pay 2% premium for Kharif crops and 1.5% for Rabi crops. The remaining amount will be jointly contributed by the central and state governments.

stories.title: Gorakhpur doctor allegedly drugs wife to record nude videos:Remarries without divorcing her; blackmails and threatens to kill her
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a female doctor has made serious allegations against her doctor husband, in-laws (mother-in-law and father-in-law), and sister-in-law. She claims that her husband drugged her and made her unconscious. Then he took nude photos and videos. After that, he started threatening to make them viral. The husband blackmailed her and took 32.50 lakh rupees to buy a Fortuner and 10 lakh rupees from an FD. Then he remarried without divorcing her. When she protested, he tried to kill her. The wife stated that her husband is an unconsciousness doctor (anesthesiologist). He has relationships with several girls. The woman filed a case against her husband, in-laws, and sister-in-law at 9 PM on Monday. The case is from the Shahpur police station area. Spent 50 lakh on wedding, then started demanding Fortuner car A 35-year-old female doctor residing in the Shahpur area is currently posted in Basti. Her father is an engineer. On Tuesday, she filed a case against her husband, in-laws, and sister-in-law for attempted murder, marrying a second time without divorce, assault, and dowry harassment. In the complaint given to the police, she stated, On November 29, 2019, I was married to a doctor residing in Nabhpur, Chhattisgarh. On November 30, I left for my in-laws' house. I am the only child in the family. Therefore, my father spent 50 lakh rupees on my wedding. Despite this, from the very first day at her in-laws' house, she was taunted that even after being the only daughter of an engineer father, they couldn't provide a Fortuner car. Later, her husband also started pressuring her to ask for money to buy a Fortuner. When she refused, along with her husband, her mother-in-law, father-in-law, and sister-in-law also started harassing her. They would drug her, make her unconscious, then make nude videos The woman doctor stated that her husband would drug her by mixing intoxicants in cold drinks and make her unconscious. After that, he would make her nude and record videos. Then he started blackmailing her by showing the videos. He would say that if she didn't arrange the money, he would viral the videos on social media, and she wouldn't be able to show her face anywhere. I told this to my parents. To save the marriage, they arranged money and gave 32.50 lakh rupees to my in-laws on March 28, 2022, to buy a Fortuner. After this, on April 14, 2022, I had a son. Still, my husband's habits did not change. I had an FD of 20 lakh rupees in the Indian Post Office, Alinagar, Gorakhpur. My husband broke it and took 10 lakh rupees. Husband and wife got separate transfers The woman doctor said - Meanwhile, my husband was posted at Balrampur Hospital in Lucknow. But, he used to live in Basti. Whereas, I was posted at Fatehpur Hospital. For a few days, we both worked at different places. After this, I was posted at a hospital in Basti. Upon arriving here, I found out that my husband had been involved with several women. When I asked my husband about this, he started beating me. He repeatedly threatened to divorce me. Meanwhile, on November 26, 2024, I gave birth to a daughter. During this time, I went to my in-laws' house. Husband said - I will keep two wives together The female doctor stated - my husband started keeping a female doctor who works in the anesthesia department with him. He also started bringing her home. When I protested, my husband and in-laws brutally beat me. The in-laws got my husband married to that other female doctor. My husband says that he will keep both wives together. Everyone will earn together. On February 13, 2025, they both went on their honeymoon, taking a flight from Chhattisgarh Airport to Pune (Maharashtra). They stayed there for 4 days. Tied with a rope and hung The female doctor said- My husband remarried without divorcing me. I continuously opposed this. Meanwhile, on May 7, 2026, my husband along with my in-laws beat me up, tied a rope around my neck, and hung me from the fan. However, my life was saved because the rope broke. After this, I was beaten up along with my two children and thrown out of the house. My in-laws came to my house in Shahpur on July 12, 2026, to get a divorce. They wanted to take my son. The father-in-law said that my son has remarried. Sign the divorce papers. I refused, citing the children. At this, my husband along with my father-in-law attacked me, in which I was injured. Shahpur Police Station in-charge Jitendra Kumar Singh said that a case has been registered under serious sections on the complaint of the woman doctor. Strict action will be taken based on investigation and evidence.

stories.title: Champat Rai visits Ayodhya two month after donation theft case:Says he will spend the rest of his life here; holds closed-door meeting with Paramhans Acharya
stories.summary: Champat Rai was seen in Ayodhya on Tuesday, nearly two months after the theft of offerings from the Ram Mandir. He reached the Tapasvi Chhawani Mandir, where Mahant Paramhans Acharya welcomed him by applying a tilak. The two also had a closed-door conversation. Speaking to the media, Paramhans Acharya praised Champat Rai's work, stating that the grand Ram Mandir was built under his leadership. The saint community wishes that Champat Rai remains in Ayodhya for life. The case of theft of offerings from the Ram Mandir came to light in June 2026. Following this, the UP government formed an SIT and started an investigation. An FIR was registered based on the SIT's interim report. So far, eight accused have been arrested. After the incident, Champat Rai had resigned from the post of General Secretary of the Trust. He had stated that he would elaborate on the matter only after the investigation was complete. See 3 pictures Champat Rai called the allegations against him baseless Champat Rai had resigned from the post of General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on June 26, 2026. A meeting of the Trust was held at the Ram Mandir on July 6. Champat Rai's resignation was accepted in this. In place of Champat Rai, new trustee retired IFS Krishna Mohan was made the acting General Secretary. After the meeting, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri had said, Champat Rai has said that it is not right to remain in office until the culprits are caught. What happened is painful. We are all saddened by this. The theft of offerings is a shameful incident. The next day, on July 7, he wrote a letter to Ram devotees on social media platform X, calling the allegations against him baseless. He had said that he would elaborate on the matter only after the SIT investigation was complete.

stories.title: Son-in-law's eyes gouged out, throat slit private parts mutilated:Couple had love marriage 3 years ago; woman's grandparents and uncle-aunt arrested
stories.summary: In Amethi, a man is allegedly killed by his wife's family, who oppose their love marriage. Police say the accused slit his throat, gouged out his eyes, and mutilated his body after dragging him inside their house when he returned from the market. Hearing his screams, the victim's family alerts police after no one opens the door. By the time officers arrive, the accused have fled, and the body is found inside a room. Enraged locals block the road late at night, prompting heavy police deployment. A case is registered against the woman's uncle, aunt, grandmother, and grandfather. Three are arrested, while the uncle is later apprehended after police shoot him in the leg during an encounter. The incident takes place on Monday night in the Gauriganj Kotwali area, and the body is sent for post-mortem after the protest ends. 3 pictures Know the complete case Kallu Kashyap, a resident of Ward No. 17 of Pure Man Singh, had a son, Ankit Kashyap (22), in his family, besides his wife. Housla Yadav's house is about 50 meters away from Kallu's house. Housla's only daughter Shweta, had an affair with Ankit. About 3 years ago, Ankit eloped with Shweta and had a love marriage. After this, Shweta's family members had filed a case of kidnapping of their daughter. Later, the police recovered Shweta and Ankit. Shweta was an adult. She insisted on living with her husband, Ankit. After this, both left home and started living in Delhi. In Delhi, Ankit used to do a private job. He lived there in a rented room. Ankit and Shweta have 2 sons. The elder son is 2 years old, and the younger one is one year old. Ankit returned from Delhi on July 31 It is said that on Friday (July 31), Ankit had come to Amethi to meet his family, leaving his wife Shweta and both children in Delhi. On Monday night, he was supposed to return to Delhi. For this, he went to the market in the evening to buy some items. Around 8:30 PM, when Ankit returned from the market, Shweta's uncle Sukai, aunt Sarita, grandfather Ram Sundar (60), and grandmother Ranjana surrounded and caught him. They dragged him to their house. They locked him in a room and severely beat him with kicks and punches. Then they gouged out his eyes. After that, they cut off his private part. Then they slit his throat. Hearing Ankit's screams, his family members reached the spot, and Shweta's family members fled through the back door. The family members first took Ankit, who was lying covered in blood, to the district hospital in a serious condition. However, seeing Ankit's critical condition, he was referred to Lucknow. Ankit succumbed to his injuries on the way while being brought to Lucknow. Highway blocked at 11 PM As soon as the news of Ankit's death was received, a large number of people gathered at the district hospital around 11:30 PM. People first created a ruckus at the hospital. After this, they blocked the Sultanpur Highway. Seeing the commotion escalate, forces from 7 police stations reached the spot. SP Saravanan T also reached the scene late at night. He pacified Ankit's family members. Only then did the people calm down and the blockade was cleared. SP Saravanan T stated- Last night, a young man was murdered. Its main accused, Sukai Yadav, had absconded. Today, during an encounter in the Tikariya forest, he was shot in the leg. He has been admitted to CHC. Sukhari already has cases registered against him under robbery, theft, and Arms Act. In this case, Sukai's wife Sarita, Sukai's mother Ranjana, and father Ram Sundar were arrested last night.

stories.title: Overbridge stuck for 1.5 years finally ready:Brings relief to 3 lakh Lucknow residents; locals say patients won't die in ambulances now
stories.summary: The overbridge in Kesari Kheda, Lucknow, which was suspended in the air for one and a half years, is now complete. This flyover, built at the railway crossing, will soon open for the general public. However, people have already started using it. The construction of this overbridge began on 17 July 2023, but due to a complex coming in its way, work remained stalled from June 2024 to June 2025. After that, the complex was demolished, and work resumed. Now, most of the flyover's work has been completed. Approximately ₹84 crore have been spent on the construction of this 974-metre long overbridge. Currently, finishing touches are being given before the inauguration of the overbridge. Work on installing streetlights on both sides and painting is underway. The people of the area are eagerly awaiting the opening of the flyover. People say that its opening will provide great relief from traffic jams at the railway crossing. Earlier, ambulances often used to get stuck in jams here. Many times, patients even died. Work had stopped due to the complex coming in the middle of the bridge During the construction of the overbridge, a four-storey complex came in the middle. Due to this, the construction work of the bridge had to be stopped. The work remained closed for about a year. During this period, more than 3 lakh people living within a 3-kilometre radius had to face daily traffic jams. Meanwhile, the business of local traders was also severely affected. 3 lakh people of the area will get relief Local resident Dilip Kumar Srivastava said that this flyover will become a source of relief for 3 lakh people. Since the construction began, there has been a lot of trouble with commuting for the past 3 years. After school, children struggle with traffic jams for hours. Seeing this, they are now breathing a sigh of relief. “A very big work has been done in this area. We are very happy. With the bridge opening, people from dozens of colonies including Kesari Kheda, Manas Nagar, Vijay Nagar, Chunnu Kheda, Prasadi Kheda, Pandit Kheda, Shubham City, Gokul State, Balkrishna Nagar will get relief,” Dilip said. The bridge has reduced the distance by 6 kilometres David Rawat, a resident of Hanskheda, said that the bridge construction will bring great relief. Four-wheelers cause traffic jams at the crossing. Due to the bad road, two-wheelers often met with accidents. Due to the absence of a flyover, one has to travel 6 kilometers extra to commute. He has a 70-year-old mother who is undergoing treatment at Lokbandhu Hospital. Once the bridge opens, the biggest relief will be in taking his mother to the hospital. Traders said will distribute laddoos on the inauguration day Local businessman Deepu Yadav said that there is a traffic jam here for two to three hours daily. This causes problems for school students and they are unable to reach their work on time. Ambulances also face a lot of difficulty in getting through due to the jam. Many times, patients could not be taken to the hospital on time and they died in the ambulance itself. Deepu said that his cement-sand shop is located here, but due to traffic jams and construction work, business was severely affected. “Now the flyover is ready. We are just waiting for its inauguration. On the day the flyover starts, traders will distribute ladoos in happiness,” he said. He said that when the construction work of the flyover was stalled, there was a lot of disappointment. Now, after the completion of construction, there is happiness. It is hoped that people and traders will get relief from the daily traffic jams.

stories.title: Trump-Netanyahu pictures trampled during Chehlum procession:Devotees bleed after chain mourning ritual; girl distributes Melody toffees
stories.summary: On Tuesday, the 40th day of Muharram, the Chehlum procession is being taken out in Lucknow. The approximately 5-kilometer long procession will start from Nazim Sahab Imambara in Chowk and proceed to Karbala in Talkatora. Thousands of people from the Shia community are participating in the procession, dressed in black clothes and barefoot. Outside Imambara Nazim Sahab, pictures of Donald Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, along with the flags of America and Israel, have been placed on the ground. People are trampling on them with their feet as they move forward. At the forefront of the procession, devotees are carrying the approximately 25-foot-high Alam-e-Mubarak of Hazrat Abbas. Many people have also joined the procession carrying pictures of Iran's former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and his son Mojtaba Khamenei. During the procession, a large number of devotees performed matam (self-flagellation) with chains. Marks of injury were visible on the bodies of many devotees due to matam. They appeared to be bleeding. Strict security arrangements have also been made for the procession. During this, a small girl distributed Melody toffees to the people. UP transfers 13 IAS officers:Four commissioners reshuffled; Indra Vikram Singh appointed new Gorakhpur divisional commissioner
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government ordered the transfer of 13 senior IAS officers on Tuesday, including the Divisional Commissioners of Gorakhpur, Basti, Bareilly, and Prayagraj. The administration released the transfer list at approximately 3:15 pm. Saumya Agarwal, who served as Prayagraj's first female Divisional Commissioner, has been reassigned to the post of State Labour Commissioner. Agarwal is married to IPS officer Mohit Gupta. Her tenure drew widespread attention following a controversy involving Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand at the Prayagraj Magh Mela on 18 January 2026. The reassignment follows the recent transfer of Inspector General Mohit Gupta to the Anti-Corruption Organisation. Dr Lokesh M. has been appointed as the new Divisional Commissioner of Prayagraj, succeeding Saumya Agarwal. See the profiles of four senior officers 1. Saumya Agarwal completed her schooling up to intermediate level in Lucknow. After obtaining an engineering degree from Delhi University, she worked for a software company in Pune. She subsequently shifted her focus towards the Civil Services, securing 24th rank in the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination on her very first attempt. Her father, Gyan Chand Agarwal, served as a civil engineer in the Indian Railways. 2. Anil Dhingra has been removed from the post of Gorakhpur Divisional Commissioner and appointed Commissioner of the UP Housing and Development Board. Additionally, he has been entrusted with the responsibilities of Director of Urban Land Ceiling and Secretary to the Housing and Urban Planning Department. A 2008-batch IAS officer, Dhingra originally hails from Delhi. Before joining the Civil Services, he qualified as a Chartered Accountant and completed an MBA at Delhi University. His initial posting was as Joint Magistrate in Farrukhabad, after which he served as Chief Development Officer (CDO) in Rampur. He later served as District Magistrate in Rampur as well. 3. Indra Vikram Singh, who was serving as Secretary to the Agriculture Department, has been appointed as the new Divisional Commissioner of Gorakhpur. Simultaneously, Principal Secretary for Agriculture Ravindra has been given the additional charge of Director of the State Agricultural Produce Markets Board alongside his current responsibilities. Originally hailing from Fatehpur, Indra Vikram Singh began his career as a Provincial Civil Service (PCS) officer. His first posting came in 2011 as Secretary to the Aligarh Development Authority. He was promoted to the IAS in 2016 and has previously served as District Magistrate in both Ballia and Shamli. 4. Bareilly Divisional Commissioner Bhupendra S. Chaudhary has been transferred to the position of Secretary to the Administrative Reforms Department. Shambhu Kumar, who served as Managing Director of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, has been appointed as the new Divisional Commissioner of Bareilly. A 2009-batch Indian Administrative Service officer of the UP cadre, Chaudhary holds a BSc in Botany. Over the course of his administrative career, he has served in various capacities, including Secretary, Special Secretary to the State Government, District Collector, and Director.
