stories.title: BSP names 24 in-charges, most of them will be candidates:Mayawati conducts interviews, asks nephew to lead campaign; caste balance under focus
stories.summary: BSP has opened the election front for the assembly first. The party has so far announced the names of 24 assembly in-charges. Their interviews were taken by Mayawati herself. It has been a tradition of BSP that the leaders who are made assembly in-charges later become the party's candidates. In such a situation, these announcements are being considered as the party's first list of candidates. Akash also fielded, will start from Hathras BSP is not just announcing names, but is also testing the strength of its organisation by holding worker conferences in every assembly constituency. A similar conference will be held on August 10 in the Sadabad assembly constituency of Hathras. For the first time, the party's national convener Akash Anand will participate in it. The party is preparing to give an election message by gathering a large crowd at this meeting. On August 25, Akash Anand will hold a program in Jewar assembly constituency of Gautam Buddh Nagar. Here, the party will declare Satveer Singh Nagar, who has already been decided, as the assembly in-charge. BSP plans to declare candidates' names in a similar manner by holding 2-3 big rallies every month. Akash will respond to Chandrashekhar in his own style In Western UP, there is a good number of Dalit, especially Jatav voters. This has been BSP's strongest vote bank. In recent years, Chandrashekhar Azad, chief of the Azad Samaj Party, has strengthened his hold among Jatav and Muslim voters in Western UP. Due to his young face and aggressive style, a section of Dalit youth has also been attracted to him. In such a situation, Mayawati has tried to answer Chandrashekhar's challenge by fielding Akash Anand. According to political analyst Harshvardhan Tripathi, a large number of Dalit youth attended Akash Anand's rallies in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. BSP now wants to extend the same strategy to the assembly elections as well. Through Akash's electoral debut from Western UP, the party wants to strengthen its organization as well as send a political message. Betting on Brahmin face in Sadabad, Gurjar face in Jewar In Sadabad, BSP has put forward Dr. Avin Sharma. This seat was once considered a stronghold of Ramveer Upadhyay, a powerful BSP leader. He was among the party's prominent Brahmin faces. After his move to BJP, BSP is now trying to re-establish this social equation through Dr. Avin Sharma. His name has already been announced at the party workers' conference. Meanwhile, in the Jewar assembly constituency, BSP has put its trust in Gurjar leader Satveer Singh Nagar. Satveer was a BSP MLA from Dadri in 2007 and 2012. In 2019, he also contested the Lok Sabha election from the Gautam Buddh Nagar seat on a BSP ticket. Considering the significant role of Gurjar voters in Western UP, this move by BSP is considered important. Caste balance seen in the first list of in-charges If you look at the declared list of BSP, the party has tried to give representation to almost all effective social classes. Instead of relying only on the Dalit vote bank, the party is also promoting influential faces from Brahmin, Muslim, OBC, and upper-caste communities. BSP has tried to re-establish the old 'Brahmin-Dalit' social equation by giving responsibility to Brahmin leaders in many seats. The social equation of that assembly constituency is also reflected in the selection of every BSP candidate.

stories.title: First Monday of Sawan sees 3 km queue in Kashi:Flower petals showered after Mangala Aarti, 40,000 Yadav devotees to perform Jalabhishek
stories.summary: Today is the first Monday of Sawan. A huge crowd of devotees has gathered to offer water at Kashi Vishwanath. A 3-kilometer long queue of Kanwariyas has formed. Devotees are getting only 1 second to perform Jalabhishek. Entry of devotees into the sanctum sanctorum is prohibited. Baba's Mangala Aarti took place at 4 AM. After this, the temple gates were opened for darshan. Priests showered flowers on Kanwariyas and devotees. The 3-kilometre area around Kashi Vishwanath Temple has been declared a no-vehicle zone. Entry is available through 6 gates of the temple. Baba Vishwanath is giving darshan to devotees today in the form of Shankar. For security, the temple area has been divided into 5 zones. Baba Vishwanath's abode has been decorated with about 50,000 flowers from Kolkata, the city of Maa Kali. Among these, the temple has been adorned with 3000 marigolds, 1500 rajnigandha, and 500-500 garlands of roses and gerberas. It took 10 to 12 hours to decorate the entire temple. 40 thousand Yadav brothers will perform Jalabhishek of Baba Vishwanath Under the banner of Chandravanshi Gopa Seva Samiti, the 94th annual Jalabhishek Yatra will be taken out this year as well, on the first Monday of Sawan. The committee's president, Lalji Chandravanshi, informed that approximately 40 thousand Yadav brothers will travel about 17 kilometers to perform Jalabhishek and worship at 7 Shiva temples and two other temples, making a total of nine religious sites. 21 Yadav brothers will perform Jalabhishek in the sanctum sanctorum of Kashi Vishwanath. The rest will offer water through the argha. The Jalabhishek Yatra will begin at 7:30 AM from Kedar Ghat. Devotees will first perform Jalabhishek of Gauri-Kedareshwar Mahadev. After this, they will reach Tilbhandeshwar Mahadev. Then, filling Ganga water from Sheetla Ghat, they will perform Jalabhishek of Mata Sheetla and Ahileshwar Mahadev located at Man Mandir Ghat. After this, the yatra will reach Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham, where devotees will perform Jalabhishek and have darshan of Baba Vishwanath. Following this, the yatra will conclude with darshan and Jalabhishek of Mahamrityunjay Mahadev, Trilochan Mahadev, Omkareshwar Mahadev, and finally Latbhairav Baba. Locker facility is closed at Kashi Vishwanath Temple Dham Kashi Vishwanath Temple administration said- There is limited space inside the temple, so devotees will come in a zig-zag line. Water arrangements have been made at various places so that women and the elderly do not suffer in the heat. Medical staff is also present. The most important change is that all locker facilities available in the Dham are closed. Earlier, this facility was available in the Dham. Devotees will only be allowed to carry milk, Ganga water, flowers, datura, etc., for Abhishek (ritual bathing). No other items are allowed inside. Kashi Vishwanath Temple's appeal- It may take 8-10 hours in the queue No vehicles will run from Maidagin to Godaulia throughout Sawan in Kashi Varanasi's ADCP Traffic Anshuman Mishra said that no vehicles will run from Maidagin to Godaulia throughout Sawan. While from Saturday night to Monday dawn, vehicles will not run from Benia to Ramapura-Khari Kuan to Jangambari, from Godaulia to Dashashwamedh Ghat, and from PDR Luxa to Ramapura. The no-entry time for cargo vehicles will continue from Saturday night 8 PM until Tuesday dawn. This will be applicable every week during Sawan. Additionally, routes have been determined for heavy vehicles to bypass the city. Entry for all large vehicles coming from neighboring districts will not be allowed from Saturday night. Vehicles carrying vegetables, fruits, and milk will not be stopped. All buses, trucks, and other large vehicles commuting through Varanasi city from Ghazipur, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Chandauli, Prayagraj, and Bhadohi will be able to use the Ring Road and NH-19. Large vehicles and essential small vehicles will be routed via the Ring Road. Special arrangements for the convenience of devotees at Kashi Vishwanath

stories.title: Man shoots wife, two children before killing himself:Four bodies found together,country-made pistol recovered nearby
stories.summary: A husband, wife, and their two children died from gunshot wounds in Balrampur. The bodies of the husband, wife, and two innocent children were found at 6:50 PM on Friday evening in Gosai Purwa of Jhauna village. Hearing the sound of gunshots, neighbors rushed to the spot. They informed the police about the incident. In the initial police investigation, it was revealed that the husband first shot his wife and both children. After that, he shot himself. However, the police are stating that the real reason for the incident will only come to light after the investigation is complete. The deceased include Bajrang Giri (28), his wife Komal (25), daughter Shraddha (3), and 10-month-old son Jaideep. Police found 2 country-made pistols and empty cartridges As soon as the incident was reported, SP Vikas Kumar, ASP, CO, and Kotwali Dehat police reached the spot. Police sealed the entire house and inspected it thoroughly. Two country-made pistols and several empty cartridges were recovered from the scene. The forensic team collected evidence and sent the bodies for post-mortem. SP Vikas Kumar stated that both brothers of the deceased are being interrogated. Police are investigating mobile phone records, domestic situation, and other angles. The real cause of the incident will only be revealed after the post-mortem report and forensic investigation. Brothers said - We were not at home Ramkumar Giri, brother of the deceased, stated that other family members were not present at home at the time of the incident. Upon reaching home, they found the bullet-ridden bodies of all four. He denied having any knowledge of the reason behind the incident.

stories.title: Rajbhar displays strength with yellow scarf:Says everyone knows who holds power; pressure on BJP for more seats or counter to SP?
stories.summary: Before the UP Assembly elections 2027, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) showcased its strength at Talkatora Stadium in Delhi. In the Social Harmony Maharailey held on Friday, the party's national president Om Prakash Rajbhar attacked the SP. He also claimed a massive victory for the NDA again in 2027. A large number of supporters wearing yellow caps and yellow stoles arrived at the rally. 3 pictures of the rally Read what Rajbhar said at the rally Addressing the rally, SBSP chief and minister Om Prakash Rajbhar accused SP and Congress of betraying Muslims. He said, At the time of independence, the share of Muslims in government jobs was about 38%, which has now reduced to less than 1%.Some parties practice politics of spreading hatred in society. Whereas under the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi, the Muslim community has also become aware of education. The selection of 53 Muslim children in UPSC (Civil Services) is an example of this. Many OBC castes politically deprived Even today in UP, a large number of backward castes including Banjara, Sapera, Prajapati, Lohar, Nai are deprived of political representation. These sections have not received rights proportionate to their population. SBSP workers should take information about the welfare schemes of the central and state governments to every household. The rally was also addressed by party's national general secretary Arvind Rajbhar, Salik Yadav, Sunil Singh and several other senior leaders. Message of seats to BJP, attempt to energise workers In the rally, Party's National General Secretary Arun Rajbhar said that the purpose of the event in Delhi was to show the party's strength to the BJP leadership. At the same time, it was to instill confidence in the workers that SBSP's reach is now up to Delhi. He said that the party is also strengthening its presence in Western UP. With the 'stick' election symbol, it is fully prepared for the 2027 battle. In fact, less than 6 months are left for the announcement of the assembly elections. NDA's allies are pressuring the BJP to clarify the status of the seats they will get in the alliance, so that they can start election preparations on those seats. In recent days, during the visit of BJP National President Nitin Naveen and General Secretary (Organisation) Dharampal Singh to Lucknow, leaders of NDA constituent parties also met them and discussed seat sharing. That is why, after Rajbhar's rally in Delhi, discussions have heated up in the corridors of power from Lucknow to Delhi. Rajbhar has tried to convey to the BJP leadership that his party also has a strong base in the districts of Western UP. Therefore, his party should not be limited only to Purvanchal or Awadh during ticket distribution. Rajbhar said - Who doesn't know who has the power? Omprakash Rajbhar, in a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, said that people used to call Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) a party of the east. However, the party also has a large support base in the western UP districts. Workers from West UP demanded that a rally be held at Delhi's Talkatora Stadium. The rally in Delhi was held based on their proposal. As for strength, who doesn't know who has the power? Rajbhar said that many castes from the Dalit and backward classes participated in the Social Harmony Rally in Delhi. People from such castes participated who are still far from government schemes and the mainstream of development. The objective of his party's rally is to connect such castes, so that they can benefit from social, economic, and political opportunities along with the benefits of government schemes. Beginning of preparations for 2027 Assembly Elections This grand rally held in Delhi is being considered the beginning of SBSP's election campaign for the UP Assembly Elections 2027. The party leadership claims that with the issue of social harmony, it is preparing to increase its support base not only in Purvanchal but also in Western and Central Uttar Pradesh. According to senior journalist Anand Rai, Rajbhar's event is not just a workers' conference, but is considered a political message for both the BJP leadership and the opposition. Om Prakash Rajbhar, who is active in Purvanchal politics, tried to convey through a rally in Delhi that his influence is no longer limited to Purvanchal. His organization is active across Uttar Pradesh and the national capital. Rajbhar continuously attacks SP Om Prakash Rajbhar has been continuously attacking the Samajwadi Party and its president Akhilesh Yadav for some time now. SP was also targeted in the rally. Arun Rajbhar said that this event was organised "to break the arrogance of SP". Even a day before the rally, Om Prakash Rajbhar, cornering Akhilesh Yadav on the issue of the resignation of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, had written on social media that ‘Dharmendra Pradhan was a Kurmi, so his resignation was demanded. If he had been a Yadav, his resignation would not have been demanded.’ Through this, he had accused the SP of doing caste politics.

stories.title: Fire brigade called to extinguish woman's funeral pyre in UP:Father alleges in-laws beat her to death and tried to destroy evidence
stories.summary: In Hathras, on Friday afternoon, a fire brigade vehicle arrived to extinguish a burning pyre of a woman. After the woman's death, her in-laws performed her last rites. No one in her maternal home was even informed. As soon as the villagers came to know about this, they informed the police about the incident. The police immediately called the fire brigade to extinguish the pyre. Fire personnel extinguished the burning pyre by spraying water. After this, the burnt remains of the woman's body were sent for post-mortem. The woman's father has accused her in-laws of murdering his daughter. The incident is from the Sahpau area. See pictures Woman living at her in-laws' house on court orders Nirmala, a resident of Sirsaganj Jaymai in Firozabad, was married to Amit Kumar alias Jackie, a resident of Thraura, in 2012. A year after the marriage, the couple started fighting. After this, Nirmala came to live at her parents' house. Meanwhile, her parents filed a police case against Amit and his family. After fighting the case for 10 years in Firozabad Court, the court ruled in Nirmala's favor 4 years ago. It ordered that Nirmala be given a house in her in-laws' place and 4 bighas of land. After this, Nirmala came to live at her in-laws' house. Nirmala has no children. Her husband Amit works in a factory in Ballabgarh, Haryana. ‘In-laws fled after locking house’ Villagers told the police, On Friday morning, Nirmala argued with her in-laws. Shortly after this, she died. Her body was found lying in the room. Amit's family members did not inform Nirmala's maternal family about this. After hastily cremating the body, they locked the house and fled. ‘Daughter beaten to death’ Father Suresh Chandra said, My daughter's in-laws beat her to death. They didn't even inform me about it. They also burnt her body. After this, everyone fled. Daughter Nirmala was the third among three sisters and one brother. All siblings are married. Her husband, who works in Haryana, has also been informed.

stories.title: Builder brutally assaulted while taking possession of plot:Slapped 11 times, rib broken in attack; suffers 12 stitches to head
stories.summary: A 58-year-old builder from Delhi was brutally assaulted in Ghaziabad in the presence of government officials. He was allegedly slapped 11 times within a minute, thrown to the ground and repeatedly kicked, leaving him with two fractured ribs and a head injury requiring 12 stitches. The builder is currently undergoing treatment at a private hospital, where his condition is reported to be serious. The victim had recently approached the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister seeking possession of his plot. Following the complaint, officials from the ACP's office and the Tehsil administration called him to the site. According to the builder, he was then attacked by the alleged encroacher in front of the officials. The incident took place on Thursday in Nandgram, while the video surfaced on Friday at around 3 pm. See 2 pictures of the assault- Builder bought the plot in 2014 The injured builder, Anil Sharma, a resident of Shashi Garden in Delhi's Mayur Vihar, works as a builder and engineer. Besides buying and selling plots, he also develops and sells residential properties. Anil said that in 2014, he purchased a 200-square-yard (approximately 1,800 sq ft) plot from Krishnapal alias Dhola, a resident of Garhi Guldhar. The plot was purchased for ₹17 lakh, and the sale deed was registered in the name of his wife, Santosh. He alleged that despite approaching officials repeatedly over the past 12 years to obtain possession of the land, no action had been taken. According to him, the plot is now worth around ₹70 lakh. Anil further claimed that whenever he attempted to take possession of the property, Krishnapal and his sons threatened him. Complaint filed with CM on 7 July Anil Sharma said that he submitted a complaint to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in Lucknow on 7 July. According to him, two days before the incident, he received a call from officials of the Ghaziabad ACP (Nandgram) office and the Tehsil administration, asking whether he had visited Lucknow and seeking details of his complaint. After he explained the matter, officials asked him to arrive at the plot with all relevant documents at 10 am on 30 July. When he reached the site, a Lekhpal (revenue officer) from the Tehsil was already present. Anil alleged that Krishnapal was also present at the location and immediately attacked him. 'I was beaten mercilessly,' says builder Describing the assault, Anil Sharma said Krishnapal first abused him while the Lekhpal stood nearby. He alleged that Krishnapal then began assaulting him, throwing him to the ground before repeatedly kicking, punching and slapping him. The attack left him with a serious head injury and two fractured ribs. Anil claimed he ran around 150 metres in an attempt to escape. However, he alleged that Krishnapal, his son and a local gangster from Garhi village caught up with him and assaulted him again. He said Dial 112 police later arrived at the scene and shifted him to the district hospital. DCP City Dhaval Jaiswal said police have launched an investigation based on the complaint. He said strict action will be taken against everyone found involved in the assault.

stories.title: Mayawati says only she will alone finalise BSP tickets:Akash Anand to announce candidates; nominees finalised for over 24 UP Assembly seats
stories.summary: Amid preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, BSP chief Mayawati on Friday issued a clear message, stating that she alone will take the final decision on candidates for all 403 Assembly constituencies in the state. She clarified that Akash Anand's role is limited to announcing candidates approved by her and dismissed speculation on social media regarding his political stature and authority over ticket distribution. Candidates finalised for more than 24 Assembly seats In a six-point statement posted on social media, Mayawati said that meetings with state and divisional-level office-bearers have been held continuously over the past several months at the party's state office in Lucknow. She said the candidate selection process is progressing through these meetings and that candidates have already been finalised for more than 24 Assembly constituencies. Mayawati added that the authority to finalise candidates has always rested with the BSP national president, and this practice will continue. She said the same process is followed not only in Uttar Pradesh but also during Assembly and Lok Sabha elections in other states. Akash Anand will only announce approved candidates The BSP chief said that on constituencies where candidates have already been selected, senior party office-bearers are announcing their names at workers' conferences only after receiving her approval. She added that National Coordinator Akash Anand will also address public meetings in some constituencies and formally announce candidates who have already been approved. Mayawati noted that Akash Anand has previously been entrusted with responsibilities during Assembly elections in various states, Lok Sabha by-elections and organisational programmes. For nearly a year, he has been conducting organisational review meetings and public rallies across the country, and she said he has been carrying out these responsibilities sincerely. Mayawati rejects speculation over Akash Anand's role Mayawati said the entire process is being carried out strictly in accordance with the party's organisational structure and has no connection with enhancing or diminishing Akash Anand's political stature. She accused some people of deliberately spreading misinformation and confusion on social media, saying such claims have "not an iota of truth" in them. She also urged BSP workers to remain vigilant against what she described as mischievous and casteist elements, adding that the party is preparing for the elections in a disciplined manner. Will BSP revive its 2007 social engineering strategy? In 2007, the BSP secured a full majority in Uttar Pradesh through its social engineering strategy that brought together Brahmins, Dalits, Muslims and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). stories.title: Woman revives after 17 hours, shows signs of recovery:Treatment ongoing in ICU; moving her hands and speaking a little
stories.summary: The condition of 65-year-old Sheela Devi, who came back to life about 17 hours after being declared dead, is now reported to be improved. She is undergoing treatment in the ICU of a private hospital in the city. According to her family, Sheela Devi is now moving her hands and also speaking in a low voice. However, doctors have described her condition as still serious and she is under continuous monitoring. According to the family, Sheela Devi's daughter is present outside the ICU, taking health updates from the doctors. Meanwhile, relatives and acquaintances are being informed about her improving health over the phone. Other family members are also continuously arriving at the hospital. Declared dead in Bareilly, regained consciousness upon reaching Agra Sheela Devi, a resident of Srinagar Colony, was suffering from a liver-related illness. About 20 days ago, she had gone to Badaun to stay with her younger son, Sanjeev Mahaur. From there, she was receiving treatment at a private hospital in Bareilly. On Tuesday, her condition became critical, and she was placed on a ventilator. According to family members, doctors at the hospital declared her dead around 3 AM on Wednesday. After that, her body was brought to her home in Agra by ambulance in the evening, where preparations for the last rites had begun, and relatives started gathering for the final viewing. Stir during the last rites The family says that around 8 PM, when the son-in-law touched her feet during the final respects, Sheila Devi's body felt a stir. After this, she held her son-in-law's hand and said, I am alive, where are you taking me? Hearing this, the family members were astonished. After the incident, family members immediately took her to Park Hospital in Agra, where doctors began her treatment. Currently, her treatment is ongoing in the ICU. The incident became a topic of discussion throughout the city. This incident of coming back to life after being declared dead has become a topic of discussion in Agra and surrounding areas. Meanwhile, family members are hoping for Sheila Devi's speedy recovery, while doctors are continuously monitoring her condition.

stories.title: UP police constable exam results declared:76,184 qualify for 32,679 posts; general cut-off 7 marks higher than OBC
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board (UPPRPB) on Friday declared the results of the Police Constable Recruitment Examination. The Board also announced the normalised cut-off marks for male and female candidates across all categories. In the Unreserved (General) category, the cut-off stands at 258.03 for male candidates and 255.84 for female candidates. Category-wise normalised cut-offs For the OBC category, the cut-off is 251.63 for male candidates and 249.27 for female candidates. For the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) category, the cut-off is 247.93 for male candidates and 247.35 for female candidates. In the Scheduled Caste (SC) category, the cut-off is 239.34 for male candidates and 236.31 for female candidates. For the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category, the cut-off is 220.10 for male candidates and 211.47 for female candidates. Document verification to begin from 17 August The Board said that the next stage of the recruitment process will comprise Document Verification (DV) and the Physical Standard Test (PST), which will commence from 17 August 2026. A detailed notification specifying the venue, date and time for document verification will be published shortly on the Board's official website for shortlisted candidates. The Physical Efficiency Test (PET) is expected to be conducted in September 2026. This news is being updated….

stories.title: Sant community upset over MP Pappu Yadav's protest:Jitendranand Saraswati demands expulsion for insulting sadhus
stories.summary: On Friday, the 10th day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, the opposition staged a unique and symbolic protest in the Parliament complex over the issue of alleged irregularities in the offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. In this protest, independent MP Pappu Yadav from Purnia arrived at Parliament dressed as a sadhu. Now, the saint community has reacted strongly to his protest. Jitendranand Saraswati, General Secretary of the All India Sant Samiti, has called it an insult to sadhus, saints, and saffron robes, and has demanded action from the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Saint community expresses strong objection Jitendranand Saraswati, General Secretary of the All India Sant Samiti, strongly criticized this protest. He said that any political party has the right to oppose the government or the BJP, but it is inappropriate to use the attire of saints and sages to convey a message that allegedly accuses the entire saint community of theft. He alleged that such a protest harms the dignity of the saint tradition and saffron attire. He said that if an unconditional public apology is not sought in this matter, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha should take cognizance of this entire incident and take appropriate action. He also said that the concerned agencies are investigating the alleged offerings case related to the Ram Temple, and the saint community will accept whatever legal decision is made. He also reiterated the demand for strict action against the culprits. Pappu Yadav Reached Parliament Dressed as a Sadhu A symbolic protest was staged in the Parliament premises by opposition parties to raise the issue of alleged irregularities in the offerings of the Ram Temple. During this, Pappu Yadav applied sandalwood paste on his forehead, wore saffron clothes, and, holding a donation box in his hand, sat down on the ground near the Makar Gate of the Parliament. During the protest, Samajwadi Party MPs Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav, and Awadhesh Prasad were seen symbolically putting offerings into the donation box. As part of the protest, Pappu Yadav was seen putting those monies into his pocket. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi also symbolically put rupees into the donation box. After this, Pappu Yadav began to act as if he was running away with the donation box, while other MPs symbolically acted to stop and catch him. During this, the MPs also humorously acted out 'beating' him. After the protest, Pappu Yadav said, I thought I would run away with the money, but the SP MPs caught me. Now they are saying they will hang me. Opposition attacks the government The opposition says that its protest was regarding alleged irregularities in Ram Mandir offerings, lathi-charge on students, and issues like the absence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Parliament. Following this, opposition MPs, led by Congress General Secretary and MP Priyanka Gandhi, protested in the Parliament complex. They held posters that read, "Why is Amit Shah missing from Parliament?" The opposition alleged that the government is avoiding answering important issues, while the ruling party called the opposition's protest a political gimmick.

stories.title: FIR against woman who made remarks against PM:CJP opposes action; calls it 'misuse of the criminal justice system'
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Friday opposed the FIR registered against Ruchika Singh for allegedly making objectionable remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a students' protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Addressing the issue, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the registration of a criminal case against the woman amounted to a misuse of the criminal justice system. He argued that if the complainant believed her reputation or that of the Prime Minister had been harmed, the matter should have been pursued through a defamation case rather than criminal prosecution. Das also questioned the legal basis of the FIR, saying, "People use abusive language every day in this country. How has that become a criminal offence?" He maintained that criminal law should not be invoked over such remarks. Case stems from July 23 Jantar Mantar protest The FIR relates to a protest held at Jantar Mantar on July 23. During the demonstration by students, a video surfaced on social media in which Ruchika Singh was allegedly seen using abusive language against Prime Minister Modi. The video later went viral, following which Smriti Singh, a resident of Ghaziabad, filed a complaint at the Noida Expressway Police Station. Based on the complaint, police registered a case against Ruchika Singh under charges of intentional insult, public nuisance and defamation. Zero FIR transferred to Delhi Police According to the police, a Zero FIR was registered at the Noida Expressway Police Station and later transferred to the Sansad Marg Police Station in New Delhi, which has jurisdiction over the area where the alleged incident took place. Police said the matter is now being investigated by the Delhi Police. Complainant says viral videos damage country's image In her complaint, Smriti Singh alleged that several videos of the woman had gone viral on social media in which she was allegedly using abusive language against Prime Minister Modi and his mother. She claimed that such remarks tarnish the country's image and sought legal action against the accused. What is a Zero FIR? A Zero FIR is a First Information Report that can be registered at any police station, irrespective of whether the alleged offence occurred within its territorial jurisdiction. After registration, the FIR is transferred to the police station that has jurisdiction over the place where the incident took place. The receiving police station then conducts the investigation and takes further legal action. Legal provisions invoked in the Noida FIR The Zero FIR registered in Noida invokes provisions related to intentional insult, public mischief and defamation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). However, legal experts note that each of these offences has a specific legal threshold that must be met before criminal liability can arise. Under Section 352 of the BNS, which deals with intentional insult, the prosecution must establish that the accused either intended or knew it was likely that the insult would provoke a breach of public peace. Mere use of offensive or abusive language, without any resulting or intended disturbance of public order, may not satisfy this requirement. Similarly, Section 253, which deals with public mischief, is primarily intended to address acts that incite serious public disorder. The provision covers conduct that could encourage mutiny within the armed forces, create fear likely to induce offences against the State, or promote enmity between different communities. Legal experts argue that this sets a significantly higher threshold than criticism or abusive remarks directed at a political leader. The offence of defamation under the BNS also contains long-recognised exceptions, including protections for comments made in good faith on the conduct of a public servant or public figure in the discharge of their official duties.

stories.title: Mother clutches daughter's school bag in tears:Waits for 70 hours, saying, 'She will surely return'; girl swept away in Bulandshahr drain
stories.summary: The school bag that 11-year-old Charu carried every day is now held tightly by her grieving mother, who sits at the doorstep hoping her daughter will return. More than 70 hours after Charu was swept away in a rainwater-filled drain in Bulandshahr, there is still no sign of her. Charu Kashyap, a Class 4 student from the Satha area, was returning home from school at around 12:30 pm on July 28 when she fell into an open drain overflowing with rainwater and was carried away by the strong current. CCTV footage has surfaced showing her walking near the drain shortly before the incident. Rescue teams have been searching a one-kilometre stretch from the drain to the Kali River, but the child has not been found. Following the incident, four Bulandshahr Municipal Corporation officials have been suspended, and a case has also been registered against the school management. See pictures Charu's mother sits all day in a distraught state, holding her daughter's bag. She waits for her daughter to call out to her. Know the full story... In Saatha locality, Rinku Kashyap lives with his wife Gyanwati and two children. Rinku, who runs a bakery shop, has an elder son Gagan, who is 19 years old and studying BBA. Charu was a fourth-grade student. As usual, Charu was returning home on Tuesday around 12:30 PM after school. While returning home, heavy rain started. Due to continuous rain for several days, the city's drains were already overflowing. Due to the heavy rain on Tuesday, rainwater was flowing with a strong current into the open drain in Dharmpal Wali Gali of Saatha area. According to eyewitnesses, as soon as Charu reached near the drain, her foot slipped. Losing her balance, she fell into the open drain. Before people nearby could try to save her, she was swept away by the strong current and disappeared from sight within seconds. Search Operation Continues from Drain to Kali River People informed the police about the accident. Police, municipality officials, and local residents who arrived at the scene began the search. Even after extensive searching, when the girl could not be found, the scope of the operation was expanded to include NDRF, SDRF, Flood PAC, Fire Service, municipal employees, and local divers. The search operation has been continuously ongoing for the past three days with over 100 personnel. The administration suspects that the strong current might have carried the girl to the Kali River. Therefore, a search operation is being conducted with the help of Poclain machines to remove bushes and water hyacinths accumulated in the river. ADM Administration, SP City, and CO City, along with several other officers, are monitoring the operation at the spot. Four Officers Suspended for Negligence After the girl was swept away in the drain, DM Kumar Harsh suspended the negligent officers of Bulandshahr Municipal Council. The suspended Junior Engineer (Civil) Amit Kumar, Junior Engineer (Civil) Kapil Mohan, Sanitation and Food Inspector Varsha Rani, and Sanitation and Food Inspector Rajendra Singh have been attached to the Directorate. Mother sits with her daughter's bag in hand, saying - "She will come..." Meanwhile, Charu's family is waiting with hope for their daughter. The mother's eyes are fixed on the door. Charu's school bag got stuck in the drain when she fell. The mother cries and weeps, clutching that bag to her chest. In a conversation with the Bhaskar team, she said, "My daughter will definitely come. My house has become empty without her. It's been three days since I saw her face. I feel like she will come from somewhere any moment now. I can't sleep all night." Charu's school dress, books, and toys are kept just as they were at home. Every member of the family gazes at them and breaks down crying remembering Charu. The mother repeatedly cries seeing her daughter's picture, while the father, Rinku Kashyap, remains engaged with rescue teams from morning till late night, searching for his daughter. Father said - "The culprits should be punished" Father Rinku Kashyap said that if there had been robust safety arrangements instead of an open drain, perhaps his daughter would have been with him today. Demanding strict action against the responsible officers and employees from the Chief Minister, he said- Whether my daughter is found or not, those who were negligent must be punished. Suspension alone will not suffice. There should be a system in place so that no other family has to endure this pain. Mother said - "Why hasn't my daughter been found even after three days?" Charu's mother also questioned the negligence of the school and the municipality. She said that the accident happened due to the open drain and those responsible should be punished. She said, My daughter is not so small that she cannot be found even after three days. What exactly happened? The stove at home has not been lit for many days According to neighbours, the atmosphere at Charu's house has completely changed since the accident. The stove in the house has not even been lit. The mother has not eaten properly for many days and keeps looking towards the door every now and then. From morning till night, the father remains engaged in searching for his daughter, sometimes along the drain and sometimes up to the Kali River. Whenever the rescue team returns, the family's hope rekindles, but each time they are met with disappointment. The people of the neighbourhood are also standing with the family and praying for Charu's safe return. Public representatives met the family After the accident, public representatives also started reaching the family's home. District Panchayat President and local BJP leader Pradeep Chaudhary met the family members and consoled them. He said that all agencies of the administration are engaged in the search for the girl and the rescue operation will continue until she is found. He also assured strict action against the culprits and all possible help to the victim's family.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar sounds poll bugle, appoints 45 Assembly in-charges:18 Dalits and 10 Muslims included; no Brahmin or Thakur leaders nominees
stories.summary: Azad Samaj Party chief and MP Chandrashekhar Azad has kicked off preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. On Friday, he released the first list of 45 Assembly in-charges. The list includes former IPS officer Aditya Prakash Verma from Hathras and former minister Mahendra Singh from Chharra, among other prominent leaders. Of the 45 appointees, 18 are Dalits, 10 Muslims, 16 OBCs, and one is from the Sikh community. No leader from the Brahmin or Thakur communities has been included in the list. Politically, the move is being seen as significant because the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has also begun announcing candidates through Assembly in-charges. Both parties now appear set to directly challenge each other while competing for the Dalit vote bank and the broader Bahujan political space. See the list--- Maximum focus on Western UP The first list has the highest number of seats from Western UP. Special emphasis has been placed on strengthening the organization in districts like Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Shamli, Hapur, Agra, Aligarh, Mathura, Bareilly, Badaun and Shahjahanpur. It is believed that the party is working on a strategy to increase its political hold in areas with Dalit-Muslim equations. In the list of 45 in-charges, the party has also taken care of social balance. The highest number, 18 Dalit faces, have been given responsibility. Apart from this, 16 people from OBC communities including Yadav, Gurjar, Prajapati, Valmiki, Maurya and several other communities have been given representation. By giving opportunity to the Muslim community on 10 seats, Chandrashekhar has tried to balance the equation of Western UP and Purvanchal. Former MLAs and prominent faces included in the list The list includes several leaders who have previously contested elections from various parties or hold influence in their regions. These include Deepak Chaudhary from Govardhan, Jagdish Baghel from Fatehpur Sikri, Tulsiram Valmiki from Govind Nagar, and Shivsagar Yadav from the Madhuban seat in Mau. Party says - Appointments made on recommendations of state committee The party claims that these in-charges have been appointed based on recommendations from the state committee. All in-charges have been entrusted with the responsibility of strengthening the organization up to the booth level, along with taking issues of social justice, constitution, and Bahujan Samaj to the public.

Governor and Chancellor Anandiben Patel inaugurated the e-Office system during the university's 69th convocation ceremony. The event is being held at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Convention Centre of KGMU. The Chancellor awarded digital degrees to 125,239 students. Vice-Chancellor JP Saini said students from 44 countries are currently studying at the university. The university has 93,536 undergraduate students, 31,006 postgraduate students, 419 diploma students and 30 online education students. In addition, 248 researchers were awarded PhD degrees. A total of 204 medals were presented to 111 meritorious students, including 80 women and 31 men. The convocation is being presided over by Governor and Chancellor Anandiben Patel. NITI Aayog member Prof Abhay Karandikar is the chief guest. Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay was invited but could not attend the event. Minister of State for Higher Education Rajni Tiwari is among the dignitaries attending the ceremony.

stories.title: MPs stage unique protest over Ram Mandir offerings row:Rahul Gandhi puts money in donation box; Pappu Yadav pretends to flee with it, SP MPs stop him
stories.summary: On the 10th day of Parliament's Monsoon Session on Friday, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress staged a unique protest in the Parliament complex over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. Independent MP Pappu Yadav, who represents Purnia in Bihar, arrived dressed as a Hindu ascetic. Wearing a sandalwood tilak on his forehead and carrying a donation box, he sat on the ground. As SP MPs Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad tried to place offerings in the donation box, Pappu Yadav jokingly snatched the money and put it in his pocket. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi also dropped money into the box. A short while later, Pappu Yadav pretended to run away with the donation box, but SP MPs caught him and took it back. In a light-hearted remark, Pappu Yadav said, "I thought I'd run away with the money, but the SP MPs caught me. Now they're saying they'll hang me." The opposition has been targeting the government over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir, the alleged lathi-charge on students, and Union Home Minister Amit Shah's absence from the House. stories.title: Kanwariya pulls 8-quintal car-shaped Kanwar with his teeth:Carries parents in palanquin; AI surveillance introduced on Kanwar route
stories.summary: Crowds of Kanwariyas are now visible on roads across Uttar Pradesh. Some devotees are heading to Haridwar to collect holy Ganga water, while others are returning after completing the pilgrimage. In Aligarh, Narendra Jat is pulling an 800kg car-shaped Kanwar with his teeth on his way to Haridwar. A statue of Lord Shiva has been installed on its roof. He said he began the journey with the resolve that the cow should be granted the status of the nation's mother, and believes Lord Shiva will fulfil his wish. In Bulandshahr, Jitendra is carrying his parents in a palanquin while returning from Haridwar with holy Ganga water. He will offer the water at the Shiv temple in Sikandrabad. Prashant Rana, from Hapur, is bringing back holy Ganga water with his grandmother, Sharda Devi, seated in a Kanwar. He is accompanied by 22 fellow Kanwariyas, and all of them will offer the holy water at a Shiv temple in Hapur. In Ghaziabad on Thursday evening, Kanwariyas created a ruckus after a Kanwar was damaged. They accused a Muslim youth of touching the Kanwar and thrashed him. He was slapped and punched repeatedly in the middle of the road before police intervened and managed to calm the crowd. Meanwhile, police remain on high alert for the Kanwar Yatra. Round-the-clock monitoring is being carried out on roads as well as across social media platforms. The Kanwar route is being monitored through CCTV cameras and AI-based surveillance.

stories.title: Woman gives birth 3 hours after her daughter's last rites:10-year-old raped, murdered by constable at crematorium; girl used to say, 'I will tie rakhi to my brother'
stories.summary: A constable raped and killed a 10-year-old girl at a cremation ground in Gorakhpur. Her last rites were performed on Thursday at 6 PM. Three hours later, her mother gave birth to a son. When the mother and sisters saw the baby's face, they burst into tears. They said that the girl had wished to tie a rakhi to her brother on this Raksha Bandhan, but before that could happen, the monster snatched her away. Meanwhile, police investigation revealed that after the rape, constable Abhishek Yadav (35) tied the girl's hands behind her back and threw her alive into the river. Her head hit a stone. She died from drowning and suffocation. The post-mortem revealed that the girl was subjected to brutality. Five bones in her body were found broken, including those in her feet and neck. Her stomach was ruptured. Deep wound marks were found on her private parts. The constable's wife told Dainik Bhaskar - What he has done is unforgivable. He has made me hang my head in shame. Where will I show my face now? We also have a daughter. I will never live with him again. On the night of 28th July, a constable kidnapped a girl from the district hospital. After examining 200 CCTV cameras, the police arrested the accused on 29th July. On Thursday, based on his identification, the police recovered the body after 36 hours. The family has demanded financial assistance of ₹50 lakhs, a job for one member, and the death penalty for the accused. SSP Dr. Kaustubh informed that the accused constable has been dismissed. An FIR has been registered against him under the POCSO Act and other sections. RASUKA (NSA) will also be imposed on him. Read the entire case from the girl's kidnapping to the last rites in 4 points... 1- Went to hospital to give food to his sister, kidnapped from there The girl's father is originally from Azamgarh. He has been living on rent in Gorakhpur with his wife and 5 daughters for 4 years. He runs the household by driving an e-rickshaw. On July 27, his 13-year-old daughter suddenly fell ill. The family admitted her to the district hospital. On July 28, the girl went to the hospital with food for her elder sister. During this time, the constable had also come to the hospital to get medicine. Seeing the girl alone, he started following her. When the girl left the hospital at 10 PM, he coaxed her and made her sit on his bike. He took her to a cremation ground 15 km away from the hospital. There he committed brutality with the girl. He beat her mercilessly. Then threw her in the river. The accused reached the police lines. There were blood stains on his uniform. He washed the uniform and then went to sleep. 2- 200 CCTVs searched, seen taking the girl away on a bike Meanwhile, when the girl did not reach home, the family started searching. The family members searched on their own for 2 hours. Late at night, the police were also informed, but the swift action that should have been taken in the initial hours was not visible. From Wednesday afternoon, police and teams from 10 police stations got engaged in the search operation. During this time, 200 CCTV cameras in the surrounding areas were examined. In the cameras, a constable on a bike was seen taking the innocent child from the district hospital. As soon as the registration number was obtained, the police reached the accused. After getting the bike's registration number from CCTV, the accused was identified on Wednesday afternoon. The police took him into custody. He kept misleading the police for 4 hours. When interrogated strictly, he confessed to the crime. On Thursday at 8:30 AM, the police recovered the girl's body based on the accused constable's identification. 3- Doctors and nurses at the district hospital chased and beat him On Thursday afternoon, the police brought the constable to the district hospital for medical examination. Doctors, nurses, and people present there surrounded the constable. They chased him and beat him severely with kicks and punches. Somehow, the police team calmed them down by explaining. Somehow, by calling heavy force, the constable was taken out in police custody. All work at the district hospital remained suspended for two hours. 4- Sister fainted after seeing the body, father performed last rites On Thursday at 5 PM, after the postmortem, the police did not take the girl's body home but took it directly by ambulance to Rajghat. On receiving this information, her four sisters rushed there. Upon seeing the body, the younger sister fainted. The father performed the last rites for his daughter. Sister used to say - This Raksha Bandhan, I will also have a brother The elder sister said that my younger sister used to tell mother that this Raksha Bandhan, I will also have a brother. I will fulfill my dream by tying him a rakhi. Today, if she were here, she would have been the happiest. She always used to ask her mother for a brother. She always used to say that she would study hard, become a doctor, and treat her mother herself. When the constable's wife learned about the incident, she held her head in despair The constable's wife lives in Molnapur village in Ghazipur with her daughter and son. When the wife received information about this incident, she held her head in shock. The wife said that due to his habits, she left her in-laws' house and lives with her children at her maternal home. Was a 2018 batch constable, had been jailed before for molestation The accused constable Abhishek Yadav is originally a resident of Hansrajpur Chaura village in the Shadiyabad police station area of Ghazipur. Abhishek is a 2018 batch constable. Currently, he is posted in Dial-112. He was appointed in 2016 on a merit basis. His first posting was in Gorakhpur. He had been posted there since then. In January 2025, he had molested a woman from Bengal. He was suspended then as well. He was also sent to jail.

stories.title: Clouds cover Gorakhpur skies:Winds blow at 45 kmph; August to begin with rain
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the sky has been cloudy since Friday morning. Cold winds blowing at a speed of 40 to 45 km/h have provided great relief to people from humidity and heat. Light sunshine is also appearing intermittently between the clouds, while light rain or drizzle is expected in some parts of the city by evening. According to the Meteorological Department, the maximum temperature of the district on Friday is estimated to be around 32 degrees Celsius and the minimum temperature 27 degrees Celsius. Clouds will continue to move throughout the day, so a significant increase in temperature is not expected. However, in areas where there is no rain and the sun comes out, humidity may be felt for some time due to moisture. Rainfall to increase with the beginning of August Meteorologists say that with the beginning of August, monsoon activities will intensify. For the next few days, clouds will remain over Gorakhpur and its surrounding areas. Light drizzle can be seen in some places, while moderate rain can be seen in others. The scope of rainfall is also likely to gradually increase. Saturday will be cloudy, with scattered drizzles On August 1, i.e., Saturday, the weather is likely to remain almost the same. The sky will be cloudy and light rain or showers may occur in some parts of the district. However, the rain will be intermittent, and the sun may also appear in between. In such a situation, humidity can be troublesome in areas where there is no rain. Rain likely in most parts of the district on Monday From August 2, Sunday, there are signs of an increase in rain activities. According to the Meteorological Department, light to moderate rain may occur in many parts of the district. With increasing rain, the daytime temperature will drop, and people will get more relief from the heat. The monsoon is likely to become more active on Monday, August 3. According to the district-level forecast by the Meteorological Department, most parts of the district may experience rain. Light to moderate rain may be recorded in some areas. The extent of rainfall is expected to continuously increase during the first three days of August. Monsoon effect to continue next week as well The Meteorological Department estimates that monsoon activities will continue in Eastern Uttar Pradesh next week as well. Its effect will also be seen in Gorakhpur. The cycle of dense clouds, rain, and occasional sunshine will continue. Due to rain, the temperature will remain controlled, and the possibility of severe heat is low. Relief from heat, but humidity will not completely disappear People will definitely get relief from the heat due to rain and cold winds, but due to high humidity in the atmosphere, the stickiness will not completely disappear. After the rain stops and the sun comes out, a sticky heat may be felt. However, due to strong winds and intermittent rain, the weather will remain pleasant most of the time. Overall, July is bidding farewell in Gorakhpur with clouds, cold winds, and pleasant weather, while August is expected to begin with an increasing spell of rain. Rain activities will intensify from Saturday, and the impact of the monsoon will be clearly visible in a large part of the district from Sunday to Monday.

stories.title: Youth beaten after allegedly brushing against Kanwar:Slapped and punched; Kanwariya says, 'All my effort has gone to waste'
stories.summary: A dispute broke out in Ghaziabad after a Kanwar carried by Kanwariyas was damaged during the yatra. The Kanwariyas accused a Muslim youth of touching the Kanwar and allegedly assaulted him in the middle of the road with slaps and punches. One of the Kanwariyas said he had followed all the religious rituals throughout the journey, but his efforts went in vain after the Kanwar broke. After being informed, police reached the spot and brought the situation under control. According to religious customs, the Kanwar was worshipped again with proper rituals. The incident took place in the Madhuban Bapudham police station area at around 4 pm on Thursday. See 2 pictures Now, the incident in detail Held hostage for 20 minutes Sonu Kumar, a resident of Bharatpur, Rajasthan, was returning to his village with Ganga water from Haridwar along with 15 fellow Kanwariyas from his village. During this, his Kanwar was touched by a young man. When Sonu asked, the young man told his name as Imran. The Kanwariyas alleged that this broke their Kanwar, after which a quarrel started. The Kanwariyas severely beat Imran. They held him hostage for about 20 minutes. Seeing the commotion, people from nearby areas gathered. This caused a traffic jam for one kilometer on both sides of the road. Some people tried to intervene, but the Kanwariyas did not listen. Kanwariya said - I have to offer water at the Shiva temple Kanwariya Sonu said- I started my Kanwar journey from Haridwar at 5 AM on July 21st. I rested only 3 times on the way. I must reach my village by August 10th and perform Jalabhishek at the village's Shiva temple on August 11th. I was undertaking the entire journey according to the rules. But, my Kanwar got damaged on the way, rendering all my hard work useless. The police somehow pacified the Kanwariyas. The Kanwar was worshipped again with proper rituals. After this, the Kanwariyas resumed their journey. Due to the commotion, traffic near Guladhar station was affected for about 20 minutes. The police cleared the crowd and normalised traffic. Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) Rajkaran Naiyar said- After the incident, station in-charges have been instructed to exercise special vigilance during the Kanwar Yatra. Warnings have been issued to stop the movement of heavy vehicles on the Kanwar route from Meerut border to Delhi border, and to strictly implement the diversion system.

stories.title: Rivers swell in UP, rain alert issued for 24 cities:9 swept away after boat capsizes in Sharda; Ganga flows over highway in Bijnor
stories.summary: The monsoon has weakened again in Uttar Pradesh, but heavy rainfall in the hills has caused 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Ghaghara (Saryu), to swell. In Lakhimpur Kheri, a boat capsized in the Sharda River on Thursday evening. 9 people were swept away. 7 were rescued, while a search is underway for the remaining two. In Bijnor, the Ganga is flowing over the Bahsuma–Thakurdwara State Highway, with vehicles seen passing through the floodwater. Nearby fields are also inundated. The administration is monitoring the situation. Since Friday morning, skies have remained overcast in more than 35 cities, including Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Kanpur and Barabanki, with cool winds prevailing. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 24 cities, while Lalitpur, Mirzapur and Sonbhadra are under a heavy rainfall alert. Residents have been advised to step out only if necessary. According to the IMD, the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal has moved towards Odisha and Chhattisgarh, weakening monsoon activity over Uttar Pradesh. Satellite images show that monsoon clouds have disappeared from nearly 90% of the state. Earlier on Thursday, rain was recorded in 29 cities, including Varanasi, Meerut and Bijnor. In Bijnor, roads were waterlogged and floodwater entered the offices of the Basic Education Officer and the Housing Development Department. In Meerut, an electricity tower along the Ganga riverbank was washed away. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon system over central India is expected to weaken soon. After that, the monsoon trough will rapidly shift towards Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal will strengthen again. As a result, the monsoon is likely to regain momentum from 3–4 August, bringing another spell of heavy rainfall.

stories.title: 'I will have relations with your wife':Sting operation exposes UP Maulanas; defend triple talaq; perform halala themselves
stories.summary: “Your divorced wife will marry me first, then halala will take place. It is my decision whether I keep her for one night or longer. You cannot ask me to divorce her.” These are the words of Maulana Rehmatullah from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, who was secretly recorded allegedly promoting halala. Although the triple talaq law has been in force for seven years, a sting operation claims that some maulanas in Uttar Pradesh are still exploiting Muslim women under the cover of religious practices. Under the traditional practice, if a husband divorces his wife by pronouncing talaq three times, they cannot remarry unless the woman first marries another man. The second husband must consummate the marriage and later divorce her of his own free will. Only then can she legally remarry her first husband. This process is known as halala. According to the sting operation, some couples avoid involving relatives in this process. Instead, certain maulanas allegedly offer to perform halala themselves. They are accused of staying with divorced women in hotels and charging money for accommodation and other expenses. During the investigation, Dainik Bhaskar's team approached two maulanas, who allegedly agreed to carry out halala themselves in the name of religion. In Gorakhpur, we contacted Maulana Rahmatullah. The Maulana runs a tailor shop. We told Rahmatullah - we have had a triple talaq. Iddat, meaning 3 months, is about to be completed. Now we want to live together again. What is the way? Halala is necessary and just as husband and wife live, it is necessary to live that way Rahmatullah : The Quran is considered divine. Halala is in it. The woman should stay away from her husband for 3 menses (menstrual periods). Then she should marry a person who is responsible. It should never be kept in mind that he (the new husband) should divorce her; this will not be according to the Quran. This is the will of the new husband. It is necessary to live in the same way that a husband and wife live together. Reporter : Then with whom should Halala be performed? Rahmatullah: If it's a brother or a close relative, they get halala done with him. This happens because he gives a divorce, but sometimes the man (who performed halala) doesn't divorce her at all. There was a 70-year-old man in Meerut. He divorced his wife. There was an acquaintance with whom he arranged a nikah (marriage) under halala. Later, he changed his mind. He said, "Where is your wife? Now she is my wife." The woman also said that she would stay there. The woman was 40-45 years old. Reporter: We don't want to get halala done with anyone from the family. Rahmatullah: Okay, your wife will be married to me. After that, halala. Now it's my will whether I keep your wife for one night or for how long. Whatever expenses are incurred in this, you will have to pay. Reporter: What will be the expense? Rahmatullah: Oh brother, whatever the Maulana's expense will be. You will have to pay for everything. We will inform the gentleman (pointing towards our source). Not much, consider it within 20 to 25 thousand. Reporter: Will I have to bring my wife here? Rahmatullah: Bring her after Muharram, then the marriage will happen. Then I will explain some things to your wife. For example, when you were husband and wife before, you didn't tell anyone each other's secrets. Similarly, you shouldn't tell anyone what I say. Reporter: Will it be physical too? Rahmatullah: This thought should not be in your mind. Tell me, when a Nikah happens, suppose your wife gets her periods on the first night, then you won't do it, then you'll do it on the second night. You will do it after 4 days, won't you? A relationship has to be built. I was just watching on YouTube. A Maulana says that the husband-wife relationship has to be maintained. You have to forget that she is my wife. Reporter: Meaning we have separated, now she has been married anew. Rahmatullah: We get ready for Nikah because of me, the relationship becomes better. Our family is of Pirs (spiritual guides). My maternal grandparents' home is in Maharajganj. There is Khutha Bazaar there. The Pir Sahib there is our biological great-grandfather. That's why we perform prayers and make amulets. Reporter: What time should I come in the morning? Rahmatullah: Come by 11-12 AM. Then leave your wife with me for 4-5 hours. What happens is that to build a relationship, we need to talk a little. I will have to explain things to her. It's not like coming and pouncing like a dog. We can book a hotel. From here, we left saying that we would bring the wife after a few days. Now we were looking for a Maulana whose stature among Muslims was even greater. Our search ended with Mufti Meraj Ahmed Qadri. The source told us that Meraj Ahmed is a Mufti in the Madina Mosque of Gorakhpur. Hundreds of people offer prayers behind him daily. We approached him and discussed Halala. 'It is in the Hadith that physical relations must be established at least once' Meraj Ahmed: In the case of divorce, Halala is the only way. It would have been better if you had not given 3 divorces. If you had given 1 or 2 divorces, you could have called her back and remarried. Since you have given three divorces, she is out of your hands. Now, if you want to have loving conversations with her, it is not permissible. Reporter: What is the way out of this? Meraj Ahmed: The way is that if you want to live with your wife and children, Islam states that the wife should have a second marriage (Nikah). If there's someone from your family, marry her to him, or marry her to someone I tell you about. She just has to spend 1 or 2 nights with him. They just have to consummate the marriage, even if it's just once. That too, because you have given a divorce. If she has completed her Iddat (waiting period), then when the second marriage (Nikah) happens, she will again enter Iddat (after the second divorce). After that, she will be 'fresh' (eligible). Then you can marry her. The only way for this is Halala. There is no other permissible way. If you go to court, they will just finalize the divorce. Iddat means a waiting period. After divorce, one has to wait for about three months. Before that, a remarriage cannot happen. Reporter: Do they have to have the same kind of relations as a husband and wife? Meraj Ahmed: Look, you will have to spend one night with him. What he does, only he knows. But, in Hadith, it is stated that a relationship (physical intimacy) must be established once. You are doing this for Allah's principle. Reporter: In our view, there is no one who is loyal, who would do something at our behest. We don't want to do it at home. Meraj Ahmed: There is a way. If you don't find anyone, let us know. We will talk to such a person who is responsible. But, the condition is that after the Nikah, you will have to take a room in a hotel for 2-3 days. It's possible that the work might be done in one day. It's possible it might take more days. After that, the Mahr (dower) money will also have to be given. And some 'Nazre Inayat' (favors/gifts), whatever they wish, that will have to be given. Whatever expenses arise, you will have to bear them. After one or two nights, they will give divorce. After 4 months pass, then you can perform Nikah (marry again). Reporter: What will be the cost involved in this? Meraj Ahmed: Look, the Mahr (dower) will not be less than 11 thousand. We'll check the rate of Dirham (silver coin). Assume it will be between 11 thousand to 15 thousand. After that, arrangements for food and drink will have to be made. A gift (nazrana) of 10 to 15 thousand will have to be given. If you don't give it, it's possible that it might come to his mind and he won't leave your wife.

stories.title: BJP survey predicts loss of 52–67 seats in UP:Recommends dropping 35% of MLAs to counter anti-incumbency
stories.summary: Before the UP Assembly elections, the BJP has received a major setback from an internal survey conducted by the party. The report indicates that if elections were held in the current situation, the BJP might have to struggle for a majority. There could be a direct loss of 52 to 67 seats for BJP. The BJP is getting 190 to 205 seats. 202 seats are needed for a majority. In 2022, the BJP received 255 seats. In by-elections, 2 more seats were added to the BJP's account. Currently, the BJP has a total of 257 MLAs. The survey agency has also given suggestions to avoid this loss. For this, the party will have to deny tickets to 35% of its current MLAs. There is maximum discontent regarding MLAs in the Purvanchal region. BJP conducted a survey through the Nation With Namo agency before the assembly elections. This is a registered organization. It conducts political surveys for BJP. I n this, experts and researchers included in the team reached all assembly constituencies from March to the second week of July and took predetermined samples. Some questions were asked to people- 2 types of discontent were seen in the survey In the survey report, people's discontent has been divided into 2 types. The first category includes discontent with the government, i.e., central and state government policies. The second category includes anger towards MLAs. During the survey, the policies and incidents related to the government on which the public expressed dissatisfaction are as follows- Displeasure with MLAs emerged due to these reasons- Team gave 2 types of suggestions in the survey report Suggestion 1- Tickets of 30 to 35% MLAs should be cut The survey revealed resentment against 30% to 35% of BJP MLAs. People clearly told the team that came to conduct the survey that if old faces are given another chance in the Assembly elections like the Lok Sabha, we will look for other options. The survey suggests that to reverse these results, the BJP will have to deny tickets to 30 to 35% of its current 257 MLAs. This will reduce people's anger towards the ruling party's MLAs. The BJP can cross the majority mark. Currently, the party is strong on 190 to 205 seats. However, based on the right selection of candidates, balancing caste equations, and issues that emerge just before the elections, there could be a fluctuation of 10% in this estimate. Faces were changed in 2022 as well Before the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP had commissioned surveys from 2 agencies. Based on that report, the BJP had denied tickets to more than 120 MLAs. New candidates were fielded on 165 out of 403 seats. Despite this, the BJP's seats decreased from 312 in 2017 to 255. This resulted in a loss of 57 seats for the BJP. Suggestion 2- Advantage in fighting elections on issues like nationalism The survey team believes that if the election remains focused on issues like religion, nationalism, and law and order, the BJP will benefit. However, if the SP succeeds in making caste equations and PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) politics a major issue, like in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP could suffer losses. Resentment against Yadavs has decreased among the new generation A member of the survey team stated that Yadavs have been considered traditional voters of the SP. During SP rule, Yadavs' matters were often heard quickly in many cases. This led to resentment against them among non-Yadav people. However, this resentment has decreased over the past 5 years. Especially Gen-Z (the new generation) does not consider the Yadav versus non-Yadav concept to be correct. Yogi's team is also conducting a separate survey The BJP organization's survey has been completed. However, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is conducting a separate election survey. A private agency is going village to village collecting feedback from people about the government, MLAs, and the Chief Minister's image. This situation has arisen after the disqualification of MLAs, by-elections, and deaths following the 2022 elections

stories.title: 'Today is a dark day in history':Allahabad HC judge says attempt was made to influence him; rescuses himself from ₹900 cr codeine case
stories.summary: 'An attempt was made to reach the judge for bail. Such attempts are a direct attack on the independence and impartiality of the judiciary. These cannot be accepted under any circumstances. This is a black day in the history of the judiciary.' This comment was made by Allahabad High Court Judge Krishna Pahal on Thursday in the codeine cough syrup case. He sent 80 petitions, including the bail application of accused Bhola Prasad, to the Chief Justice and recused himself from all cases. Judge Krishna Pahal said at the start of the hearing - After the judgment was reserved, the accused attempted to reach the presiding judge personally. Calling it an assault on judicial dignity, he said such tendencies cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. Bhola Prasad is the father of Shubham Jaiswal, the kingpin of the codeine cough syrup gang. Shubham is absconding. He has already been declared a fugitive. The next hearing will now be on 7th August. Judge said- If ignored, trust will be shaken Actually, about 80 accused in the codeine cough syrup case have filed bail petitions in the High Court. For their hearing together, the court had fixed Thursday, July 30 at 10 AM. Along with the lawyers of the accused, Additional Advocate General Anoop Trivedi and AGA First Paritosh Kumar Malviya were also present on behalf of the state government. As soon as the hearing began, the court said that the order could have been reserved after the hearing was completed, but later attempts were made by the accused to reach and contact the presiding judge. The court said that if such conduct is ignored, it will weaken the roots of judicial independence and the common people's faith in the justice system will be shaken. Judge said - Prestige of the judiciary cannot be put under the cloud of doubt Judge Krishna Pahal said, ‘If in such circumstances the decision had come in favor of the party whose arguments appeared strong, then despite the legal strength of the judgment, this doubt could have arisen that the decision was the result of some external influence or improper attempt rather than judicial discretion.’ The reputation of the judiciary earned over years cannot be put under the shadow of such doubt. The court said - Justice is not only sufficient to be done, but it should also be clearly and unequivocally seen that justice has been done impartially. Attempting to make personal contact with a judge in a pending case is against the ethics of advocate conduct and the constitutional values of an independent judiciary. The High Court, calling it an assault on judicial dignity, said that such a tendency cannot be accepted in the court premises under any circumstances. The court warned lawyers and accused, saying - Judicial independence is not a special privilege, but a constitutional right granted to every citizen. Any attempt to weaken it should be strongly condemned. High Court has already refused to cancel the case In the codeine cough syrup case, the accused first filed petitions to have the case cancelled, but these petitions were rejected by three different division benches of the High Court and one division bench of the Lucknow bench. The court said that there is sufficient basis for investigation in the matter. After this, the accused filed applications for anticipatory bail. Even on these anticipatory bail petitions, no relief was granted to any petitioner by the High Court, and arrests continued. Following this, petitions were filed for regular bail. In these too, the regular bail petitions of four accused have been rejected by different benches of the High Court. Case was registered on 15 November, 2025 In the case registered at Kotwali police station on 15 November, about 40 people, including Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal, were named. As the investigation progressed during the inquiry, many names came to light. Many of them have already been arrested. Now know what are the charges against Shubham A case has been registered at Kotwali against 28 drug traders of Kashi, including interstate gang leader Shubham Jaiswal and his father Bhola Jaiswal. The allegation is that 89 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup worth ₹100 crores were bought and sold. In the name of 93 medical stores in Kashi alone, 84 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup were bought and sold. Most of the medical stores in whose names the business was shown were not found at the location. Later, the fraud of this illegal business network spread across Bengal and Bangladesh was exposed. The investigation revealed that cough syrup was sold to 9 closed firms. These include Messrs Srishti Pharma, GT Enterprises, Shivam Pharma, Harsh Pharma, DSA Pharma, Mahakal Medical Store, Nishant Pharma, VPM Medical Agency and Shri Balaji Medical. According to the Commissioner, fake firms were created only for the purchase and sale of codeine-containing syrup. Cases are also registered against Shubham Jaiswal in other districts including Sonbhadra, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Ghaziabad, and Chandauli.
