stories.summary: West Bengal government has approved land acquisition for a new railway line. This project aims to improve connectivity to the India-China-Bhutan tri-junction area. The new rail link will boost tourism in the Jhaldhaka-Bindu-Todey Tangta region. Railways and the forest department will conduct a joint survey after the monsoon. This strategically important project was previously stalled due to state government non-cooperation.

stories.title: Child rights body takes up with Meta issue of CSAM ads on Instagram
stories.summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights has taken action against Meta, prompted by allegations regarding s associated with child exploitation materials on its platforms. Seeking accountability, the commission requested clarification from Meta about these grave concerns. After assessing the company's response, a formal investigation is now underway. This decision aligns with growing attention on child safety practices across digital platforms.

stories.title: Cyber crime reports down from 1.2L in 2024 to 16,377 now: Government
stories.summary: Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.

stories.title: WA tests optional age verification pilot, says user privacy will be protected
stories.summary: To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. With the new law's emphasis on stricter regulations for children's personal data, WhatsApp is taking care to safeguard user privacy during this important verification process.

stories.title: Government to grill Meta brass on child abuse, AI content
stories.summary: In an important meeting scheduled for this week, government officials will confront Meta executives regarding pressing issues. The discussions will center around the presence of child sexual abuse material, the rise of AI-created content, and the measures in place for takedowns involving notable personalities. Compliance with local laws and the efficiency of Meta's content moderation efforts, particularly in monitoring synthetic content, are also poised to be key topics of concern.

stories.title: Government may allow fees on UPI payment above Rs 2k
stories.summary: The government may allow a small charge on UPI payments exceeding two thousand rupees. This levy would apply to transactions made to businesses and not individuals. Official estimates suggest this change will impact only five percent of all UPI transactions. Most daily purchases like groceries and taxi fares will remain unaffected by this potential fee. Industry experts anticipate a possible ceiling on the absolute amount charged for these transactions.

stories.title: Over 30 operatives killed by 'Indian agents' since 2020: LeT commander
stories.summary: Rizwan Hanif, a commander affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba, has alleged that Indian agents have systematically killed more than thirty individuals in different Pakistani locations since 2020. He characterized these murders as acts of religious persecution and rejected the authority of foreign entities. This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

stories.title: Computer-based NEET? Govt tells SC decision after Nilekani report
stories.summary: The government informed the Supreme Court about considering NEET's shift to computer-based testing. This decision awaits the Nandan Nilekani task force's report on public examination systems. Measures are being taken to make the exam more secure and prevent unfair means. The National Testing Agency has already moved seven major exams to computer-based formats. NEET (UG) currently remains the only major pen-and-paper examination conducted by the NTA.

stories.title: '100% pure'? Stop misleading products' sale, FSSAI tells Dabur
stories.summary: Dabur India has been instructed by the FSSAI to halt the sale of items claiming to be '100% pure.' This decision stems from a violation of food regulations deemed misleading to consumers. The FSSAI identified unauthorized organic claims on various products. Despite Dabur's assertion that its labels meet regulatory standards, the company will eliminate '100%' references from its marketing efforts.

stories.title: Census phase 2 likely to accept half-filled forms
stories.summary: Census authorities are considering allowing partially filled online forms for self-enumeration. This change aims to ease the process for respondents and enumerators alike. Previously, blank fields prevented form submission, discouraging self-enumeration. The population enumeration exercise is scheduled nationwide for February 2027. Select snow-bound regions will conduct enumeration earlier, from September 1 to 30.

274 fugitives brought back from 36 nations since 2019
stories.summary: Government brought back 274 fugitives from 36 countries since 2019. Assets worth over Rs 17,874 crore were attached during this period. This contrasts with the UPA government's record of fewer extraditions annually. Legal frameworks were updated, and diplomatic efforts intensified for fugitive recovery. This approach reflects a coordinated "whole of government" strategy for justice.

stories.title: BJP attacks Cong 'double standards' on students stirs
stories.summary: The BJP has called out the Congress party for its hypocritical stance on examination irregularities. They pointed to the Congress's lack of response to student protests in both Jharkhand and Karnataka. Additionally, the BJP criticized Priyank Kharge for his defense of police action against demonstrators, claiming that the opposition is purposefully causing disruption in Parliament over these issues. The BJP argues that this selective outrage stems from political motivations.

stories.title: Florida tests exposed endangered Caribbean corals to predatory bacteria; over half resisted spread
stories.summary: In the Caribbean, researchers are exploring the use of predatory bacteria as a means to combat coral diseases. Laboratory tests have demonstrated that these microscopic bacteria can successfully eliminate harmful Vibrio bacteria while preserving the coral's vital microbiome. This promising method provides a focused mechanism to defend corals against disease. However, additional field trials are necessary for its application in conservation efforts.

stories.title: An illinois family gave its old farmhouse for firefighters to train inside before it burned
stories.summary: A four-generation family farmhouse in Illinois was given a meaningful final purpose before being demolished. The Kestel family donated the vacant house to the New Lenox Fire Protection District, where nearly 100 firefighters trained in realistic live-fire rescue and firefighting exercises over three days. Although watching the home burn was emotional, the family said knowing it helped firefighters gain life-saving experience made its final farewell a fitting tribute to their family's legacy of community service.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: 'Look for the job you would take if you didn't need a job' and timeless career advice
From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
stories.summary: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.

stories.title: For every Rs 100 India spends on R&D, govt gives Rs 48, pvt Rs 45
stories.summary: The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Additionally, multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping India's research environment, although the overall research intensity still lags behind other major economies.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Chandrika Kumaratunga: 'Power is a joke, but it gives me the authority to do what I think I need to do for the country'
US saw 2,562 woodwasp interceptions (1952–2020); wood packaging was the main pathway
stories.summary: Wooden packaging serves as the primary channel for introducing woodwasps across the globe. A thorough investigation reviewed decades of border inspection data from three different nations. Findings revealed that almost all interceptions were associated with pallets, crates, and other dunnage utilized in shipping. The evolution of trade routes has affected the source of these intercepted woodwasp species. Consequently, maintaining international regulations on wooden packaging is vital for enhancing biosecurity initiatives.

stories.title: China's tree patches restored forests, but reached only 19–30% of natural diversity in 20 years
stories.summary: A 20-year study in southwest China found that planting small patches of native trees can help restore damaged tropical forests without planting entire landscapes. The approach successfully rebuilt forest cover, but researchers found that biodiversity and mature forest conditions recovered much more slowly, showing that long-term restoration still requires sustained effort.

stories.title: Big clean energy milestone: NPCIL cumulatively generates over 1,000 bn units of N-power, avoids 860 million tons of CO2 emissions
stories.summary: India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.

stories.title: MPs feel left out of foundation stone laying, parliamentary panel steps in
stories.summary: A parliamentary panel has called attention to the frequent exclusion of MPs from events related to rural road schemes. To rectify this, the committee has urged the introduction of mandatory invitations for MPs to ceremonies. Additionally, it proposed uploading high-quality photos showcasing MP involvement online. A quarterly system will be implemented to monitor adherence to these protocols, ensuring that the established parliamentary etiquette is upheld for PMGSY projects.

stories.title: Egyptian doctor wrongly connects organ in a way that bowel waste is channeled back to stomach, UK cancels his licence
Terror suspects spotted, search ops launched in J&K’s Poonch
stories.summary: Following intelligence indicating potential terror suspects in Poonch, security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported. Earlier, a significant search initiative was executed in the Thanamandi area of Rajouri district.

stories.title: Experts warn great white sharks are 'already lurking off UK beaches' and another toothy predator could follow
stories.summary: With rising ocean temperatures, great white sharks are migrating further north than ever documented. Researchers suggest that these formidable predators might already be silently exploring British waters. This phenomenon signifies a broader ecological crisis, forcing various marine species to adapt their hunting and migration patterns in response to shifting sea temperatures, highlighting the urgent need for conservation efforts.

stories.title: Scientists identified seven new diamond frog species in Madagascar after a 12-year search
stories.summary: Scientists have identified seven new diamond frog species in Madagascar. These discoveries highlight the island's extensive undocumented wildlife and hidden diversity. Modern genetic tools and traditional anatomy revealed evolutionary differences previously unseen. Many of these frogs inhabit small, isolated ranges, emphasizing conservation needs. This finding underscores Madagascar's ongoing biological mysteries and the importance of habitat protection.

stories.title: Vaishno Devi fake silver row: Court seeks detailed probe report, orders evidence preservation
stories.summary: The Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate has taken decisive action by ordering the preservation of evidence in a troubling case of fake silver offerings amounting to Rs 550 crore. In response to a petition seeking to secure all relevant physical and electronic evidence, the court acknowledged allegations of adulteration and pilferage concerning around twenty tonnes of silver.

stories.title: NC, PDP announce protest plans; BJP to celebrate Article 370 abrogation
stories.summary: Kashmir's political landscape will witness separate protests from the NC and PDP this Wednesday, marking seven years since Article 370 was abrogated. The NC is pushing for the restoration of its statehood, whereas the PDP demands the reinstatement of Article 370. Meanwhile, BJP's celebratory events, including a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, suggest a contrasting narrative on the changes in Jammu and Kashmir's sentiments following the abrogation.

stories.title: After opening golf tournament, CM Omar says authorities must not allow repeat of migrant worker killings
stories.summary: Omar Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers, emphasizing that such acts are unacceptable and calling for heightened security measures. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area, recalling a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, well before militancy took root.

stories.title: CPI (ML) L whose students wing was at forefront of Gen Z protests wants voting age lowered to 16
Rooftop solar scheme crosses 50-lakh household mark
Over 170 migrants rescued after Channel boat catches fire; UK says 'all will be returned' to France
Why vultures can eat rotten meat without getting sick
US built a neighbourhood upon 22,000 tons of buried toxic waste, then children began returning home with burns
stories.summary: Originally designed to be a groundbreaking canal project, this site succumbed to a fate of pollution as industrial and municipal waste accumulated over decades. The catastrophic rainfall in 1976 triggered the release of these harmful chemicals into nearby homes, displacing numerous families. This incident catalyzed the formation of the Superfund program, dedicated to remedying toxic environmental disasters across the nation.

stories.title: Indian cargo vessel sinks after attack in Yemeni waters; all 14 crew rescued
US judge blocks New York's ban on ICE officers wearing face masks
EU eyes tougher border controls after Ceuta migrant surge triggers alarm
stories.summary: European Union ministers are demanding stricter measures against migrant smuggling networks. They also seek stronger return policies following a large influx into Ceuta. The bloc is enhancing border security and intelligence sharing with external partners. Disinformation by smugglers fueled the unprecedented migration surge into the Spanish enclave. This crisis has reignited divisions within the European Union over migration management.

stories.title: Gaza mass funeral for 112 Palestinians, including dozens of children, recovered from 2023 strike
New rules for US citizenship: Trump administration wants new educational requirement for naturalization
Child protection panel launches inquiry into Meta over alleged child sexual abuse material ads
stories.summary: The NCPCR has initiated a formal investigation following alarming claims from a BBC report which suggested that s on Meta’s platforms like Instagram were linked to the promotion of child abuse material. In response, the child rights organization has demanded clarity from Meta Platforms Inc. Furthermore, the NHRC has instructed the Delhi Police to look into these troubling assertions, as both entities scrutinize Meta's adherence to child protection regulations.

stories.title: ‘No insurance, no fuel’: SC directs govt to prepare pilot project, flags 16.54 crore uninsured vehicles
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has initiated a pilot project that connects fuel supply to the vehicle's insurance status, aiming to enhance adherence to mandatory third-party insurance laws. Additionally, the court has extended the insurance requirement period for new vehicles, intending to ensure that accident victims receive prompt compensation. Monitoring compliance will be supported by automatic number plate recognition cameras.

stories.title: ‘Will give fitting reply at appropriate time’: Sunetra Pawar on Congress’ ‘gungi gudiya’ jibe
IShowSpeed criticizes Diamond Gym’s "fatigue maxxing" after seeing 300 burpees before workout
stories.summary: IShowSpeed, the internet sensation, recently shared his thoughts on a trending clip from Diamond Gym. He expressed concern over the gym’s rigorous practice of performing 300 burpees before workouts. Known as 'fatigue maxxing', this method aims for maximum exhaustion. Diamond Gym has gained notoriety for its extreme training styles, and Speed's critique has sparked new discussions surrounding these intense fitness trends.

stories.title: 75-country Green Card ban illegal, rules Indian-American judge Amit Mehta; DHS says Trump upholding highest standards
Study finds 84% of U.S. coastal wetlands sinking as seas rise
Toxic plants yield enzymes that could power future medicines
'Good precedent': Kangana Ranaut backs police action against Udhayanidhi Stalin for crass remark
B.C. restores 70 hectares as Cowichan marsh faces 60% loss by 2100
stories.summary: British Columbia invests $500,000 in a large-scale Cowichan Estuary restoration project. This initiative aims to strengthen watershed health and improve climate resilience for the region. The project focuses on rebuilding vital habitat for fish and wildlife populations. Indigenous stewardship is central, guiding land use and planting culturally significant species. This significant effort protects biodiversity and supports local communities dependent on the estuary.

stories.title: Farmers back ethanol in meeting with agriculture minister, say it will boost income, secure energy
Uttarakhand CM Dhami welcomes Kanwariyas in Haridwar, inaugurates health camp amid Kanwar Yatra
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday welcomed Kanwariyas arriving in Haridwar for the annual Kanwar Yatra, showering flower petals on Shiva devotees from a helicopter and washing the feet of five pilgrims as a mark of respect.

stories.title: “Extinct” snail returns—1,000 reintroduced to Norfolk Island after 30 years
stories.summary: Campbell's keeled glass snails have reached a major conservation milestone on Norfolk Island. Over one thousand critically endangered snails have now been released onto the island. This marks a significant comeback after the species was presumed lost for decades. The successful recovery program involved extensive collaboration and captive breeding efforts. Researchers will continue monitoring the snails to ensure population growth and survival.

stories.title: SC calls to 'dismantle' ‘men’s clubs’ in Bar Councils, orders co-option of 2 women members
Archaeologists uncover 600-year-old saint statue beneath Berlin's oldest district
stories.summary: Excavations in Berlin's Molkenmarkt uncovered medieval religious artefacts from the 14th and 15th centuries. These discoveries include well-preserved saint figurines and a Madonna and Child sculpture. An extraordinary cache of ceramic figures containing human bone fragments was also found. These finds offer fresh evidence of devotional practices in medieval urban life. The discoveries contribute to understanding medieval Berlin and its spiritual traditions.

stories.title: From Hype To Help: How AI Is Solving India's Real Problems
stories.summary: India is harnessing the power of artificial intelligence to address its various developmental challenges effectively. In educational settings, AI supports teachers in remote areas, while in agriculture, it assists farmers facing changing climate conditions. The healthcare system is being transformed through AI-driven diagnostics, and access to government services is increasing. Furthermore, AI contributes to strengthening climate resilience and streamlining agricultural loan assessments, prompting significant investments in the necessary infrastructure.

stories.title: Security on high alert in Jammu & Kashmir: Pakistani drone sighted in Kathua, anti-terror search intensifies in Poonch
stories.summary: A Pakistani drone was spotted over Kathua's Hiranagar sector, prompting a security search. Security forces also conducted a large anti-terror operation in Poonch district. An unexploded mortar shell was recovered from a house in Kathua. These events occur amid heightened tensions along the India-Pakistan border. India stated it will safeguard its national interests as needed.

stories.title: Meet Darshan Magdum, Indian member of US boy band, who finally gets O-1 visa and the Internet is behind it
Iran war depletes US missile stocks, raises concerns over readiness for China
Delhi SIR dates extended: BLO visits till August 17, final rolls on October 27
How the US army built the 1,500-mile Alaska Highway in just 8 months
Hidden for 2,000 years, this Egyptian tomb held 560 ushabti figurines meant to serve the dead in the afterlife
stories.summary: Excavations at Tell Quesna have revealed a remarkable funerary complex adorned with hundreds of burial artifacts. Among the treasures, archaeologists discovered 560 ushabti figurines, believed to assist the deceased in the afterlife. Additional finds included protective amulets and pottery, with imported items from Rhodes highlighting trade links with the Mediterranean. These artifacts significantly enhance our knowledge of ancient Egyptian spiritual beliefs and rituals.

stories.title: When Jeff Bezos asked his team to help after a rainforest charity saving the Amazon said it was blocked from using 'Amazon' in Google Ads
What is 'Operation Fortress'? Reform UK's military plan to stop migrants crossing English Channel
'RSS involvement in Sainik Schools increasing', says Rahul Gandhi; Parl panel chief demands evidence
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged increasing RSS involvement in Sainik Schools during a committee meeting. He referred to a media report while making his claim to the panel. The committee chair asked Rahul Gandhi to provide supporting documents for his allegations. Other BJP members also questioned the basis of his statements. Gandhi has previously accused the RSS of capturing public institutions.

stories.title: ‘Why the hurry?' Punjab Assembly opposes E20 policy, alleges Centre acted under US pressure
stories.summary: Punjab's Assembly passed a resolution opposing the Centre's E20 fuel policy. Concerns were raised about potential vehicle damage from the higher ethanol blend. The state questioned the accelerated rollout and alleged external pressure influenced the decision. The Aam Aadmi Party is campaigning nationwide against the policy. They demand consumer choice and lower prices for the blended fuel.

stories.title: How John Beal transformed polluted Hamm Creek into a thriving salmon habitat
stories.summary: John Beal, a dedicated Vietnam veteran, took it upon himself to revive Seattle's Hamm Creek, which had suffered from pollution. His approach included removing trash and reintroducing native plants to restore the ecosystem. By founding I'M A PAL, Beal rallied local volunteers and secured necessary funding, reigniting community passion. His perseverance has led to Hamm Creek's reintegration with the Duwamish River, fostering rich wildlife and ensuring a lasting ecological legacy.

stories.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin arrest drama: 'No double meaning in my speech; TN CM using diversion tactic,' says DMK leader - top developments
stories.summary: Udhayanidhi Stalin faced arrest over alleged remarks linked to actor Trisha. The Madras High Court directed his release on station bail after questioning. DMK workers staged protests across Tamil Nadu following the arrest. The TVK government and opposition engaged in a war of words. Udhayanidhi denied allegations and stated his remarks were distorted.

stories.title: Only 4 companies? Critics say barring small companies from hiring H-1B for 1-2 years is not enough
'Madrassa pass-outs develop terrorist-like mindset': UP deputy CM Keshav Maurya
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters at Vidhan Bhavan, Maurya alleged that madrassa students do not express patriotic slogans and linked their education to extremism. "Anyone who receives a madrassa education does not chant 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' nor sing 'Vande Mataram', and develops a terrorist-like mindset," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. The remarks were strongly criticised by senior Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav.

stories.title: California's Ranch fire burned 459,123 acres; 8 years later, 71,000 seedlings have been planted
stories.summary: Eight years after California's devastating Ranch Fire burned more than 459,000 acres, the US Forest Service and partner organisations planted 71,000 conifer seedlings in just eight days. The reforestation effort is part of a long-term plan to restore damaged forest, reduce future wildfire risk and support natural recovery across the Mendocino National Forest.

stories.title: How people in Chile's Atacama Desert evolved to survive drinking arsenic-poisoned water
Scientists discover Greenland sharks can see for centuries, debunking blindness myth
stories.summary: Recent studies reveal that Greenland sharks possess well-preserved visual systems that can last for centuries, challenging the previous notion that they were nearly blind. Research shows that their eyes are uniquely suited for low-light environments, demonstrating impressive adaptability. Scientists found healthy rod cells and active genes responsible for light detection, indicating these sharks have a remarkable ability to maintain their eyesight throughout their extended lifespans.

stories.title: Dordoi Bazaar: Shipping container market to commercial heart of Central Asia
'Private media entity organising it': Govt says 'no role' in Sheikh Hasina's proposed August 5 event
stories.summary: The MEA stated no government involvement in a private media event. The proposed forum concerns former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh sought clarification from India regarding its support for the event. Hasina resigned in August 2024 and has been living in Delhi. She faces a death sentence for crimes against humanity.

stories.title: 'Insult to nation': Mamata attacks BJP over Netaji remarks, alleges pressure on TMC leaders
'Who is PM Modi to forgive?' Rahul says students 'need apology not forgiveness'
stories.summary: In an Instagram video posted on Friday night PM said that he will forgive young protesters accused of abusing him and his late mother, saying they are misguided children and it is “our job to show them the right way” “Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve their child. Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them - and serious questions about a broken education system,” Gandhi said in a post on X where he also shared images of his interaction with parents and students.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Giorgia Meloni: "To the women of this nation I want to say that being underestimated is a great advantage, because…”
North Carolina man worked 100-hour weeks for 58 years to save a bankrupt boat company, rejected a $400 million offer and gave it to charity
SC orders nationwide action against 'digital arrest' scams; tells RBI to share SOP on 'mule accounts'
'Answered public discontent with bullets and repression': MEA slams Pakistan over 'farce' PoK polls
stories.summary: In a strong statement, the Ministry of External Affairs demanded action against cross-border terrorism, directly targeting groups like Lashkar-e-Taiba following claims about Indian agencies taking down their commanders. They lambasted the local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as illegitimate, citing repression of civilians by Pakistani forces. Moreover, India urged the global community to address Pakistan's actions firmly.

stories.title: 'Will do whatever is necessary for national interest': India after Pakistan deploys 250 Chinese Howitzers
stories.summary: India stated it will protect national interests after Pakistan deployed Chinese artillery guns. Pakistan has reportedly deployed around 250 Chinese-made SH-15 artillery systems. India criticized Pakistan's recent elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir as a farce. The spokesperson noted civilian deaths during a crackdown in the region. Both nations continue to modernize their respective artillery capabilities.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark; flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence & more
Travel planning India's most underappreciated vacation task: Survey
Scottish biotech company turned whisky waste into a source of omega-3
Scientists find slugs, beetles and crabs help spread seeds for 186 plant species
'Gungi gudiya' row: NCP workers barge into Maharashtra Congress office over remark on deputy CM Sunetra Pawar — watch
'Decisions at appropriate time': Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren breaks silence on recruitment row amid protests
stories.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren addressed recruitment row concerns seriously. Protesting job aspirants demand an independent probe into examination irregularities. The state CID investigation is gathering pace with several arrests made. Former CM Raghubar Das urged dialogue and a CBI inquiry for justice. The indefinite sit-in continues, with protesters vowing to escalate their agitation.

stories.title: Biodiversity boosts forest growth; loss could cut gains 17% by 2050
'Sadhu-saint not involved': CM Yogi on Ram Mandir donation theft case
stories.summary: Addressing reporters, CM Yogi said said the initial SIT report had not found any involvement of religious figures in the alleged theft of offerings made at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple. "No involvement of any sadhu-saint was found in the SIT's initial report in the case related to the alleged embezzlement of offerings (chadhava) at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple," he said.

stories.title: More than 330,000 gallons of rotting fish sauce in a Canadian town are finally being removed after 20 years of unbearable stench
Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to…"
How Korea's Haenyeo developed extraordinary cold resistance that lets them dive into near-freezing seas without oxygen tanks, even in their 70s
When wildfires make their own weather: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
stories.summary: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026. This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms. India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency. While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable. The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

stories.title: Andrew Tate's lawyer warns Trump of political fallout if he doesn't help jailed influencer in UK extradition case
How Felix Dennis launched a 10 million-tree vision to restore England's woodlands
stories.summary: Felix Dennis began planting a small wood in 1996, which grew into the Heart of England Forest. This project aimed to restore native broadleaf trees across South Warwickshire. The charity was established in 2003 to continue purchasing and planting land. Dennis envisioned 25,000 acres of woodland open to the public. After his death in 2014, the forest has expanded significantly.

stories.title: Scientists discover four dangerous fish bacteria in Brazil for the first time; one has jumped to a new host species
stories.summary: For the first time, Brazil faces a significant challenge as bacteria previously exclusive to Asia and the USA have been identified within its borders. These bacteria, known to cause columnaris disease, pose an acute risk to the thriving aquaculture sector. Researchers have isolated four species from the Flavobacterium genus, which can infect both Nile tilapia and indigenous fish species.

stories.title: Arrested Jaish suspect surveyed area near CM Suvendu Adhikari's residence: Official
'Many friends yet to return': Patna students restart protest over NEET stir crackdown
stories.summary: The demonstrators demanded immediate release of all students still in jail and the withdrawal of criminal cases registered against those arrested during the statewide agitation. "We want a verified list of those who have been released from jail and those who are still behind bars after being arrested during the protests," one of the protesters said. A student activist from Siwan also alleged excessive use of force during earlier protests.

stories.title: Ancient Roman women left more than 120 inscriptions inside a hidden cave in Spain dedicated to a mysterious goddess
Scientists warn Earth could hit the 1.5°C climate limit sooner than expected
stories.summary: Global warming has significantly accelerated, with the past decade warming faster than any comparable period. Researchers removed natural climate fluctuations to reveal this underlying warming trend. Five major global temperature datasets confirm this acceleration with high statistical confidence. This observed increase suggests the world may approach key climate thresholds sooner. The long-term trend could cross the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C limit before this decade ends.

stories.title: Iran won't escalate tensions but will defend itself, says Pezeshkian amid Trump's warning
stories.summary: Iran states it will defend its security while the US president claims a last chance for a deal. Conflicting reports emerge regarding ongoing negotiations between Iran and the United States. Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz remains subdued amid these diplomatic claims. Iran's IRGC reportedly launched a drone attack on a US military base in Kuwait. Tehran also prepared retaliatory strikes on Ukraine after a vessel incident.

stories.title: Madras HC orders Udhayanidhi Stalin's release after arrest over 'double meaning' remark
World's oldest amber has been found in China, and it is 65 million years older than expected
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, scientists uncovered ancient amber specimens in China that are approximately 385 million years old. This significant find pushes the amber fossil record back by an impressive sixty-five million years. It indicates that early vascular plants may have developed advanced resin-producing capabilities, which could have provided a defensive advantage against wildfires and fungal diseases. The research advances our understanding of plant resilience during the Devonian era.

stories.title: Countries with most black mambas: From South Africa to Kenya, where the deadly snake is found
stories.summary: The black mamba, often cited as the most dangerous snake on the African continent, occupies a wide array of habitats. This snake thrives in arid savannas and rocky terrains throughout sub-Saharan Africa. Countries such as South Africa and Zimbabwe frequently report incidents of black mamba bites. Remarkably, sightings have increased in Kenya and Zambia at higher altitudes, with Tanzania and Botswana also within its expansive territory.

stories.title: Scientists in Iceland are turning carbon dioxide into stone by injecting it into volcanic rock, and it could redefine the fight against climate change
Europe's shrinking rivers have hit shipping, power and tourism
stories.summary: Record low water levels in Europe's major rivers are disrupting electricity production, cargo transport and business operations as heatwaves and drought continue across the continent. Nuclear and hydropower plants have cut output, shipping on the Danube and Rhine has slowed, and companies are reporting lower earnings, highlighting the growing economic impact of prolonged extreme weather

stories.title: Long before GPS, Polynesian sailors crossed the Pacific by reading stars, waves, winds, birds and clouds
Sudden drop in altitude: Flyers injured as Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence
Mark Zuckerberg's wife invested $125 million in a school for the disadvantaged; now she is closing it to focus on AI
stories.summary: The Primary School, offering tuition-free education to low-income families, has officially closed, impacting around 540 children who depended on its support. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, the school's benefactor, is redirecting its resources towards biotechnology and artificial intelligence. As part of its commitment, it has announced substantial funding aimed at assisting affected students and local organizations.

stories.title: Rose-ringed parakeets: From escaped pets to one of the most recognisable birds
AAP protest E20 petrol policy: Kejriwal, Sisodia stage sit-in after march to PM Modi's residence stopped
stories.summary: Delhi Police stopped Arvind Kejriwal and AAP leaders marching to Prime Minister Modi's residence. The party staged a sit-in protest on Firoz Shah Road after being prevented from proceeding. They carried over 2.30 lakh petitions against the Centre's E20 petrol policy. Kejriwal stated the government should listen to vehicle owners' concerns about the fuel.

stories.title: HC to FDA: Why was license suspended despite 100% compliance? Who will pay for losses?
'Promoting enmity, provoking riot': What are the 9 charges against Udhayanidhi Stalin over Trisha remarks
Centre summons Meta's global team on August 5-6 to raise CSAM, AI concerns
'I will fight tooth and nail': Brewery owner who offered free beer if Trump died, loses licence
stories.summary: Kirk Bangstad, owner of Wisconsin's Minocqua Brewing Company, has vowed to "fight tooth and nail" after the state revoked his brewery's operating permits. The action follows allegations that the company illegally transported beer from Illinois without the required permits or paying taxes. Bangstad, whose brewery previously made headlines for promising free beer if Donald Trump died, called the revocation an "absurd act of heavy-handedness" and plans to appeal.

stories.title: Cocaine worth 1,002 lbs found hidden in rebar truck at California border
stories.summary: Federal officers seized more than $20 million in cocaine hidden beneath the floorboards of a commercial truck carrying 269 bundles of rebar at California’s Calexico border crossing, arresting the driver after finding 366 packages of narcotics.

stories.title: UK pilot spots mysterious 'flying saucer' just 100 feet from passenger plane near Gatwick Airport; officials say the near miss reduced the aircraft's safety
Cancelled experiment: Britain tried to test a balloon that could cool the planet
Russia downs 320 drones: Six killed, warehouses damaged in Moscow, St Petersburg
stories.summary: Russia’s defence ministry said it brought down or destroyed 320 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions overnight, as governors reported six people killed, nine injured and warehouses damaged near Moscow and St Petersburg.

stories.title: 'Did I say anything wrong?' Udhayanidhi Stalin's first reaction after detention over 'vulgar' remark
A rare yellow-flowered California plant unseen since 1957 has been rediscovered
'Resignations are part of politics': DKS on two Congress MLAs quitting over Karnataka cabinet snub

Meet Jo Nagai: 10-year-old Japanese student who discovered butterflies can remember their time as caterpillars after he noticed that the caterpillars he had raised to recognise him after turning into butterflies
Video of dolphin carrying its dead newborn through the Indian Ocean reveals a deep and old 'mourning ritual'
stories.summary: Fraggle, a grieving mother dolphin, carried her deceased calf for six days, a poignant testament to her profound maternal love. Captured by drone footage in the Indian Ocean, this heart-wrenching scene revealed the support of her pod, which gathered around her in solidarity during her mourning. This behavior, seen in over twenty cetacean species, underscores their intricate social connections and possible awareness of mortality.

stories.title: Volunteers spent 40 days inside a French cave believing only 30 days had passed
Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, who probed Babri Masjid demolition, dies at 87
CRPF officer kills two colleagues, injures one before killing self in Assam
Most ancient Arctic carbon entering the ocean gets buried
‘Two sides of same coin’: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose quits TMC, takes swipe at BJP
'Long history of unlawful violence': Global watchdogs condemn Pakistan's crackdown in PoK
stories.summary: International oversight bodies are sounding the alarm over growing violence and restrictions on media freedom during elections. Amnesty International has documented harsh actions against protesters in PoK's Rawalakot, and the Committee to Protect Journalists has identified worsening conditions for reporters. Alarmingly, two independent journalists are reportedly missing after being abducted from their office, with the protest movement accounting for more than eighty fatalities.

stories.title: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts under review, temporarily blocks access for users
Indian agents killed over 30 LeT operatives in Pakistan since 2020, claims Lashkar leader
Govt proposes mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication systems from Oct 2028 to cut road crashes
21 Bangladesh nationals detained in J&K’s Ramban
stories.summary: Twenty-one Bangladesh nationals were detained in Ramban district last week. Officials are questioning them to learn who facilitated their movement. The group was caught moving in two vehicles during a checking drive. None of them could produce valid identity or travel documents. Investigators are probing if any network assisted these illegal immigrants.

stories.title: Mortar shells found in Poonch border villages
J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
stories.summary: A suspect was apprehended in Pulwama carrying a hand grenade and anti-national posters. This arrest occurred during a security operation following recent migrant worker killings. Authorities booked the local man under stringent anti-terror laws, including the UAPA. Security forces are increasing patrols and checkpoints across the valley. This intensified security aims to maintain peace and prevent further unlawful activities.

stories.title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
stories.summary: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, a significant increase over previous years. Delhi-NCR led the nation in transplant procedures, while Tamil Nadu topped deceased organ donors. India now ranks third globally in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Deceased donor transplants continue to fall short of the substantial demand for organs. Government initiatives aim to strengthen organ donation and transplant services across the country.

stories.title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
stories.summary: The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters. This move aims to allow students to pursue their studies without prosecution fears. However, cases against individuals with criminal records will not be dropped. The court will also establish guidelines for the use of graded force by police. Discussions on modalities for dropping cases against genuine students are ongoing.

stories.title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
stories.summary: The Census 2027 population enumeration phase begins August 17 in snow-bound northern areas. This phase will capture caste details for the first time since 1931. Parents' date and birthplace will also be recorded as declared by respondents. Passport and Aadhaar numbers may be collected voluntarily during the exercise. The questionnaire for this significant census phase will be notified soon.

stories.title: 60 venomous snakes, cocaine, guns and 22,000 dollars in cash seized during New Mexico drug raid
stories.summary: Federal agents investigating an alleged cocaine trafficking operation in New Mexico made a shocking discovery after uncovering 60 snakes, half a pound of cocaine, three firearms and 22,000 dollars in cash during a raid on a home in the South Valley area near Albuquerque. The seizure inventory included cobras, mambas, pit vipers and pythons, along with an inland taipan, widely regarded as one of the world's most venomous snakes.

stories.title: Opposition toughens stand, washout of session likely
stories.summary: Parliament's monsoon session faces potential washout amid opposition demands. Opposition insists on discussing Ram temple donations and police actions. Union ministers criticize opposition for boycotting legislative proceedings. Bills were passed without debate due to the ongoing parliamentary standoff. The government has not yet assured discussions on the opposition's key demands.

stories.title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS
stories.summary: The Unified Pension Scheme for central government employees has seen low adoption rates. Only a small percentage of National Pension Trust

stories.title: Meta CEO Zuckerberg must apologise: Parliamentary Panel
SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has sought the government's response regarding the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act. Concerns were raised that the new law might erase existing benefits for transgender individuals. Senior advocates reported that hormone treatment is being denied due to fear of prosecution. They also alleged the discontinuation of the national portal for transgenders. The court questioned the retrospective invalidation of previously issued transgender identity cards.

stories.title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
stories.summary: Government agencies are considering releasing the ARAI study on E20 fuel's impact. This report, submitted in June 2024, studied E10-compatible vehicles. Fuel consumption increased slightly for two-wheelers and cars in the study. Mass emissions met regulatory requirements for all vehicles tested. The release aims to remove misconceptions among vehicle users about E20 fuel.

stories.title: After success of students protest, Kisan Morcha plans to hit streets
Quote of the day by Paulo Coelho: 'If you're brave enough to say goodbye, life will reward you with a new hello'
Man reunited with lost wedding ring after 10 years as 9-year-old niece finds it in Minnesota lake
stories.summary: A Minnesota man has been reunited with his wedding ring nearly a decade after losing it at the bottom of a lake, thanks to an unexpected discovery by his 9-year-old niece during a family vacation. Stephen Meyer lost his wedding ring in 2016 while swimming with his son in Lake Belle Taine, where his family owns a cabin.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Marco Rubio: 'God has blessed me in many ways but none more important than my wife Jeanette'
'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
stories.summary: The FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. This practice misrepresents the true nature of alcoholic beverages and misleads consumers. Manufacturers were found using neutral alcohol and adding identical flavouring substances. Several companies, including United Spirits, faced prohibitions and notices. The regulator stressed that characteristic taste should develop naturally through base ingredients.

stories.title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has extended legal protection to live-in relationships. These relationships are now covered under Section 498A of the IPC. The court stated that the law must adapt to changing societal norms. Cruelty within such relationships will now be punishable by law. This decision aims to protect women from domestic violence and harassment.

stories.title: Quote by Ludwig Wittgenstein: 'The real question of life after death isn't whether or not it exists...'
stories.summary: Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein challenged the preoccupation with life after death, suggesting that eternal existence does not address the fundamental questions of life’s meaning. His reflections emerged amidst the chaos of World War One. In contemporary discussions on digital immortality, this crucial insight often gets overshadowed; authentic meaning resides in fully embracing the present and living with intention.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JS Mill: 'I have learned to seek my happiness by limiting my desires...'
stories.summary: Victorian philosopher John Stuart Mill believed that true happiness lies in limiting our desires rather than endlessly pursuing them. After facing a mental crisis due to his upbringing, Mill shifted his philosophy, warning that unending desire leads to a hedonic treadmill. Today, our consumer-driven culture reflects this endless chase; by curbing material wishes, we can unlock a wealth of inner fulfillment and deeper contentment.

stories.title: Man rejects Rs 2 crore offer in India and chooses $160K in the US because...
Colombia intercepted a boat near the Malpelo sanctuary carrying 1,764 pounds of marine animals

stories.title: In 1974, Spain imported two tons of American red crayfish for aquaculture; 50 years later...
stories.summary: Fifty years ago, American red crayfish were introduced to Spain's Guadalquivir River basin, and they have since established a permanent presence. These aggressive invaders have wreaked havoc on local wildlife and disrupted aquatic ecosystems. Yet, local communities have successfully built an economy around their harvesting and processing. This dependence has sparked legal disputes, resulting in a compromise that permits regulated harvesting, balancing ecological health with economic viability.

stories.title: In 2022, France promised 1 billion trees within a decade; four years later, a court...
stories.summary: France's top court invalidated a tree-planting funding decree due to procedural flaws. Ministers failed to consult the public on forestry subsidies impacting biodiversity. This ruling halts financial support for planting one billion trees over ten years. The government must now create a new legal framework with public input. Future funding will focus on restoring damaged forests and promoting diverse tree species.

Victoria’s 1987 forest experiment surprised researchers 30 years later
stories.summary: In a pioneering study within Victoria's mountain ash forests, surprising findings have emerged over extended periods. Intense thinning of trees fostered lush growth and increased diameters in the surviving trees. These enhanced specimens exhibit greater fire resilience and are likely to create hollows for various wildlife. Interestingly, Leadbeater's possums thrived in thinned and acacia zones, absent from untouched areas. This indicates that forest thinning may yield substantial ecological advantages.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Tom Holland: I personally think if something's not a challenge, there's no point doing it, because you're not gonna learn much
stories.summary: Tom Holland underscores the significance of challenges in fostering personal growth and learning. Starting his career on stage, he seamlessly transitioned to international fame, mainly as Spider-Man in the Marvel cinematic universe. His ability to take on varied roles in different genres showcases his dedication to artistic exploration. Holland's evolution serves as a powerful reminder to embrace adversity as a stepping stone to success.

stories.title: Meet Will Grand, the LSU graduate who turned food waste into 10,000 meals
stories.summary: A simple observation about food waste at Louisiana State University led former student Will Grand to start Giving Greek, a student-run organisation that has donated more than 10,000 meals to a Baton Rouge homeless shelter. The largest moon in the Solar System is bigger than Mercury and hides an ocean beneath its icy surface
stories.summary: Ganymede, Jupiter's largest moon, possesses planet-like dimensions and a hidden ocean. This moon is larger than Mercury and contains more water than Earth's oceans. Ganymede also generates its own magnetic field, which is unique among moons. Its layered interior includes an iron core and a rocky mantle. These features make Ganymede an extraordinary and planet-like celestial body.

stories.title: ‘Can some amount be released from frozen TMC funds?’ SC asks ED on Mamata-led faction’s plea
stories.summary: The Supreme Court questioned the Enforcement Directorate regarding fund release for TMC's daily expenses. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal argued the party cannot pay employee salaries currently. The Enforcement Directorate opposed the submissions, citing an ongoing money laundering investigation. The court is hearing a plea challenging the Calcutta High Court's refusal of interim relief. The Enforcement Directorate froze accounts holding over Rs 440 crore as part of its probe.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Robert De Niro: Time goes on. So whatever you're going to do. Don't wait
stories.summary: Robert De Niro emphasizes the necessity of taking prompt action in his thought-provoking quote. Renowned for his remarkable performances, De Niro also co-established the Tribeca Film Festival, aiming to support Manhattan's resurgence. His enduring career showcases a commitment to growth and embracing challenges. This powerful message serves as a reminder to capitalize on opportunities and refrain from delay.

stories.title: N3on Toronto Caribana Carnival golf cart accident explained: What really happened?

N3on was a passenger and not driving the golf cart when the accident happened. An injured woman was taken for surgery and is reportedly recovering well. Several rumors about lawsuits and injuries have circulated online since the event.

stories.title: Western Australia’s humpback sightings fell 60%; days later, weakened Southern Ocean seabirds appeared thousands of kilometres away on the country’s east coast
stories.summary: Unusual whale and seabird sightings in the Southern Ocean suggest changing ocean conditions. Marine heat waves are affecting waters around Australia and Antarctica. These warming events disrupt food webs and push marine life off course. Limited monitoring hinders understanding of these significant ecosystem shifts. Better long-term data is urgently needed to track these accelerating changes.

stories.title: $10k grant helped grow 3,500 hectares of forest protecting Kalgoorlie
stories.summary: Kalgoorlie-Boulder once suffered severe dust storms due to mining activities. A greening initiative began in the 1970s to combat this environmental problem. Thousands of hectares of forest now protect the city from windblown dust. This long-term project dramatically reduced dust levels over twenty years. The city now enjoys improved air quality and beautified landscapes.

Promising results were observed during tests in a Costa Rican forest reserve, providing a scalable approach to studying primate cognition in real-world settings.

Captive-born frogs lack essential toxins, which are likely produced by skin bacteria in their natural habitat. Scientists are experimenting with feeding toxins to frogs and studying their biology for conservation to protect vital ecosystems and biodiversity.

stories.summary: Renowned as one of Africa's deadliest inhabitants, the black mamba is a swift and aggressive serpent that can grow to an impressive fourteen feet. Its venom, rich in neurotoxins, results in a fatality rate of nearly one hundred percent if medical intervention is not administered promptly. In many remote regions, the difficulty of obtaining antivenin enhances the danger these snakes present.

In 2016, nations created the world's largest marine reserve in Antarctica
stories.summary: The Ross Sea Marine Protected Area became a global conservation milestone after years of negotiation. This vast Antarctic reserve was established by the CCAMLR member states in 2016. It protects a significant marine ecosystem supporting diverse wildlife and vital phytoplankton blooms. Scientific study of climate change impacts is also a key benefit of this protected area. stories.title: Scientists claim the shrinking Pacific Ocean will lead to the formation of a new supercontinent 'Amasia'
stories.summary: The Pacific Ocean, which is the largest ocean on Earth, is gradually shrinking due to the convergence of tectonic plates. Subduction zones around its edges are consuming the ocean floor at a rate faster than new material is formed. Scientists estimate that in 200 to 300 million years, the Pacific could entirely close up, pulling continents together to create a new supercontinent.

Scientists mapped the shrinking ice cap to identify the best site for drilling the mountain's first ice core, hoping it will reveal thousands of years of environmental and archaeological information before melting erases it.

Meet the General Grant Tree: The world's second-largest tree that became America's only living National Shrine

Eisenhower declared it a living National Shrine in nineteen fifty-six. This sequoia honors men and women who served the nation. Its size and history make it a remarkable natural landmark.

stories.title: Raji Doshi, 12, designed an algae system to reduce ocean acidity; now eyes $25,000 science prize
stories.summary: A young student from Connecticut is a finalist in a science competition for her innovative project. Her project proposes using algae and natural calcium buffers to reduce ocean acidification. This innovative idea could help protect vulnerable marine organisms from acidic conditions. She is competing for a substantial grand prize and valuable scientific mentorship. Her work highlights the significant contributions young minds can make to environmental solutions.

stories.title: Pacific trend raised US Southwest wildfire area 22%, cut Australia’s 19%

Conversely, it eased fire conditions in eastern Australia during the study. Researchers analyzed decades of wildfire and climate data for these findings. Understanding these ocean-climate links can improve future wildfire forecasts.

stories.title: Nearly 81 years after Hiroshima, scientists discover a hidden metal alloy created by the atomic bomb blast
stories.summary: Scientists found a new metallic alloy in Hiroshima shoreline sand. This alloy formed from extreme heat and rapid cooling during the 1945 atomic blast. Researchers identified its unique chemical makeup and crystal structure in microscopic particles. The discovery offers insights into matter behavior under extreme conditions. This finding could inspire future materials science research and nuclear forensics.
