stories.title: US scientists analysed 55 storm and atmospheric variables to identify hurricane rapid intensification
stories.summary: Coastal communities might soon benefit from enhanced hurricane forecasting. A groundbreaking statistical model predicts rapid hurricane intensification up to five days in advance, significantly improving early warnings. This innovation analyzes a multitude of environmental factors, allowing forecasters to anticipate dangerous storm developments with increased accuracy, ultimately safeguarding lives and property from unexpected hurricane threats.

stories.title: 'Cancel JPSC exam': Jharkhand students continue protest, seek CBI investigation
Israel, US military learnt Trump cancelled Iran strike through social media: Report
'2024 movement fooled Bangladesh': Taslima Nasreen's 'lesson' warning over Delhi student protests
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen believes Bangladesh's student movement misled people. She drew parallels between past protests and recent demonstrations in Delhi. Nasreen stated that Islamic fundamentalists were behind the Bangladesh movement. This experience reinforced her concerns about the consequences of such actions. The developments in Bangladesh should serve as a cautionary lesson for others.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham may exempt child sex offenders from early release scheme
Hungary shut its only nuclear plant for the first time in 44 years
stories.summary: Hungary's sole nuclear facility has been offline due to unprecedentedly low levels of the Danube River. This shutdown exacerbates power shortages amid a fierce summer heatwave, prompting the government to urge both households and businesses to conserve energy. Consequently, Hungary must depend on costly electricity imports from neighboring countries, highlighting the fragility of energy systems in the face of severe weather changes.

stories.title: 'Cruel terrorist act': Moscow mayor on restaurant blast that killed 3, injured 21
Brazilian scientists sampled 800 trees across 63 Amazon locations; their atomic fingerprinting...
stories.summary: Brazilian scientists are innovating with an isotopic mapping model designed to tackle illegal logging head-on. This novel forensic tool examines atomic signatures within trees, allowing them to trace the origination of timber effectively. Currently, the model can eliminate ninety-two percent of the Amazon rainforest from potential illegal wood sources, utilizing stable isotope analysis for secure chemical fingerprinting. The goal is to bolster law enforcement investigations and diminish global timber crime.

stories.title: Ex-nurse revives baby who stopped breathing during Arizona post-office visit
stories.summary: A former nurse's quick actions saved an infant's life at an Arizona post office. Mary Schwarz performed CPR and airway clearing on baby Nova who stopped breathing. Police Lieutenant Shari Aguilar then transported the infant to a nearby clinic for immediate medical attention. Nova, who had prior heart issues, began breathing again during the car ride. This incident highlights the critical importance of CPR training in everyday situations.

stories.title: 9,000 discarded Christmas trees help restore New Orleans wetlands
stories.summary: New Orleans is giving used Christmas trees a second life by dropping them into coastal marshes to help slow land loss. The bundled trees trap sediment, reduce wave energy and support marsh grass growth. Scientists say the method helps restore wetlands in selected areas but is only one part of Louisiana's broader coastal protection efforts.

stories.title: US general warns Pentagon he lacks naval assets to keep shielding Israel from missiles: Report
Ramlila body asks 'Ramayana' makers to hold special screening before release, warns of protests
stories.summary: The Shri Ramlila Mahasangh requested a special preview screening of the upcoming Ramayana film. This demand aims to prevent any scenes that might offend Hindu sentiments. The organization warned of protests if their preview request is not accepted. The film's trailer features Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana. Ramayana: Part 1 is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 release.

stories.title: Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
stories.summary: India's expanding higher education system produces millions of graduates annually. However, quality job creation has not kept pace with this educational growth. Many educated youth struggle to find stable, well-paying employment opportunities. This mismatch fuels widespread frustration and youth-led protests across the nation. The situation highlights a critical challenge for India's demographic dividend.

stories.title: Researchers mapped 128 million US buildings for landslide exposure; 6.5 million Americans live in...
stories.summary: A recent study identifies millions of Americans at risk from landslide hazards, revealing that densely populated eastern states have higher exposure. The challenges mount for rural communities when recovery from landslides is needed, contrasting with wealthier cities that implement zoning and engineering strategies to minimize risk. The findings stress the importance of increased public investment and disaster aid for rural areas facing these dangers.

stories.title: Wildfires near Bordeaux spark fears of hidden damage to France’s wine
stories.summary: France's worst wildfires in decades now threaten Bordeaux's famed wine production. Smoke taint can subtly damage grapes, affecting taste and value for years. This danger arrives during a sensitive ripening period for the grapes. The wine industry already faces market pressures and export challenges. Climate change poses ongoing threats to this vital agricultural sector.

stories.title: 6-7 and the First World War: How Internet absurdism became Dada's unlikely heir
'Not Korean heart ... counting fingers': Shehzad Poonawalla's swipe at Rahul Gandhi over Gen Z post
stories.summary: Shehzad Poonawalla criticised Rahul Gandhi's recent social media post. He interpreted Gandhi's gesture as counting corruption and bribes daily. Poonawalla accused the Gandhi family of extensive involvement in corruption. Rahul Gandhi had shared a Korean finger heart gesture on Friendship Day. This outreach aimed to connect with younger audiences on social media.

stories.title: In 1925, the world’s first motel opened in California with rooms for $1.25; after closing in 1991...
stories.summary: The iconic site of the world's first motel in San Luis Obispo is now on the market. With various redevelopment options available, buyers are encouraged to re-envision this historic property. Established in 1925 and ceasing operations in 1991, this site presents a unique opportunity to either preserve or transform a piece of hospitality history amidst the recent trend of revitalizing classic motels into boutique experiences.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "Change will not come if we wait for some other person or some other time. We are the ones..."
'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
Assam floods: 82 dead, 1.78 lakh affected as relief efforts intensify - key points
College students in US are choosing to live in retirement communities for affordable housing
stories.summary: College students in the US are moving into retirement communities, paying lower rent in exchange for volunteering with older residents. Supporters say the arrangement helps students find affordable housing while reducing loneliness for both generations and building meaningful relationships.

stories.title: Virginia students save family from lake during golf tryouts
stories.summary: Three Culpeper teenagers are heroes after rescuing a family whose kayaks overturned. They heard a splash and a child screaming, then immediately acted. The teens swam to the struggling family and brought them safely back to shore. Police and school officials praised their quick thinking and courage. Their actions highlight the importance of immediate response in water emergencies.

stories.title: You can make yourselves ‘luckier’: Science-backed tips to rewire your brain for luck
stories.summary: Cultivating a belief in your own luck can reshape your brain to recognize new opportunities. By documenting moments of serendipity, you start to see that luck is more frequent than originally believed. Individuals branded as unlucky often experience heightened anxiety, which narrows their perspective. In contrast, self-proclaimed lucky individuals expect good things and interact more openly. Ultimately, creating your own luck demands conscious choices and more frequent attempts.

stories.title: Bordeaux vineyards escaped the immediate wildfires, but repeated heatwaves are shrinking...
stories.summary: European vineyards face an early harvest due to prolonged heat and drought conditions. Wildfires across southwestern France and Greece have forced thousands to evacuate their homes. Emergency services continue to battle numerous blazes, particularly in Greece and on Crete. Spain sees some relief as national emergency declarations are lifted in certain areas. Record continent-wide warmth exacerbates fire risks and impacts air quality for millions.

stories.title: 'To end discrimination against women': Taslima Nasreen calls for UCC implementation in India, Bangladesh and Pakisatn
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen urged India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan to adopt a Uniform Civil Code. She stated this law is essential for eliminating discrimination, particularly against women. Nasreen highlighted that Hindu women in Bangladesh lack equal inheritance rights. She also expressed disappointment over disruptions at her felicitation ceremony. The author emphasized the importance of freedom of expression for all individuals.

stories.title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
Engineers linked two deep wells through 629°F rock beneath Oregon’s Newberry volcano; the experiment could unlock round-the-clock power without burning fuel
stories.summary: Mazama Energy connected two deep wells reaching 629 degrees Fahrenheit. This marks the world's hottest enhanced geothermal system ever built. The company plans three more wells in 2026 targeting hotter rock. This project aims to unlock superhot rock for cleaner energy production. Geothermal energy could become a significant player in the clean energy mix.

stories.title: Can BJP crack Punjab? Inside its strategy to challenge AAP and Congress in 2027
'Kerala stands united': Rahul Gandhi offers support as rains claim 8 lives, leave 8 missing
Teen's routine fishing trip ends with a South Dakota record that had stood since 1970
stories.summary: A routine fishing trip on South Dakota's Wall Lake turned into a record-breaking moment for teenager Jack Backman after he caught a one-pound pumpkinseed, setting a new state record. Thinking he had hooked a crappie, Backman was surprised to discover the rare catch. The fish beat a 12-ounce state record that had stood since 1970.

stories.title: 'Double standards': Pakistan rejects UN report on civilian casualties in Afghanistan strikes
Quote of the day by LeBron James: "I think the reason why I'm the person who I am today is because…" - an inspiring lesson on resilience, adversity and the power of difficult beginnings
stories.summary: LeBron James credits his difficult childhood for shaping his current character and perspective. He views past hardships as the essential foundation for his achievements. These challenging experiences fostered patience, gratitude, and determination within him. His journey demonstrates that starting circumstances do not permanently define one's future. Real success often carries a responsibility to help others facing similar struggles.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Indonesia ferry fire kills 5, rescue teams recover Nirmal Purja's body & more
'If India is so great, why settle in Dubai?' Raj Thackeray targets Vivek Oberoi, R Madhavan
Students from around the world experience the Jain way of life in Rajasthan
'Ready to face death': Pappu Yadav defiant after FIR over Ram Temple donation 'theft' skit
stories.summary: Pappu Yadav remains defiant after police filed a case against him and other opposition leaders. The FIR stems from a Parliament skit which depicted alleged theft of Ram Temple donations. Yadav stated he is ready to face death to protect people's faith and religious sentiments. Varanasi Police registered the case following a complaint by a religious leader. Another complaint was filed against the MP in the national capital.

stories.title: California vineyards used owl boxes to attract barn owls, reducing rodent numbers by up to 52%
stories.summary: A new study from California has found that barn owls help vineyards control rodents naturally by both hunting them and making them more cautious. Researchers observed up to 52% fewer rodents in vineyards with more owls. The findings suggest that encouraging barn owls through nest boxes could reduce the need for pesticides while supporting biodiversity and sustainable farming.

stories.title: 'That hurts us': CWG silver medalist Lovlina flags 'missing' Northeast on Glasgow restaurant's India map
The towel on the chair: How it became India's ultimate status symbol
158 exam irregularity cases await trial; CBI seeks fast-track disposal under new anti-paper leak law
stories.summary: Over 150 recruitment exam irregularity cases await trial, some dating back two decades. The CBI will ask high courts to move these pending matters to new fast-track courts. Dedicated prosecutors and resources will be provided to expedite the conclusion of these trials. The new anti-paper leak law mandates day-to-day hearings and trials within three months. This initiative follows recent student protests and calls for examination system reforms.

stories.title: 'Mekedatu project is permanent solution': Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar on Cauvery water dispute with Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar views the Mekedatu dam project as a permanent solution. He stated the Supreme Court and central government have already responded to the proposal. Shivakumar urged all stakeholders to move forward without further delays or wasting time. This project aims to bring both states to the table for amicable discussions. The Cauvery water dispute centers on sharing river waters during periods of low rainfall.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Selena Gomez: You have to be uncomfortable sometimes in order to move forward
stories.summary: Selena Gomez, the renowned pop artist, champions the idea that navigating discomfort can be crucial for personal evolution. Transitioning from her Disney roots, she successfully emerged as a singer, actress, and entrepreneur. With transparency about her mental health battles, Gomez inspires others to seek professional support. Through her Rare Beauty brand, she also promotes mental wellness initiatives worldwide, illustrating that challenges often pave the way for growth.

stories.title: King Charles, Prince William pay tribute to ex-British soldier Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche
5 dead, 41 missing after ferry catches fire off Indonesia's Madura Island
'He will not be taken back': Mayawati expels former MP Ashok Siddharth from BSP again
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party president Mayawati expelled former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddarth from the party. Siddarth faced expulsion for indiscipline and violating party directives in several states. The party chief also announced the expulsion of coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal for similar reasons. Mayawati clarified that senior Uttar Pradesh office-bearers would not hold state roles. Ramji Gautam will continue as Punjab in-charge until upcoming assembly and Lok Sabha polls.

stories.title: 150-year-overdue library book returned in Australia; racks up Rs 16 lakh 'late fee'
stories.summary: A library received a book returned after 150 years overdue. The calculated late fee reached approximately twenty-eight thousand Australian dollars. This rare book was discovered during home renovations and was damaged. It was borrowed by a local resident's great-great-grandfather in the 1870s. The book will now join the library's local history collection.

stories.title: 'Police powers misused': Prashant Kishor alleges voter intimidation, files complaint over Bankipur bypoll
'Still a student, learning every day': Rahul Gandhi's Gen Z-style Friendship Day wish
Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs at 1st embassy outreach
stories.summary: Indian diaspora members voiced concerns over anti-India content and visa issues. Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami assured actions were being taken to address these matters. Visa requirements for Chinese citizens traveling to India will be eased soon. The embassy plans to establish a legal assistance framework for professionals. Cultural outreach programs will also be expanded to promote Indian diversity.

stories.title: 'Govt forgets when donations are stolen': Congress defends Rahul Gandhi after Ram Mandir skit FIR
How being poor damages your brain, new study finds
stories.summary: Long-term financial strain can significantly speed up the aging of the brain. Research highlights that persistent monetary worries contribute to cognitive decline, particularly noticeable by the age of fifty-three. Brain scans portray more severe shrinkage in individuals facing such hardships, with men from lower socioeconomic backgrounds suffering even harsher effects. Providing support for those in financial distress could play a vital role in preserving cognitive health in the future.

stories.title: Delhi HC transfers special judge assigned to paper leak cases a week after taking charge
'Drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan to hurt India': PM Modi during 'Nasha Mukt Yuva' launch - top quotes
Study warns Northern Hemisphere lakes could lose around 40 days of winter ice by 2100
stories.summary: A new international study has found that lake ice across the Northern Hemisphere could shrink by about 40 days by the end of this century if emissions remain high. Researchers identified critical winter temperature thresholds beyond which ice loss accelerates sharply, raising concerns over water quality, freshwater ecosystems and communities that depend on stable winter ice.

stories.title: 100-million-year-old ichthyosaur's last meal found; bite marks implicate giant Kronosaurus
stories.summary: A remarkable ichthyosaur fossil, hailing from 100 million years ago, has provided a glimpse into its final feast, which included fish, cephalopods, and even a pterosaur. Using sophisticated scanning methods, scientists could identify these stomach contents non-invasively. Notably, the fossil bears evidence of severe bite marks, implicating the Kronosaurus queenslandicus as the likely predator, illuminating aspects of Australia’s ancient marine food web.

stories.title: How an escaped aquarium plant unleashed California's killer algae in 2000
'Let Cauvery unite our people': Karnataka BJP chief calls on Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to bridge 'differences'
'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
Culture can slow ageing, says study
Global breastfeeding rates rise, India yet to arrest decline
Japan earthquake aftermath: Woman dies of heat stroke in parked car; toll rises to 36
stories.summary: An elderly woman died from heat stroke while sheltering in her car after a massive earthquake. Authorities are warning of growing heat-related risks for evacuees amid sweltering temperatures. Thousands remain displaced, with many sleeping in cars or outside their homes for privacy. Temperatures are climbing, raising fears of further heat-related illnesses among survivors. The government is rushing essential supplies to evacuation centers to improve living conditions.

stories.title: Washington wildfires scorch over 2,50,000 acres of land; trigger mass evacuations
stories.summary: Thousands of firefighters battled multiple wildfires across Washington state on Saturday. Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and imposed a burn ban. The fast-moving Old Trails Fire in Spokane threatened thousands of structures and forced evacuations. Power utility Avista implemented safety shutoffs, leaving many customers without electricity. Officials confirmed some structures were destroyed as the extent of damage was assessed.

stories.title: 'Rs 18cr stolen every year': Raj Thackeray alleges Siddhivinayak temple donation scam
3 killed in US Idaho shopping area shooting; gunman among dead
stories.summary: Three people died and two were injured after a gunman opened fire. The shooter was also among the deceased, with authorities investigating the motive. The chaotic scene unfolded near a busy In-N-Out Burger restaurant on Saturday afternoon. Witnesses described seeing an armed individual and people fleeing the area in fear. Law enforcement confirmed the threat to the community was over after the incident.

stories.title: Long hours hurting resident docs’ mental health, NMC tells SC
stories.summary: Resident doctors face significant psychological distress from long working hours. The National Medical Commission acknowledged these demanding schedules impact their health. The commission stated reasonable working hours are essential for doctor and patient wellbeing. However, NMC expressed inability to enforce this, citing health authorities' domain. A doctors' group highlighted rising suicide cases due to these conditions.

stories.title: Railway Board panels suggest premature retirement of 5 officers
stories.summary: Railway Board committees recommended premature retirement for five Group A officers. This action targets corruption, lack of integrity, and inefficiency within the service. Two senior administrative grade officers and three junior administrative grade officers were affected. These decisions were made under the Indian Railway Establishment Code provisions. Previously, thirty-two officers were retired in 2022 for similar reasons.

stories.title: CBI files EPFO cheating case against Anil Ambani
stories.summary: The CBI has filed a cheating case against Reliance Capital and Anil Ambani. This action stems from an alleged Rs 1,816 crore loss to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation. EPFO invested Rs 2,500 crore in Reliance Capital’s debentures which later defaulted. While the issue was settled earlier, ED findings prompted a new fraud case. Anil Ambani denies any wrongdoing in this matter.

stories.title: E20: AAP plans pro-choice rally to PM residence
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal announced a march to the Prime Minister's residence on Tuesday. He demanded consumers have a choice between pure petrol and E20 fuel. Kejriwal also called for E20 fuel to be priced lower than pure petrol. He challenged the government to release scientific studies supporting the E20 fuel policy. The AAP leader advised consumers to consider electric vehicles for future transportation needs.

stories.title: Monsoon hope as WMO sees an El Niño counter
stories.summary: India faces a risk of below-normal monsoon rainfall due to El Niño. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole may offer some relief to the country. This oceanic pattern could improve rainfall conditions in southern India. It might prevent the monsoon from slipping into a deficient phase. International forecasts suggest a positive IOD could develop soon.

stories.title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
stories.summary: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan questioned the Supreme Court collegium's lack of transparency in judicial appointments. He noted that recent collegium resolutions provided no reasons for their decisions. This opacity, he argued, could allow unsuitable individuals to enter the judiciary. Citizens possess a right to know deliberations concerning judicial elevations and transfers. The JALDI report highlights varying transparency levels across India's higher courts.

stories.title: July GST collections up 15.4% to Rs 2.1 L cr on higher imports
stories.summary: Goods and Services Tax collections rose 15.4 percent to Rs 2,11,205 crore in July. This increase was largely due to a 29 percent jump in integrated GST on imports. Strong economic activity and higher commodity prices also contributed to the robust tax collections. Central GST mop-up increased 12.3 percent while state GST grew 8.7 percent. Net collections after refunds went up 15.8 percent, reflecting continued economic resilience.

stories.title: Government approves 2 tunnels for Valley-Jammu connectivity
Indian-origin mayor of US city asks ICE to 'go home', says he will always support the immigrant community
India-China border trade resumes after 6 years
stories.summary: India and China have reopened two key Himalayan trade routes after six years. Traditional border trade resumed Saturday through Lipulekh and Shipki La passes. Chinese authorities restricted the initial batch of traders to twenty people. Indian traders can export 36 categories of goods, while Chinese traders bring twenty. A new trade mart was also inaugurated near the international border.

stories.title: NEET-PG aspirants to face Aadhaar, iris authentication
Twitch streamer ExtraEmily gets her own Hulu and Disney+ series as Creator Essentials brings her Twitch content to TV
stories.summary: Twitch streamer ExtraEmily is launching her own television series titled Creator Essentials. This new show features fifteen episodes, each approximately twenty-two minutes long. The series is designed for teenagers and highlights her personality and gaming adventures. This move expands her reach beyond Twitch to major streaming services. It signifies a growing trend of online creators transitioning to television.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Sigmund Freud: 'The more perfect a person is on the outside, the more demons they have on the inside' and why absolute perfection is a facade
Quote of the day by Mohammed bin Salman: 'I fear that the day I die, I am going to die without accomplishing what I have in my mind'
Twitch streamer SmaK reveals Twitch apologized after sudden 30-day ban over joke as creators criticize the platform’s automated ban system
stories.summary: Twitch streamer SmaK received a thirty-day ban after making a joke during a livestream. He was joking about needing to go away while reacting to chat messages. Twitch later removed the ban and apologized for the mistaken suspension. This incident highlights issues with automated moderation systems and context. SmaK has since returned to streaming after the platform corrected its error.

stories.title: Florida evangelist who says passengers have no choice but to listen to her sermons removed from flight; Alaska Airlines puts her on no-fly list
Cloudburst damages structures in Kishtwar; rain halts Amarnath Yatra
stories.summary: Flash floods in Kishtwar's Chatroo area damaged shops and houses early Saturday. Vehicles were washed away, and the national highway sustained damage from debris. The Amarnath Yatra was suspended from Jammu due to incessant rain. Schools remained closed in several districts as a precautionary measure. Affected shopkeepers and business owners will receive government compensation.

stories.title: Fear stalks Kashmir’s brick kilns after terrorists kill 2 migrant workers
stories.summary: Two migrant labourers were killed Friday evening in Kulgam, causing panic among workers. Brick kilns across south Kashmir halted operations as labourers stayed indoors. Many workers expressed concerns about their safety and earning a living. Security forces visited the kilns and assured the labourers of protection. Officials directed authorities to ensure the safety of all migrant workers.

stories.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani snubbed at funeral of soldier killed in Iranian missile strike: Report
Green Card updates for August: EB-1 may become unavailable for Indians
'Prepare to depart': US embassies issue alert across Middle East amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: US embassies in Middle East urged citizens to depart due to potential conflict escalation. The security alerts warned of unpredictable Iranian actions and possible attacks on US interests. President Trump threatened Iran with severe military action following alleged truce violations. Iran warned countries supporting the US against facing war's flames. Regional shipping and travel face disruptions amid ongoing hostilities and heightened tensions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia arrests over 14,000 in week-long crackdown on residency, labour violations
NEET-PG 2026 gets major overhaul: Centres closer to home, single-shift exam, fewer questions with no change in test duration
stories.summary: NEET-PG exam sees significant changes for candidate convenience and enhanced security. Candidates now select three preferred states for their examination centre locations. The exam duration remains the same, but questions reduce to 180 for more time. Aadhaar and iris biometrics strengthen registration and exam day security measures. NEET-PG 2026 will be conducted in a single shift for uniform assessment.

stories.title: 'Girls' clothes torn, heads broken': CJP founder demands PM Modi apology over police action on July 20th
Army's intelligence units, Rajasthan police bust counterfeit combat uniform racket in Sriganganagar
stories.summary: Indian Army intelligence and Rajasthan police seized nearly 1,000 meters of unauthorized combat cloth. This action followed a lead pointing to a local firm supplying counterfeit army-pattern fabric. The coordinated operation on July 30 uncovered a wider network distributing fake military uniforms. Similar counterfeit cloth was previously seized in Bareilly, traced to Sriganganagar. Unauthorized sale of military camouflage cloth is restricted and banned in many sensitive regions.

stories.title: 'You should've apologized': Congress targets PM Modi over his 'forgive you' remark in Insta video
stories.summary: In a bold move, Congress leader Supriya Shrinate has taken aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding he apologize for the alleged brutal treatment of students during recent protests. She accused the government of cruelty and called for accountability, urging the Prime Minister to step into Parliament and address the issue directly, particularly after his comments about supporting the youth.

stories.title: 13-year-old Oregon student designs a chamber that turns moisture in the air into water for drought-hit farms
stories.summary: In a remarkable feat of ingenuity, a young student has created technology that converts air moisture into potable water. This device stands as a sustainable beacon for farmers struggling with inadequate water supply. Featuring a Peltier module for condensation, it smartly monitors water delivery and environmental factors through advanced sensors. Roy Kim aspires for his invention to play a significant role in alleviating the global water challenges faced by agriculture.

stories.title: Mushroom hunters find rare snake nest in Nepal forest, officials restrict access
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott: “There are lots of resources each of us can pull from our safes to share with others…”
‘My return to Kolkata proves injustice cannot be permanent’: Taslima Nasreen
stories.summary: Exiled author Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata after nineteen years of absence. She stated her return proves injustice is not permanent and spoke for women's rights. Nasreen expressed concern over rising religious extremism in Bangladesh and curtailed freedom of speech. She lamented not finding a permanent home in the Bengals, though Europe offered security. The writer emphasized her advocacy for equality and human rights, not offense.

stories.title: Wife not entitled to interim maintenance if adultery allegation is prima facie true: SC
Trump rejects Iran link in Minnesota cyberattacks, blames Governor Tim Walz instead
Savannah Guthrie begs public after mother's disappearance; ransom note said 'buried in nature'
DMK moves SC seeking immediate release of Cauvery water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: The DMK has petitioned the Supreme Court for immediate Cauvery water release from Karnataka. Karnataka's government faces a directive to release 3,500 cusecs daily for fifteen days. The plea also seeks to clear an accumulated water release shortfall of 9.46 TMC. Karnataka's Chief Minister urged protesters to withdraw their agitation against water releases. The state government will protect farmers' interests while respecting judicial orders.

stories.title: ‘Egg-therapy could turn on its head’: Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya cautions party workers
stories.summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya cautioned party workers against arrogance and complacency. He warned that the "egg therapy" could turn against them if they become overconfident. Bhattacharya acknowledged that extortion culture has not been fully eradicated since the government took power. He emphasized the need to free the business ecosystem from partisan politics. The party is making earnest efforts to build a government for West Bengal.

stories.title: 'Returned to the US 3 days before visa expiry': Indian H-1B holder shares what happened next
CBI books Anil Ambani, Reliance Capital in Rs 1,816 crore EPFO fraud case
West Bengal to clear all pending CAA applications within six months, says Suvendu Adhikari
stories.summary: West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari pledged to resolve all pending CAA applications soon. He stated the law grants citizenship and is not meant to revoke it. Nearly twenty-four thousand citizenship certificates have already been issued to eligible refugees. The government will delegate powers to district magistrates for faster application processing. This initiative aims to provide citizenship to persecuted minorities from neighboring countries.

stories.title: UK finance minister John Healey to present first Budget on October 28
2,000-pound US bomb hits Iran family home; Centcom says 'we never target civilians'
India’s students do not need PM Modi's forgiveness, they are owed his apology: Rahul Gandhi
Ladakh Police file zero FIR against influencer over alleged anti-Amit Shah Facebook video
'Days of threat culture over': Bengal CM assures security to Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen
'Disappointed with PM Modi': Shehzad Poonawalla’s sarcastic 'dictator' jibe at oppn after quitting BJP
stories.summary: Taking a jibe at PM Modi's critics, Shehzad Poonawalla expressed "disappointment" with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership style. He sarcastically suggested Modi learn dictatorship from past Congress leaders. Poonawalla cited Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru as examples of strong rule. He also mentioned past Congress governments' actions during protests. The former spokesperson concluded Modi had not met Left-liberal expectations.

stories.title: Major row over airport detention of Johns Hopkins health researcher Fatima Ameaka; Colleagues say she is brilliant but DHS says she is an 'illegal'
Spain races to secure Ceuta border with floating barrier after mass crossings and 67 deaths
PM Modi inaugurates Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre in Mysuru
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Viveka Smaraka youth centre in Mysuru. This centre aims to inspire young Indians with nation-building and service ideals. The Prime Minister highlighted youth strength driving India's economic growth and development. He also emphasized education in mother tongue and promoting local products. The new facility will nurture youth dedicated to national service and societal welfare.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja dies in avalanche; India's medal rush continues in CWG 2026 & more
stories.summary: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja died in a Broad Peak avalanche, ending his legendary career. India secured more medals at the Commonwealth Games 2026, reaching a total of thirty. Rahul Gandhi demanded an apology from Prime Minister Modi for NEET students. A stricter anti-paper leak law has now come into force nationwide. Complaints were filed against Rahul Gandhi and Pappu Yadav regarding a protest.

stories.title: ‘How did Hockey India executive board not know?’ Congress questions govt over saffron jersey row
stories.summary: Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge questioned the government regarding the hockey jersey color change. He stated the decision was made without Hockey India Executive Board approval. The traditional blue jersey identity is deeply connected to Indian sports traditions. Hockey India defended the design, citing consultations with players and staff. However, the president claimed no prior knowledge of the implemented decision.

stories.title: Innocent Canadian man spent 18 months in prison after police missed underscore in username
Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
'Defeat delimitation': In Tamil Nadu, Rahul Gandhi's appeal to parties with 'Ettappan' warning
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi labeled the proposed delimitation exercise a BJP conspiracy. He stated it aims to disenfranchise people and reduce Tamil Nadu's political power. Supporting delimitation makes one a 21st-century Ettappan, a Tamil term for traitor. He urged all Tamil people and parties to oppose this proposal. National parties were also asked to defeat the delimitation in the House.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr.: "Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only ..."
Antarctica's Concordia Station hit minus 119.4°F, its coldest temperature in 16 years
stories.summary: Antarctica's Concordia Research Station recorded its coldest temperature in sixteen years on July eighteenth. This extreme cold was caused by polar winter and high elevation conditions. The station sits atop the East Antarctic Plateau, far from ocean influences. Meteorologists attribute the deep freeze to a persistent high-pressure system. Such measurements offer valuable insights into Earth's climate system.

stories.title: Clavicular US college tour: Everything to know about the Kick streamer’s US livestream event
stories.summary: Clavicular is set to begin his US College Tour on August 2, 2026, where he plans to livestream visits to colleges and fraternities across America. His announcement has received mixed reactions online, while many fans also remember his viral Arizona State University selfie that became a popular internet meme earlier this year.

stories.title: Air India expands Canada network with new Mumbai-Toronto flights, upgrades Delhi route
'Not met a single parent or student': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi over 'forgiving' students video
How 832 solar panels help one farm produce food, energy and extra income
Explained: What changes after India's tougher anti-paper leak law comes into force
stories.summary: A new anti-paper leak law is now in effect across India. Investigations into exam fraud must now conclude within two months. Trials will be expedited through fast-track courts, aiming for quicker resolutions. Individuals face up to ten years imprisonment and significant fines for paper leaks. Organized rackets will receive even harsher penalties, deterring future examination malpractices.

stories.title: Students don’t need PM Modi’s forgiveness; they deserve his apology: Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: He criticised the Prime Minister for not meeting a single grieving parent or a student whose future was stolen by a leaked question paper. He said the Centre had failed to acknowledge the suffering of students and their families.

stories.title: ‘Act of aggression against Iran’: Araghchi warns UK over US access to British military bases
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister warned Britain that allowing US strikes from its bases is aggression. He stated this action grants Iran the right to self-defense under international law. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham approved continued US military base access for operations. Burnham also reaffirmed UK commitment to maritime security efforts in the Strait of Hormuz. London maintains it is not part of any war with Iran and supports diplomacy.

stories.title: Rose Metcalf helped guide 400 people off the sinking Costa Concordia, signalled rescuers with her earring
stories.summary: In a dramatic turn of events aboard the Costa Concordia, Rose Metcalf, a dancer, played a pivotal role in the life-saving efforts. She rallied crew members to create a human chain, ensuring safe evacuation amidst panic. Innovatively, Metcalf descended the ship's side to reach the water's edge and signaled a rescue helicopter with a makeshift light. Her courage and resourcefulness were instrumental in saving lives during that dire night.

stories.title: 'Honey trap' angle emerges in Bengal Jaish probe; woman arrested from Jharkhand
‘Sentiments hurt’: Seers, lawyers file police complaints against Pappu Yadav, Rahul Gandhi over Ram Temple skit
stories.summary: Seers and lawyers filed police complaints in Varanasi against Pappu Yadav and opposition leaders. They alleged their religious sentiments were hurt by a protest enacted in Parliament. The opposition leaders staged a symbolic protest over alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement. This protest occurred after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced regarding temple donations. Legal action has been sought against the opposition leaders involved in the demonstration.

stories.title: Ram Temple skit row: Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav, Awadhesh Prasad booked for 'insulting Sanatan Dharma'
stories.summary: Seers and lawyers filed police complaints in Varanasi against Pappu Yadav and opposition leaders. They alleged their religious sentiments were hurt by a protest enacted in Parliament. The opposition leaders staged a symbolic protest over alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement. This protest occurred after allegations of financial irregularities surfaced regarding temple donations. Legal action has been sought against the opposition leaders involved in the demonstration.

'Go that way': Migrants say Moroccan authorities directed them towards Spain's Ceuta
stories.summary: Moroccan illegal migrants reported encouragement from authorities and social media messages. Thousands crossed into Spain's Ceuta enclave, with many returning due to hardship. At least sixty-seven people died during the unprecedented border crossing event. Spain is reinforcing the Ceuta border after tens of thousands entered. The crisis has sparked political tensions and renewed migration policy debates.

stories.title: His grandfather paid $2,200 for an Allis-Chalmers tractor in 1953; 62 years later, Kevin Klahn bought it back and restored it
stories.summary: Kevin Klahn restored his grandfather's 1953 tractor after buying it back. This vintage Allis-Chalmers WD tractor became a symbol of family heritage. The meticulous restoration project took many hours of dedicated work. It preserved the machine's original character and historical significance. The tractor returned home, representing dedication and enduring family bonds.

stories.title: Major US Black university mandates business suits, bans certain headwear in new dress code
US makes visa bond programme permanent: Effective date, affected countries explained
'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised NSA Ajit Doval's significant national security contributions. Doval's strategic advice has strengthened India's defense and foreign policy since 2014. Shah highlighted Doval's instrumental role in every major national security decision made by Prime Minister Modi. The NSA's decades-long career in intelligence has been vital for India's transformation. Doval accepted the Lokmanya Tilak National Award with humility, thanking leaders.

stories.title: 'Almost as if I am a terrorist': Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest over E20 protest
'Terrorists asked caste, community': Family claims Kulgam victims were 'identified' before being shot
stories.summary: Two Chhattisgarh labourers were killed in a terror attack at a brick kiln in Kulgam. Attackers allegedly questioned the victims about their caste and community before opening fire on them. This incident echoes survivor accounts from a previous terror attack in Pahalgam. The victims were identified as Deepak Ratrey and Bhupendra Bhaina from Chhattisgarh. Authorities are coordinating to return the bodies and provide financial assistance to the families.

stories.title: 'Whenever we seek statehood': Farooq Abdullah questions 'timing' of Kulgam terror attack
stories.summary: Two migrant labourers were killed in a terrorist attack in Kulgam district. National Conference president Farooq Abdullah questioned the timing of this incident. He noted such attacks occur when his party demands statehood restoration. People's Democratic Party chief Mehbooba Mufti called the killings a security lapse. She requested a high-level investigation and compensation for the victims.

stories.title: 'Will march to PM's residence over E20': Kejriwal announces August 3 protest

Sunken German warship from WWII resurfaces due to low river levels in Serbia
President Murmu assents to anti-paper leak amendment Bill
Minnesota's largest coal plant is now wiring 1.7 million solar panels powering 150,000 homes
stories.summary: The largest coal plant in Minnesota is transitioning to embrace renewable energy by hosting a substantial solar farm. Leveraging the existing transmission systems of the coal facility, the Sherco Solar project is now recognized as the most extensive solar installation in the state. This forward-thinking initiative accelerates grid connection for new energy innovations, with exciting plans for future development and battery storage integration.

stories.title: NSA Ajit Doval receives Lokmanya Tilak National Award for national security contribution
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah presented the award at a ceremony held on the 106th death anniversary of freedom fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak. The event took place at the Kataria High School ground in Mukundnagar and was attended by Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, deputy chief ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, along with several senior political leaders and dignitaries.

stories.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke falls sick again while meeting people in building parking
stories.summary: According to those present, he suddenly felt unwell and moved to the rear of the building, where he vomited. He later returned upstairs to his residence without speaking to the media. Confirming the incident, Dipke's father, Bhagwan Dipke, said doctors had been called to examine his son. Dipke had disclosed on July 25, during the protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, that he had been diagnosed with typhoid.

stories.title: More tests, less health: Why India might be testing itself sick
2,000-year-old grapevines in Ethiopia may preserve an ancient farming legacy
J&K CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 10 lakh aid after Kulgam terror attack kills two labourers
'Airports were earlier named after one family': PM Modi inaugurates Andhra's Bhogapuram airport
'Forgiveness only on reel or will you withdraw cases?': Abhijeet Dipke comments on PM Modi's late night video
'Enjoys playing victim card': Congress attacks PM Modi's 'forgive youth' remark
FSSAI cracks down on three firms over food safety violations
stories.summary: FSSAI recalls raisins over excessive pesticide residues, suspends a nutraceutical licence and bans folinic acid syrup over misleading claims.

stories.title: 'Same people who litter here, use dustbin abroad': Bombay HC on civic sense
stories.summary: A bench of Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground in Mumbai. The judges said public participation was essential to keeping the city clean and urged civic authorities to enforce the rules without hesitation.

stories.title: First J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months: Two Chhattisgarh labourers die after being shot
stories.summary: One of the labourers, identified as Deepak Ratray, died before he could be shifted to a hospital. The second victim, Bopinder, was initially admitted to Government Medical College (GMC) Anantnag before being referred to SKIMS Hospital in Soura, where he later succumbed to his injuries. Officials said both victims were in their twenties and had travelled from Chhattisgarh in search of work.

stories.title: Spain says most migrants have returned to Morocco after deadly border rush
stories.summary: Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.

stories.title: India screens nearly 11,000 travellers after Ebola emergency, no case detected
stories.summary: India has screened over ten thousand international travellers from Ebola-affected nations. No Ebola cases have been detected in the country so far, officials confirmed. Enhanced screening and preparedness measures were implemented across all entry points. Mumbai and Delhi airports saw the highest numbers of screened passengers. The government continues to strengthen surveillance and public awareness campaigns.

stories.title: Suspected Ebola case in Delhi: BSF constable from Congo mission admitted to RML, sample sent for testing
stories.summary: A BSF constable returning from Congo developed fever during quarantine. He was admitted to an isolation ward at RML Hospital for surveillance. His blood sample was sent for confirmatory testing to NIV Pune. Health authorities are monitoring the situation closely while awaiting test results. The case remains suspected, and Ebola infection has not been confirmed.

stories.title: This 44-year-old Swedish man survived being buried beneath a metre of snow for nearly two months against all odds
Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
stories.summary: India's monsoon rainfall is expected to be below normal during August and September. This forecast is influenced by the continuing risk of El Niño, which often weakens the monsoon. July rainfall, however, turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. These showers helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit significantly by the end of July.

stories.title: 16.4% deleted in Haryana draft roll; 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Draft voter rolls in Haryana and Andhra Pradesh reveal significant exclusions. Over sixteen percent of Haryana's electorate and over ten percent in Andhra were removed. Reasons cited include deaths, permanent shifts, and multiple registrations. However, genuine voters can still be added during the claims period. This process allows for corrections and additions to the electoral rolls.

stories.title: PM Modi: I forgive those who abused me & my mother, our job to guide them
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will forgive young protesters accused of abuse. He stated these misguided children need guidance and correction, not punishment. The Prime Minister believes punishing them will not change circumstances effectively. Mistakes made at a young age present an opportunity for correction and societal acceptance. This decision indicates that cases against these youngsters will likely be withdrawn.

stories.title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
stories.summary: A Delhi court sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment. They were convicted for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma. The court found Sharma was lynched solely on account of his religion during the 2020 riots. While the prosecution sought the death penalty, it was declined by the judge. The judge considered educational backgrounds as a mitigating factor for the convicts.

stories.title: Amid opposition protest, Lok Sabha passes births & deaths bill
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, without any debate. Opposition members disrupted Rajya Sabha proceedings, preventing any business from being transacted. The bill aims to make delayed registrations of births and deaths more stringent. Congress and SP MPs raised issues concerning police actions and alleged temple donation theft. The Rajya Sabha was ultimately adjourned for the entire day.

stories.title: India flags POJK at world stage
Floating solar plants get Rs 5,000cr push
Govt extends PM-Kisan yojana
Samudra Manthan gets Cabinet nod
Reaction teams to flag 'fake info' on E20 blending
Ethanol kept petrol prices lower: Govt
stories.summary: Ethanol blending saved consumers nearly thirty rupees per litre on petrol. Global crude prices reached one hundred thirty-five dollars a barrel recently. The government kept fuel prices unchanged for seventy-five days initially. E20 petrol now costs one hundred two rupees per litre in Delhi. Allegations of foodgrain diversion for ethanol were also rejected.

stories.title: Senthil Balaji gets pre-arrest bail from SC in Tasmac corruption case

Kick streamer Clavicular says Kick spent nearly $700K promoting his clips and gives creators an unlimited clipping budget
stories.summary: Kick streamer Clavicular revealed the platform funded his viral clip promotions. He stated Kick spent nearly $700,000 in one month for this purpose. This strategy aimed to attract new users to the Kick streaming service. Clavicular believes his content and lifestyle appeal contributed to his rapid growth. Kick's investment highlights a new trend in platform-driven creator promotion.

Quote of the day by Daisaku Ikeda: 'A peaceful life does not mean a life free of toil and suffering' and the true meaning of happiness
SC slaps Rs 1 lakh fine on Rajasthan government for harassing official
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered Rajasthan to pay one lakh rupees to a government official. This payment is compensation for harassment caused by political interference in a prosecution sanction. The court criticized the joint secretary of the former chief minister for undue influence. Such interference was deemed a blatant display of political dictate by the state. The official was unnecessarily dragged to court, prompting the court's strong observations.

stories.title: Quote by Masashi Kishimoto: 'The difference between insanity and genius is measured only by...'
stories.summary: Masashi Kishimoto's narrative of Naruto brilliantly illustrates that success can redefine our understanding of genius. Initially daring concepts are frequently brushed aside until they garner widespread acclaim. This phenomenon, known as outcome bias, skews our judgment, prioritizing results over the initial creative thought. A historical example can be found in Thomas Edison's light bulb, which marked a shift in societal perception.

stories.title: PM Modi, Burnham discuss trade pact in 1st call
Cabinet eases captive waterfront norms to spur private investment
stories.summary: The Cabinet approved a revised shipping ministry policy for captive waterfronts. This aims to accelerate private investment and provide greater operational certainty. Existing captive users can develop additional facilities to meet enhanced requirements. Government entities can obtain waterfronts on a nomination basis without competitive bidding. The policy extends concession periods and strengthens infrastructure development at major ports.

stories.title: YouTuber Hank Green faces backlash after admitting AI use in research for Ask Hank Anything episode
stories.summary: YouTuber Hank Green admitted using AI for research, sparking viewer criticism and trust concerns. He apologized for over-reliance on AI due to heavy work pressure. Green clarified AI did not write his scripts or form his opinions. This incident has prompted a broader discussion on AI's role in educational content. Viewers now await Green's efforts to rebuild trust through future work.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Archimedes: 'Give me a place to stand, a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I shall move the World', and how to find your own fulcrum
Cabinet approved two major tunnel projects in J&K
stories.summary: The Cabinet approved two strategic tunnel projects in Jammu and Kashmir. These projects will provide all-weather connectivity between the Kashmir Valley and Jammu. The tunnels will bypass difficult stretches of NH-244 affected by adverse weather conditions. Improved road infrastructure will boost regional connectivity and economic activity. These projects are fully Centre-funded and will be completed in five years.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Osamu Dazai: 'I could believe in hell, but it was impossible for me to believe...'
stories.summary: In 'No Longer Human,' Osamu Dazai presents a poignant exploration of suffering that vividly unravels the often inaccessible nature of happiness. The novel dives deep into feelings of despair, alienation, and loneliness, illustrating the stark realities echoed in modern psychology regarding depressive thought patterns. Its ongoing relevance speaks to a universal condition of isolation that resonates across generations, securing its place in literary discussions.

stories.title: J&K: Properties of 11 Pak-based terrorist handlers attached in Ramban
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police attached properties of eleven Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Ramban district. These assets, valued at approximately Rs 90.7 lakh, were seized to prevent terror financing activities. Credible evidence established the accused were operating as handlers from across the border. This action is part of ongoing efforts to dismantle cross-border terror networks. Similar property attachments were carried out in Reasi and Ramban districts recently.

stories.title: Chhattisgarh worker shot dead, another wounded in first J&K terror attack on migrants in 21 months
stories.summary: Terrorists shot dead a 24-year-old labourer from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam. Another worker from the same state was critically wounded in the attack. Security forces have launched operations to trace the attackers responsible for this incident. This incident marks the first fatal attack on migrant workers since October 18. Officials condemned the attack and directed security forces to intensify operations.

stories.title: 'Abuses never solve anything': PM Modi posts late night video amid row over Noida woman's remarks
South Africa released 11 formerly captive elephants onto wild reserves; five years later...
stories.summary: In an inspiring study, South African elephants reintroduced into reserves demonstrated remarkable behavior akin to that of free-roaming herds. Researchers observed that these elephants not only adapted seamlessly to their natural habitats but also maintained optimal stress hormone levels. This research underscores the potential for long-term captive elephants to regain their independence, offering a promising outlook for the conservation efforts throughout southern Africa.

stories.title: Singapore student left home saying she was going to college; hours later her family found her...
stories.summary: A Singaporean student, Siti Aishah Siregar, disappeared after telling her family she was going to college. Her family discovered her passport missing and a flight ticket to Cambodia in her email. Singapore police confirmed the 20-year-old had already departed the country on an outbound flight. Her father issued an emotional appeal on Facebook for assistance to locate his daughter.

stories.title: Indian woman slammed for showing off 'Green Card in just 2 months': 'They are not even hiding it anymore'
Meet Quazeem Tiamiyu, a student who turned discarded wood into insulation for beverage coolers
stories.summary: Quazeem Tiamiyu developed safe insulation from wood fiber for beverage coolers. This bio-based component offers an environmentally friendly alternative to toxic polyurethane foam. His innovation utilizes cellulose nanofibrils and wood flour as binders and stabilizers. The new foam demonstrates comparable thermal conductivity to conventional insulation materials. Researchers are working to enhance durability and explore new manufacturing possibilities.

A $215,280 Colorado home is being sold; but the buyer must remove the woman living inside
stories.summary: A unique property in Colorado is on the market but comes with a twist: prospective buyers cannot conduct inspections. The current resident, entrenched due to a drawn-out foreclosure process and personal loss, is determined to defend her home against eviction efforts. Real estate experts caution potential buyers about the substantial legal and financial pitfalls they may encounter in this unusual situation.

stories.title: What happened to 'Green Cards stapled to diplomas': Attorney reacts to proposal of $100,000 OPT fee
'Not Morocco, please': The human stories behind Spain's migrant crisis - report
'India always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy': Jaishankar speaks to Iran FM Araghchi
A Michigan woman owns 19 acres between two planned Toll Brothers communities
stories.summary: A woman from Michigan has initiated legal action against Toll Brothers concerning their wastewater management and access rights. Her property, undeveloped, is situated between two upcoming luxury housing estates. The lawsuit alleges that the developers have disregarded her property rights and neglected environmental regulations. She aims to reinstate her access easement and challenge the site plan approvals.

stories.title: 'Paradise for spies' no more: Japan launches first centralised intelligence body since WWII
'Pak-trained Mujahideen have turned their guns inwards': India slams Islamabad over PoK crackdown
stories.summary: India condemned Pakistan's admission of training and arming militants who have turned against the state. The Ministry of External Affairs also criticized Pakistan's harsh crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Over forty civilians were reportedly killed during the violent suppression of peaceful demonstrations. India stated that Pakistan's actions exposed its disdain for the region's innocent inhabitants.

stories.title: In 1924, Arctic charr from Lake Geneva were stocked into Lake Allos; a century later...
stories.summary: Introduced to Lake Allos in 1924, Arctic charr exhibit remarkable metabolic adaptations within just a century. These fish showcase rapid physiological changes, attributed mainly to their phenotypic plasticity, resulting in distinct body shapes. Notably, juveniles from Lake Allos consistently demonstrate elevated metabolic rates, even under controlled conditions. This research underscores the species' ability to swiftly adapt to their ever-changing environmental landscape.

stories.title: Assam floods: Death toll rises to 80; state shifts focus to rehabilitation, announces loan relief
Travel alert for visa holders in US: Immigration experts say domestic flying has become risky, alarming rise in number of airport arrests
Explained: India's first urban ropeway is almost here. Can Varanasi's sky-high commute change how Indian cities travel?
stories.summary: Varanasi is launching India's first urban public transport ropeway soon. This aerial system will connect the railway station with Godowlia Chowk. It promises to significantly reduce travel times and ease traffic congestion. The project serves as a test case for aerial mobility in heritage cities. This innovative transport model could influence future urban development across India.

stories.title: Chinese man didn't invite mother to his wedding over her looks; boss fired him and hired her
stories.summary: A company founder in China has sparked debate after revealing he fired an employee who refused to invite his mother to his wedding because he was ashamed of her appearance. The businessman later offered the employee's mother a job. The incident has divided opinion over workplace values, family responsibility and workers' rights.

stories.title: Japanese proverb of the day: Why "If in a hurry, take the roundabout path" teaches that slowing down is often the fastest way forward
IMD flags below-normal rainfall in August; heavy rain alerts for Kerala, Assam, Northeast
PM Modi, UK PM Andy Burnham discuss AI, defence, Strait of Hormuz in first phone call
Brazil's President confirms visa rejection for two US officials over alleged election meddling
CM Dhami inaugurates Kalash Bandhan Maha rally in Bhagwanpur on 650th birth anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas
stories.summary: Guru Ravidas Temple before flagging off the Kalash Yatra. He later carried the ceremonial Kalash on his head and proceeded to the event venue at CMD Inter College.

stories.title: CBI arrests 2 in Suvendu Adhikari aide murder case, probes political links
Govt summons Meta's global team over PM Modi post restriction, to question algorithmic bias
stories.summary: India's government has summoned Meta's global team to discuss Prime Minister Modi's post. Officials will question the social media giant on algorithmic bias and content moderation. Meta's global representatives will also appear before a parliamentary panel for scrutiny. Hyderabad police have also registered cases against Meta India's head. This marks an escalation in the government's oversight of the company's practices.

stories.title: Meet Kai Sato: The California sailor who spent 34 days lost at sea after his Hawaii dream turned into a fight for survival
Female mammals usually outlive males, but a 27-year study found the pattern was reversed among...
stories.summary: A comprehensive study spanning twenty-seven years has revealed that female birds face lower survival rates compared to their male counterparts. This trend has been observed in thirty-five distinct bird species throughout North America. The challenges posed by migration and reproduction seem to disproportionately affect females. Furthermore, genetic factors related to sex chromosomes may play a role in this issue.

stories.title: Lost in an Australian rainforest for 17 days, this mother survived by refusing to give up on her children
US downlists Razorback Sucker after one population grows from 100 to 36,000 fish
stories.summary: After more than 30 years of conservation work, the US Fish and Wildlife Service has reclassified the razorback sucker from endangered to threatened under the Endangered Species Act. The freshwater fish, found only in the Colorado River basin, has recovered through habitat restoration, fish stocking and control of invasive species. However, ongoing threats such as drought, changing river flows and non-native predators mean the species will continue to receive legal protection while recovery efforts move forward.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Taylor Swift: ‘My response to anything that happens, good or bad, is to keep making things,’ and how creativity can outlast every setback
stories.summary: In Taylor Swift's view, the act of making serves as a meaningful response to both adversities and triumphs in life. This creative outlet aids in managing complex emotions and builds inner resilience. Similar to the likes of several other creators, who transmuted their difficulties into impactful art, the process of creation alone provides fulfillment, independent of outside validation.

stories.title: 3,400-year-old Bronze Age log boat helped archaeologists uncover the River Trent
Tahir Hussain gives first public reaction after being sentenced to life in prison
Thousands of rubber ducks raced through a London canal to raise money for critically ill children, turning a charity event into a colourful spectacle
US, Israel considering land blockade to cripple Iran's economy: Report
139 Indians released from Russian Army, 2 dozen remain: MEA warns against shady job offers
Visa revocation, travel ban for reckless drivers: US says no second chance to those who put American lives at risk

Australian tree dropped from aeroplanes over Florida's Everglades

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain gets life imprisonment; 18 killed trying to breach Morocco border, army sent to Ceuta & more
Delhi riots 2020: Why Tahir Hussain escaped death penalty in IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
stories.summary: A Delhi court sentenced Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment. They were convicted for the murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma. The court rejected the death penalty, citing reformation possibilities. The prosecution argued the case was rarest of rare. The conviction occurred after the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Banksy: ‘People forget that invisibility is a superpower,’ and why choosing what not to share is a form of freedom
stories.summary: Banksy's quote highlights privacy as a superpower in today's world. Modern culture increasingly values visibility over personal discretion and control. The artist's anonymity allows their impactful art to speak for itself. This perspective challenges the notion that constant sharing equates to success or validation. Choosing what remains private offers a powerful form of personal independence.

stories.title: Flagstar 2021 data breach victims can claim up to $25,000 before August 11
stories.summary: Flagstar Bank has agreed to pay $31.5 million to settle a class action lawsuit over two cyberattacks in 2021 that exposed the personal information of more than 2.1 million customers. Eligible customers could receive payments ranging from about $60 to as much as $25,000, depending on their claims, if they submit the required forms by August 11, 2026.

stories.title: US state department uses AI-generated map that mislabels African countries at Brazil conference
Meet Alexander Zanders: The founder revolutionising Africa's 'unbankable' farmers into a $100 billion opportunity with just a credit assessment
stories.summary: UfarmX is revolutionizing the agricultural finance landscape in Africa by establishing a robust, data-driven credit system for farmers. Founded by Alexander Zanders, the company seeks to bridge the crucial financing gap faced by millions of farmers. Already, UfarmX has successfully assessed thousands of farmers, enabling meaningful commerce, and is changing how agricultural investments are perceived throughout the continent.

stories.title: Meet Lucas Tadao: 14-year-old Brazilian student who turned cassava peels into biodegradable trays that could help replace Styrofoam and reduce plastic pollution
How beavers are restoring rivers, wetlands, and wildlife across North America
stories.summary: Once nearly eradicated due to extensive fur trapping, beavers are making a notable comeback in North American rivers. Their innate talent for constructing dams contributes to the formation of ponds and wetlands, which support a wide array of wildlife. The rejuvenated habitats formed by beavers enhance resilience against droughts and wildfires in arid areas.

stories.title: Bhiwandi building collapse: Contractor, owner under lens; collector says structure was beyond repair
How Iran's military ran a $4bn gambling network as part of a sanctions-dodging op: Report
In 1997, a mysterious sound echoed across the Pacific. Years later, scientists traced the 'Bloop' to Antarctica
Ethanol blending saved consumers Rs 30/litre during crude spike: Govt
stories.summary: The petroleum ministry defended India's ethanol blending program on Friday. It stated that blending saved consumers nearly thirty rupees per litre. Food security obligations always take precedence over ethanol production needs. Rice is only one approved feedstock, used when surplus stocks are available. Ethanol blending acts as insurance against global oil price shocks.

stories.title: India, Bhutan sign Rs 4,000-crore credit pact, review development projects
stories.summary: India and Bhutan reviewed development projects and signed a Rs 4,000-crore credit line. They also expanded cooperation in the health sector and approved new projects. India provided financial and technical assistance for various initiatives. Electric vehicles were handed over as part of green mobility support. The two nations also inaugurated new parks developed under Indian funding.

stories.title: Punjab man Gurpreet Singh added to FBI’s ‘most wanted’ over alleged drug trafficking, illegal arms trade
Quote of the day by Richard Feynman: “The first principle is that you must not fool yourself and…”
A Swedish doctor spent 80 minutes trapped beneath river ice. Months later, she returned to work after one of medicine's most extraordinary recoveries
Netherlands tried to recreate prehistoric Europe on reclaimed land
70-million-year-old mammal fossil discovered in Mongolia rewrites the story of early mammal evolution
stories.summary: A new fossil from Mongolia's Gobi Desert has reshaped mammalian evolutionary understanding. This 70-million-year-old Tamirkhan balcarceli fossil belonged to zhelestids, which were previously misunderstood. The complete skeleton shows zhelestids were not early placental mammals as once thought. Instead, they were part of the extinct zalambdalestoid lineage, which evolved similar teeth independently. This discovery alters interpretations of mammalian diversity during the Late Cretaceous period.

stories.title: This Brazilian truck driver has built more than 1,700 wooden homes for stray dogs and cats, giving them shelter from rain and cold
Scientists say massive Pacific Ring of Fire eruptions may have cooled Earth for centuries
stories.summary: Large volcanic eruptions from the Pacific Ring of Fire influenced past climate. These eruptions correlate with major glacial advances and cold spells. Over eighty percent of glacial advances occurred near significant eruptions. Volcanic sulphur aerosols cause atmospheric cooling and reduce solar radiation. These eruptions may have intensified the 8.2 ka cold event.

stories.title: A Massachusetts mother helped save one of America's dirtiest rivers
A wild Himalayan spice is helping 200 families protect 100 sq km of forest while generating an income of Rs 39 lakh
stories.summary: Indigenous communities in Arunachal Pradesh are now earning livelihoods from a native spice. This wild Himalayan spice, known locally as Khagi, is helping over two hundred families. The community-led system for harvesting and marketing the spice supports forest patrols and biodiversity monitoring. This initiative provides a direct economic incentive for people to protect their forests and agricultural land. The project also contributes to the conservation of important transboundary wildlife habitats.

stories.title: Indian national in US on visitor visa jailed for $3.7 million fraud scheme targeting elders
Scientists trained 182 pet dogs to sniff out one of America's most destructive invasive insects, and most successfully found its hidden eggs
Archaeologists discovered Spain's oldest known Roman library inside a villa in Córdoba
stories.summary: Archaeologists identified a room at Fuente Álamo as the oldest Roman library. This space was previously thought to be a shrine to the god Mithras. The library's architecture matches known Roman library designs and is the westernmost in the empire. Its discovery highlights the cultural ambitions of its wealthy owner. This finding offers a unique glimpse into Roman intellectual life in Baetica.

stories.title: TASMAC corruption case: Supreme Court grants DMK's Senthil Balaji interim protection from arrest
14-year-old Montana boy uses Rodeo Lasso to save drowning man on camping trip
stories.summary: A family camping trip in Montana turned into a dramatic rescue when 14-year-old Jory Thomas used his rodeo lasso skills to save a man from the fast-moving Yellowstone River. After a raft and paddleboard crashed into a bridge pillar, one person was swept downstream. Jory roped the man on his first attempt and pulled him safely to shore before emergency responders arrived.

stories.title: U.S. avocado imports cut chemical use, reduce nitrogen pollution by 10%
stories.summary: New United States import rules for Mexican avocados prompted growers to reduce chemical use. This change significantly lowered nitrogen pollution in nearby Mexican waterways. Stricter inspections and phytosanitary certificates encouraged more careful pest management practices. The market access incentivized cleaner production methods without halting trade. This demonstrates how trade policies can yield unexpected environmental benefits.

stories.title: World's first power plant: Salt water meets fresh water to generate electricity
Supreme Court grants Omar Abdullah divorce after settlement with estranged wife Payal
Solved water crisis by turning seawater into drinking water using solar power
In 2003, a retired man planted trees on forgotten land alone; 20 years later, it had become one of Sao Paulo's largest urban forests
SP pressures opposition to take up Ayodhya donation scam, Congress focuses on police crackdown
BJP trying to force Muslims, minorities to worship Hindu deities, says Owaisi; DMK slams Vande Mataram bill as 'fraud'
stories.summary: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi slammed the bill criminalizing insult to Vande Mataram. He stated the bill forces minorities to worship Hindu deities and violates religious freedom. DMK MP A Raja called the legislation a fraud against India's secular fabric. Congress questioned the Home Minister's absence during the bill's passage. Opposition parties argue the government is imposing its views on citizens.

stories.title: Teen lifeguard saves 3 in massive waves on first day, earns Trump’s praise
stories.summary: A 16-year-old lifeguard named Ryder Williams performed a dramatic ocean rescue in Santa Cruz. He bravely pulled a 10-year-old boy from powerful surf at Seabright Beach. After his shift, Williams also helped save two more individuals in a separate incident. This heroic teenager received nationwide praise for his actions and bravery. His dedication highlights the importance of lifeguard training and quick response.

stories.title: America cancelled the world's most powerful particle collider, leaving a 22.5-km tunnel hidden beneath Texas for more than 30 years
400 hours counting caterpillars changed what we knew about LED lighting
Help families file compensation with Russian embassy, match DNA of Indians killed in war: SC to govt
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the MEA to appoint a nodal officer for families. This officer will coordinate with families of Indians who joined the Russian military. The court also asked for DNA matching and assistance with compensation claims. The Centre previously stated 217 Indians joined the Russian military, with 49 deaths reported. Efforts are ongoing to verify deaths and trace missing individuals.

stories.title: 14-year-old Indian American girl builds system to predict driver fatigue, eyes $25,000 prize
