stories.summary: A lucky lottery player in Florida has finally claimed the massive $800 million Mega Millions jackpot after the prize went unclaimed for more than four months. According to the Mega Millions website, the winning ticket was sold in Florida for the Tuesday, July 28 drawing. The jackpot carried a cash option of $344.2 million and became the third Mega Millions jackpot to be won this year. It also ranks as the 10th-largest jackpot in the history of the lottery.

stories.title: Use of maize & rice for ethanol production sees huge jump
Quote of the day by King Charles: "I'm a dangerous person because…" - a powerful lesson on caring deeply, speaking up and standing by your convictions
stories.summary: King Charles III's quote highlights the danger of caring deeply about issues. He acknowledged that his public activism as Prince of Wales would cease upon becoming king. Meaningful improvements often begin with individuals noticing potential for betterment. Strong convictions attract criticism, as history demonstrates with early environmental advocacy. Genuine engagement over passive observation drives progress and solves persistent problems.

stories.title: TMC vs TMC: Mamata urges EC to wrap up Trinamool dispute, opposes more time for rival camp
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee urged the Election Commission to conclude its party dispute inquiry. Her faction submitted its response while the rival group sought extensions. The rival faction has failed to submit its response despite two granted extensions. Mamata Banerjee believes the rival group is creating false evidence to develop their case. She requested an early conclusion to the proceedings without further delays.

stories.title: Researchers mapped 5,600km of Canada’s coast using 170 years of records; kelp persistence reached...
stories.summary: Recent historic charts and satellite data illustrate the impressive durability of kelp forests on Vancouver Island. In cooler, wave-exposed zones, eighty-eight percent of kelp survived over a century, while warmer, sheltered waters faced a concerning decline to fifty-two percent. These insights reveal crucial regional variations in kelp forest resilience amid rising temperatures and serve as pivotal guidance for future conservation initiatives aimed at protecting these essential marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Africa’s richest billionaire plans to donate one-third of his wealth
stories.summary: Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, will donate one-third of his wealth to charity. This significant philanthropic commitment is part of his succession plan. His daughter, Halima Dangote, revealed this plan in a recent interview. The billionaire's fortune is valued at approximately $36.5 billion. This donation aims to embed philanthropy into the family's long-term vision.

stories.title: US: Gladwin residents asked not to use toilet, shower after lightning damages wastewater plant
Meta tells IT ministry PM Modi's posts will get additional oversight, senior reviews
stories.summary: Meta assured the government of enhanced oversight for Prime Minister Modi's posts. This assurance followed the brief removal of his video addressing the NEET paper leak issue. The company admitted the video's temporary removal was due to an unintended error. Prime Minister Modi had discussed stricter measures against paper leaks in the video. Meta officials will meet government representatives soon to discuss this incident further.

Uttar Pradesh aims to become AI hub as CII summit brings together policymakers, industry leaders
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh hosted an AI Tech Summit to discuss artificial intelligence's growing role. The state aims to build a robust AI ecosystem through innovation and digital infrastructure. Lucknow is being developed as an AI City to foster research and entrepreneurship. Industry leaders urged partnerships for curriculum development and workforce upskilling. The summit highlighted Uttar Pradesh's potential as a national AI leader.

CJP protest: Delhi Police refutes claim that woman protester sustained gunshot injury
stories.summary: Delhi Police rejected claims of a gunshot injury sustained by a woman protester. Her medico-legal certificate showed only a simple blunt-force injury near her right ear. The official medical document did not mention any gunshot wound from the incident. Police advised the public to verify information before sharing such claims. The allegations were described as baseless by the Delhi Police department.

stories.title: California researchers surveyed Point Reyes lagoon 19 times and found 73 pelicans killed by otters
stories.summary: Along California's Abbotts Lagoon, river otters have been spotted hunting brown pelicans, resulting in the discovery of seventy-three deceased pelicans during nineteen research visits. This unexpected predation correlates with the rising otter population in Northern California. While fish are their usual fare, larger birds provide a richer source of energy. Recent reports indicate that pelicans are adapting by learning to evade the hunting otters.

stories.title: 500,000-year-old elephant bone tool found in England reveals advanced early human technology
stories.summary: An ancient elephant bone tool found in southern England reveals early human sophistication. This five-hundred-thousand-year-old implement was used for shaping stone tools precisely. Researchers found microscopic evidence of repeated use on the bone fragment. The discovery shows early humans planned and curated their technology carefully. This find offers new insights into Middle Pleistocene hominin intelligence and adaptability.

stories.title: Teen donates handmade plushies to hospital
stories.summary: Sophie Histed, a thirteen-year-old, crocheted thirty plush toys for children. She learned the skill online and practiced for four years. These handmade toys were donated to the paediatric ward at Calvary North Adelaide Hospital. Hospital staff appreciated the thoughtful gesture and distributed the gifts. Sophie plans to continue her charitable crocheting efforts in the future.

stories.title: Scientists discover ancient silk production in Uzbekistan nearly 2,000 years before the Silk Road
stories.summary: New evidence from Uzbekistan suggests ancient Central Asians raised silkworms around 2000 BCE. These findings challenge the traditional timeline for silk production in the region. Archaeologists discovered ancient silkworm cocoons and mulberry tree remains at Sapalli Tepe. This indicates local sericulture was established long before the Silk Road trade routes developed. These discoveries place silk production alongside other early Eurasian exchanges of knowledge and goods.

stories.title: Scientists changed the fats in honeybees’ diets before pesticide exposure; survival rose to 90%, compared with below 50% on other diets
stories.summary: New research suggests honey bees can better survive pesticide exposure. Bees fed polyunsaturated fats showed a 90% survival rate. This dietary fat type also supported nerve function and energy balance. The findings indicate nutrition can strengthen bee resilience against agricultural stressors. This knowledge could inform bee diets and pollinator habitat planning.

stories.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations Amendment Bill amid disruptions and political debate. Rahul Gandhi attacked the government over alleged police action and education privatization. Union ministers rebutted Gandhi's claims, calling them baseless and false allegations. The bill introduces stricter punishments for examination-related offenses and paper leaks. This legislation aims to ensure fairness and prevent unfair means in public examinations.

stories.title: Israel elections explained: How they work, who’s in the race and what’s at stake
An Oregon EMT disabled ambulance cameras she says recorded patients without notice
stories.summary: A former EMT from Oregon has filed a lawsuit against her employer for $800,000, alleging wrongful termination after she disabled covert recording cameras present in ambulances. The company reportedly set up these cameras without informing patients or obtaining their consent. This case raises significant issues regarding patient privacy and the increasing trend of surveillance, particularly given the strict recording regulations in Oregon.

stories.title: The Republic of discontent: Seven decades of student revolt in India
stories.summary: From a food riot in Calcutta to a satirical cockroach party that just cost a minister his job, India’s students have spent seven decades proving they are the country’s most unpredictable political force.

stories.title: Meet the 13-year-old who designed affordable ‘allergy spoons'
stories.summary: Abigail Stein developed an ingenious spoon designed to identify food allergens, providing a safety net for students with severe allergies during school meals. This innovative Allergy Spoon changes color upon detecting specific allergens, enhancing awareness and safety. Abigail was celebrated as a leading finalist in a prestigious young scientist challenge, with aspirations that her practical solution will address a significant concern for many families.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'advice' to PM Modi, and 3 guarantees to students over police action on protesters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of denying him Lok Sabha speech rights. He refused to apologize for blaming Amit Shah for police brutality. Gandhi demanded the Home Minister's dismissal and an independent probe. He alleged police used pellet guns and nail-fitted lathis on students. Gandhi promised justice and accountability for the injured students.

stories.title: Australia built a $187,000 electric fence across Wild Horse Plain, but the real reason lies beneath one of its rarest alpine wetlands
stories.summary: A new electrified fence protects rare alpine wetlands in Kosciuszko National Park. This enclosure safeguards endangered sphagnum bogs and associated fens from wild horse impacts. Horse activity damages these vital peatland ecosystems and their stored carbon. The $187,000 project was funded by biodiversity offsets from Snowy 2.0. This targeted measure protects a small but environmentally important area within the park.

stories.title: A trekking pole pierced a nurse through the torso; he then hiked 10 miles for...
stories.summary: In an incredible display of resilience, a nurse endured a life-threatening injury on Granite Peak in Montana. With a pole piercing his side, he bravely trekked over ten miles down the treacherous terrain. Relying on his medical expertise, he evaluated his injuries and chose to make the strenuous descent, aided by his friends. Now on the mend, he dreams of conquering the mountain again next year.

stories.title: Half of England declared in drought as July records near-zero rainfall
Evening News Wrap: Air India crash probe finds no fuel switch fault; RS clears Vande Mataram Bill & more
Florida sixth grader Naboshree Santra developed biodegradable soilshade balls designed to...
stories.summary: An 11-year-old Florida student has reached the finals of a national science competition. Her innovative soilshade balls help farmers conserve water during dry weather conditions. This eco-friendly invention slows evaporation and keeps soil moist for extended periods. She will compete for a $25,000 prize and mentorship from 3M scientists. The competition celebrates young innovators using STEM to solve real-world problems.

Inside China's fake Paris: The $1 billion replica with an Eiffel Tower and French streets that fooled the internet

Times Samman Dehradun 2026: A tribute to brave hearts from Sainya Bhoomi
Vande Mataram Bill 2026 explained: What changes and what punishment it proposes
Bihar transgender welfare board approves proposal to build temple dedicated to PM Modi
stories.summary: The Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board approved constructing a temple for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. A board member stated the prime minister provided the community with respect and rights. This proposal was moved during the board's inaugural meeting after the new act's implementation. The board functions under the Bihar government's Social Welfare Department for community empowerment. This decision reflects the transgender community's institutional representation in the state secretariat.

Over 1 lakh schools run with just one teacher; Andhra tops list with 16,357

In 2018, an undocumented migrant scaled a Paris apartment building to save a four-year-old boy hanging from a fourth-floor balcony, earning the nickname 'Spider-Man of Paris'
stories.summary: Mamadou Gassama, an African migrant, rescued a child hanging from a Paris balcony. His brave actions led to him being honoured by the French president. Gassama received French citizenship and an internship with firefighters. This incident brought Gassama international recognition and a new life.

stories.title: Barracuda bites Texas girl, 13, but cannot shake her ocean dream
stories.summary: A Texas teenager is recovering after a rare barracuda attack during a family vacation. Claire Macdonel experienced the frightening incident in shallow waters while wearing a shiny bracelet. She is now home and preparing for surgery to repair her hand injury. Despite the painful ordeal, Claire still dreams of becoming a marine biologist. Her family shares the story to raise awareness and encourage water safety precautions.

stories.title: For more than 300 years, the Bermuda petrel was believed extinct. A remarkable discovery in 1951 gave the 'lost bird' a second chance
stories.summary: The Bermuda petrel, once thought extinct, was rediscovered in 1951. A young naturalist, David Wingate, led a long recovery effort for the cahow. Conservationists protected nests and restored Nonsuch Island for the seabirds. The cahow population has grown, though challenges remain from storms. This story highlights species recovery and the importance of habitat restoration.

stories.title: 'Donate your $1 trillion fortune by 2036': Nobel economist challenges Elon Musk after his 'money won't matter' prediction
stories.summary: Nobel laureate Daron Acemoglu challenged Elon Musk to donate his fortune by 2036. Musk responded positively, suggesting he may consider a major philanthropic move. His past giving has focused on science, education, and technology initiatives. Donating such a vast sum presents practical challenges regarding asset transfer and oversight. This potential commitment marks a notable shift in his philanthropic approach.

stories.title: E20 petrol and vehicle mileage: What Nitin Gadkari said amid growing concerns

MEA goes the meme way to reinforce India’s position on J&K, Ladakh

Researchers studied 1,561 forest plots across 10 tropical countries; non-native trees formed 28% of stems in young moist forests, but declined as the canopy returned
stories.summary: Young tropical forests show many non-native trees while canopies remain open. As forests mature and canopies close, these non-native species tend to decrease. This pattern was observed across ten tropical countries in a recent study. Early forest regeneration is vulnerable to invasive species, which can establish easily. Understanding these dynamics aids effective forest restoration planning and native ecosystem recovery.

stories.title: Inside Coober Pedy: The Australian desert town where thousands escaped 50°C heat by building an entire underground world beneath the Earth
stories.summary: Coober Pedy, Australia, features a unique town built underground by opal miners. Residents live below the surface to escape the harsh desert climate and high cooling costs. This subterranean living provides stable temperatures year-round, offering practical comfort and savings. Underground homes and businesses are common, transforming excavated mining areas into functional spaces. The town's success depends on specific geological conditions and dry weather for construction.

stories.title: Indian national Amritpal Singh added to FBI’s 'Most Wanted' list in drug trafficking case
E20 petrol row: Arvind Kejriwal alleges 'strong-arm tactics’; BJP hits back
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal raised concerns over the Centre's alleged pressure on automakers regarding the compatibility of vehicles with E20 petrol. He suggested that vehicles manufactured before 2023 might suffer from damage and performance issues. However, the BJP dismissed these allegations, referencing statements from leading industry figures who confirmed E20 petrol’s safety following comprehensive testing and validation, thus reinforcing the automotive sector's support for the E20 initiative.

stories.title: Often called Japan's Titanic, the 1954 sinking of Toya Maru claimed more than 1,500 lives and reshaped ferry safety
In 2006, a rescued dog saved Houssein Hamze from a bomb; in 2026, he refused to flee Lebanon and stayed to care for hundreds of animals
stories.summary: Houssein Hamze turned his life around after his dog saved him from a devastating bomb attack, and he founded a shelter for abandoned animals in his village. Ignoring the threat of drone strikes, he continually provided food and water for displaced animals. His remarkable dedication attracted international recognition and donations, allowing him to persevere in his mission of promoting kindness towards animals.

stories.title: Bermuda snails were thought to be extinct from the island, a decade later breeders have released over 100,000 of them back
stories.summary: Once thought to be lost forever, the incredible Bermuda snail has been successfully revived. A decade ago, a small group was rediscovered and subsequently bred at Chester Zoo. Thousands were released back into safeguarded woodland areas in Bermuda, where six colonies have thrived. This success not only supports ecosystem recovery but also allows conservationists to shift their attention to breeding another rare native snail species.

stories.title: Russia's Telegram crackdown: Pavel Durov charged with aiding terrorism, puts him on international wanted list
Captain Cook released pigs and goats in New Zealand to feed future sailors
Largest Private Land Donation: Tompkins turns Patagonia purchase into park

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi praised youth protests and criticized the education system in Parliament. He stated that every Indian should be proud of the youth's actions. Rahul also shared a student's definition of a true student. He alleged rampant privatization and RSS capture of the education system. The opposition leader targeted home minister Amit Shah over alleged police actions.

stories.title: Oregon engineer spent $100,000 on a retired Boeing 727 and turned it into a home
Ancient footprints found in Kenya reveal how early human relatives may have travelled and lived together 1.43 million years ago
stories.summary: Ancient footprints found in Kenya offer rare glimpses into early human relatives. These impressions date back approximately 1.43 million years to a lakeshore environment. The tracks suggest several large-bodied individuals moved together across muddy ground. This discovery provides new evidence about hominin body size and social organization. The findings reshape current ideas about Homo erectus and Paranthropus boisei.

stories.title: Coal block scam case in Supreme Court: Ex-PM Manmohan Singh gets clean chit two years after his death
El Salvador archaeologists lifted a burial sealed beneath 2,800-year-old volcanic ash; the person lay face down with a sea turtle-shaped vessel near one hand
stories.summary: Archaeologists discovered a 2,800-year-old burial in El Salvador clutching a sea turtle vessel. This Mesoamerican burial may belong to a pre-Maya civilization which practiced human sacrifice. The skeleton was found under volcanic ash from an eruption dating to 850-830 BC. Cassava remnants found in the pit symbolize continuation and spiritual resonance. Further chemical analysis will reveal more about the individual's life and diet.

stories.title: One of America's most active volcanoes: How Pagan Island became home to just two residents
Spain's 'cannibal cave': New fossils reveal adults were also eaten by Homo antecessor
China lost more than 50% of its mangrove forests by the 2000s, now it has restored 22,500 hectares of the trees
stories.summary: China has made remarkable strides in restoring its mangrove ecosystems, committing to large-scale projects that have expanded coverage significantly. By planting and revitalizing thousands of hectares, not only has biodiversity surged, but the quality of these crucial habitats has also seen improvement. Robust legal measures now safeguard more than ninety percent of mangrove areas, complemented by the establishment of an international center focused on mangrove conservation in Shenzhen.

stories.title: A 66-million-year-old dinosaur highway in Bolivia reveals more than 16,000 fossil footprints from the final days of the dinosaurs
Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina plans Bangladesh return: 'I may be killed, I may be sent to prison'
stories.summary: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh by December. She is prepared to face arrest, imprisonment, or even execution upon her arrival. Hasina fled the country in August 2024 after widespread protests ended her rule. Her party faces repression and legal proceedings following the change in government.

stories.title: Delhi Police serves notice to X over 'derogatory' posts targeting constitutional heads
stories.summary: Delhi Police has requested X to remove content deemed defamatory towards constitutional authorities. The platform must also provide user details and preserve all related data. This action follows similar directives for posts targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The police social media monitoring team continuously scans for objectionable online material. These developments occur amid heightened political tensions following recent student protests.

stories.title: In 2001, scientists released beetles to fight an invasive tree. Years later, an endangered bird had lost 94% of its habitat along one western river
Antarctica averages minus 55°C at Vostok Station, yet a lake remains liquid beneath four kilometres of ice
stories.summary: Lake Vostok, a massive body of water, lies four kilometers beneath Antarctic ice. This subglacial lake remains liquid due to insulating ice and geothermal heat. Its existence challenges our understanding of life's extreme limits and nature's magic. The lake has been isolated from the atmosphere for millions of years. Scientists continue to study this unique environment and its potential inhabitants.

stories.title: A 13-year-old boy was airlifted after a rabid beaver attacked him at a Maryland state park, forcing officials to close the swimming beach
NEET-UG leak probe: CBI gets 3 more days to file annexures in chargesheet, hearing on August 3
stories.summary: A special court will consider the CBI's chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. The agency filed charges against thirteen accused, including NTA experts and coaching associates. Investigations uncovered the entire conspiracy from paper leak sources to beneficiary candidates. "These devices could create supply chain vulnerabilities that could disrupt US economic and national security and could create a cybersecurity risk that threatened American critical infrastructure," the agency said. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr added, "The FCC will continue to do our part to secure America’s critical supply chains."

stories.title: In 1934, this Pennsylvania mountain went from a hawk killing ground to the world's first raptor sanctuary and changed bird conservation forever
Middle East war escalates: Multiple dead in US-Saudi strikes in Iraq; Iran targets Hormuz ships - top developments
stories.summary: United States and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Iran claimed to have intercepted oil tankers and fired missiles at US installations. Eight Iraqi PMF members were killed in the joint US-Saudi attacks. Oil prices climbed amid concerns over energy supply disruptions. Diplomatic efforts continue as tensions between nations rise.

stories.title: Our FTAs fair & equitable, protect farmers, MSMEs, labour sector: Govt to NDA MPs
stories.summary: Government ministers defended trade pacts, contrasting them with past agreements. These new deals involve larger economies and aim for balanced growth. Fisheries sector exports have doubled, showing significant economic expansion. New markets are emerging, offsetting reduced exports to the United States. The government secured substantial committed investments from European and New Zealand trade partners.

stories.title: Shark attack rescuer Charlie Verco breaks world paddleboarding record
stories.summary: Australian paddleboarder Charlie Verco won his fourth Molokai to Oahu world championship in Hawaii in record time, just weeks after rescuing a woman during a great white shark attack off Sydney's Coogee Beach. The trained surf lifesaver said a relaxed approach helped him break the previous course record by three minutes.

stories.title: 'Deeply concerning': In UNSC, India strongly condemns attacks on commercial ships near Hormuz
stories.summary: Speaking at an open debate of the United Nations security council on the situation in the Middle East, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, said the recent escalation after a brief lull in fighting was deeply worrying. He urged all sides to return to dialogue and diplomacy to prevent the conflict from worsening.

stories.title: Oman proposes Gulf-backed voluntary fees to use Hormuz
stories.summary: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states for managing the Strait of Hormuz. This proposal includes collecting voluntary fees for ships utilizing the vital waterway. Iran has yet to respond to the Omani proposals for trade disruption resolution. The plan aims to avoid sole Iranian control and make fees voluntary. Gulf Cooperation Council ministers met to discuss waterway safety and cooperation.

stories.title: Italy's fertility rate falls to 80-year low: Report
stories.summary: Italy's birth rate fell nearly four percent last year, reaching a historic low. The fertility rate dropped to 1.14 children per woman, a significant decline. Economic pressures and a lack of support for working mothers contributed to this trend. This rate is far below the 2.1 needed for a stable population. Motherhood desires clash with job insecurity and high living costs.

stories.title: New chapter in reading: AI companion tools let readers chat with books
stories.summary: New artificial intelligence tools now let readers ask questions directly to books. These innovative platforms offer e-books and audiobooks alongside AI chatbots for immediate answers. Companies like Sinai.ai and Amazon's Audible are developing these interactive reading experiences. However, copyright and author compensation remain significant unresolved issues for these tools. Some platforms are exploring ways to pay authors and publishers for their content.

stories.title: US envoy Gor to visit Bangladesh as Dhaka deepens ties with Beijing
stories.summary: US special envoy Sergio Gor will visit Bangladesh on July 30. He will meet Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and the foreign minister. This visit follows Prime Minister Rahman's recent tour of China. The US seeks understanding of Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities. Washington remains concerned over China's economic corridor proposal.

stories.title: NEET has flaw in design, it is not necessary: DMK's Dayanidhi Maran
stories.summary: DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran demanded NEET be scrapped in Lok Sabha. He argued the proposed paper leak law amendment misses the core issue. Maran highlighted DMK and Tamil Nadu's long-standing opposition to the medical entrance exam. He also raised concerns about Meta smart glasses recording protesting students. Maran mentioned issues with WhatsApp broadcast limits for MPs and a removed Facebook post.

stories.title: Union minister, BJP MP got NHB subsidies, mantri refunded it: Government
stories.summary: Union minister Bhagirath Choudhary and MP Lumba Ram received central scheme aid. Choudhary has since refunded the subsidy to the National Horticulture Board. The government informed Parliament about these financial assistance instances. Existing scheme guidelines lack specific conflict of interest provisions. All eligible applicants are treated equally under the transparent NHB mechanism.

stories.title: India slams POK elections, Pakistan's claims over Indus Valley legacy
stories.summary: India has condemned Pakistan's legislative assembly elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The Ministry of External Affairs called the polls a cosmetic exercise to hide illegal occupation. India reiterated its firm stance that the entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India. The spokesperson highlighted Pakistan's promotion of terrorism and religious fundamentalism. This stance questions Pakistan's claims to any pluralistic cultural legacy.

stories.title: Dealers can't keep over 400 tonne stock of sugar: Government
stories.summary: The government has capped sugar stock at 400 tonnes per dealer. Dealers must liquidate excess stock by August 1 and sell within thirty days. This measure aims to prevent hoarding and stabilize sugar prices. The essential commodities act was invoked to impose these restrictions. Sugar exports have also been banned amid monsoon deficit forecasts.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned as opposition seeks Shah statement on police action
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha adjourned for the day amid opposition protests demanding a statement. MPs demanded Union Home Minister Amit Shah explain police action against demonstrators. The House was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11 am. Later, legislative business was attempted while opposition MPs continued their sloganeering. The Deputy Chairperson adjourned the House till Wednesday as protests persisted.

stories.title: PM Modi's message to key ministries: Be youthful, dynamic and adaptable
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged government ministries to remain youthful and forward-looking. He stressed the need for young entrepreneurs' active participation in key sectors. Officials were asked to devise industry-aligned courses for emerging sector skills. Proactive communication is vital to counter misinformation on major national initiatives. Citizens must remain at the center of all policy decisions and governance reforms.

stories.title: Centre notifies 7th draft for ecological zones in Western Ghats
stories.summary: The Centre has released its seventh draft notification for ecologically sensitive areas. This proposal aims to protect 56,825 sq km across six Indian states. States have raised objections, primarily Kerala, citing livelihood concerns. The draft allows for phased implementation, potentially speeding up the process. This initiative follows previous attempts since 2011 to conserve the fragile region.

stories.title: 1 officer, 1 car: Government tightens rules for use of official vehicle for staff
stories.summary: Government has tightened rules for official vehicle usage by employees. Officers will now receive only one official car, even with additional charges. They are also barred from using PSU vehicles except during official tours. This aims to optimize vehicle utilization and prevent misuse of government assets. Strict compliance is sought from all ministries and departments.

stories.title: Centre may table bill to make deepfakes, digital arrest separate offences
stories.summary: The government plans to introduce a bill addressing digital arrests and AI deepfakes. Existing laws do not define these emerging digital crimes effectively. The Supreme Court urged the government to create specific offenses for these issues. This new legislation will categorize digital arrest and deepfakes as distinct offenses. Consequential punishments and asset freezing measures will be included in the proposed law.

stories.title: MBBS admissions: NMC puts focus on ability, not disability
stories.summary: New National Medical Commission guidelines assess functional abilities for disabled students seeking MBBS admission. Medical boards will now evaluate candidates' capabilities rather than just disability percentages. Enabling units will provide support and a barrier-free learning environment for these students. Reasonable accommodations and assistive devices will be considered before making admission decisions. Patient safety remains a key consideration while promoting inclusive medical education for all.

stories.title: UK company in spotlight as Nishikant Dubey vows 'disclosure' in Parliament
stories.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey plans to disclose information about a UK-registered company. He will reveal which Indian politician is a director in Backops Limited. Dubey stated that Brian Lovegrove and Ulrik McKnight are linked to this company. These individuals are associated with numerous companies and TV channels registered at one address. The MP will present these findings inside Parliament soon.

stories.title: NEET row: CBI chargesheets 13 in paper leak
stories.summary: The CBI has filed a chargesheet against thirteen individuals in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. These accused include three NTA subject experts and several middlemen involved in question distribution. The agency's investigation confirmed the circulation of leaked questions prior to the examination date. Digital forensics and expert opinions corroborated the accused's involvement in the paper leak. Further investigation is ongoing, with a supplementary chargesheet anticipated soon.

stories.title: Delulu opposition thinks youth are with it, Rahul suffering from FOMO: NDA
stories.summary: BJP and allies defended the government's handling of student protests and paper leaks. They asserted that the youth trust Prime Minister Modi's commitment to reforms. Opposition leaders were criticized for using students for political gains and spreading cynicism. The government highlighted its efforts to reform the education system and address concerns. Measures were taken to clean the examination system after incidents occurred.

stories.title: 1st direct freight train opens new India-Nepal chapter
stories.summary: India and Nepal have initiated a new era of rail connectivity. The first direct commercial container freight train arrived in Nepal last week. This new service is expected to significantly reduce transit times and logistics costs. The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link inaugurated in June 2023. Direct freight movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, boosting bilateral trade.

stories.title: What happened to Yonna? Twitch streamer reacts after e-bike accident on livestream
stories.summary: Twitch streamer and TikTok creator Yonna crashed an e-bike during a recent IRL livestream after losing control and hitting a gate. She first answered “No” when friends asked if she was okay but later laughed and joked about the incident. No serious injury has been confirmed. Yonna recently returned to Kai Cenat’s Streamer University 2026 as Drama Club director.

stories.title: Don't touch water bodies under garb of beautification, Supreme Court tells Bihar government
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the Bihar government to stop filling historic ponds in Darbhanga. This action follows allegations that the state is filling water bodies for public amenities. The court warned the state not to touch the ponds without its explicit approval. The project aimed to beautify and rejuvenate Gangasagar, Digghi, and Harahi Lake. The Supreme Court directed the government to ensure the ponds' areas remain intact.

stories.title: Congress, BJP spar over Pralhad Joshi's pick as education minister
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized Pralhad Joshi's appointment as education minister. Gandhi accused Joshi of defending rapists in a past TV interview. BJP spokesperson Anil Baluni refuted these claims, stating Joshi commented on remission processes. Baluni accused Gandhi of distorting facts for personal attacks. The exchange highlights a political dispute over the minister's past statements.

stories.title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
stories.summary: CRPF analysis indicates police action against protesters followed standard operating procedures. Non-lethal means like pellet guns were authorized for crowd dispersal. Force gradient was followed, with lower measures failing before pump action guns. Protesters and personnel sustained injuries during the July 20 incident. The matter is now sub judice before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world
stories.summary: India now ranks as the world's second-largest supplier of seafaring personnel. This significant achievement is highlighted in the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. The report indicates India's share of global sailors has doubled over the past five years. Indian officers comprise thirteen point four percent of the world's officer workforce. This growth positions India strongly within the global maritime industry.

stories.title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
stories.summary: The Supreme Court accepted a father's request concerning the air crash inquiry report. The government will submit the final report in a sealed cover to the court. An NGO questioned the inquiry's impartiality and adherence to standard procedures. The Air Accident Investigation Bureau anticipates completing its investigation within six weeks. The final report is expected to be ready for distribution around October 2026.

stories.title: After stalemate, government, opposition spar over paper leak law in Lok Sabha
stories.summary: Parliament debated a bill to strengthen penalties for exam paper leaks. Opposition members supported student protests and criticized police actions during demonstrations. Government speakers highlighted past paper leaks and PM Modi's reform efforts. They emphasized the bill's aim to protect student welfare and ensure fair examinations. The proposed law seeks to deter organized gangs and individuals involved in leaks.

stories.title: Kai Cenat defends Tyla from alleged catcaller during Disney World livestream, fans applaud response
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Kai Cenat defended singer Tyla from a man during a Disney World livestream. He confronted the individual who was allegedly shouting at the singer. The brief exchange was captured on the livestream and quickly went viral online. Fans praised Kai for his respectful and mature handling of the uncomfortable situation. The livestream also marked the reunion of Kai and Tyla after nearly two years.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Elif Shafak: 'Do not go with the flow. Be the flow' and how to break passivity
Trump, Zelenskyy discuss Patriot production, Russia peace talks at White House
stories.summary: US President Trump and President Zelenskyy met to discuss Ukraine's defense capabilities. They focused on expanding Patriot missile interceptor production and defense cooperation. The leaders also explored efforts to restart stalled peace talks with Russia. Ukraine's president described the meeting as positive and productive for future support. This visit coincided with Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral and a sanctions push.

stories.title: Twitch streamer NateDeBaiits heartbroken after fatal California birthday party shooting claims friend's life
stories.summary: A birthday party for Twitch streamer NateDeBaiits tragically ended with a shooting. One person died and six others sustained injuries during the California event. The deceased was identified as Desiderio Romero V, a close friend of the streamer. Police are investigating the incident which occurred after a fight broke out. No arrests have been made as authorities review evidence.

stories.title: Trump, Netanyahu hold 'excellent' White House meeting as Iran differences come into focus
stories.summary: US President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu met at the White House to discuss Iran. Both leaders sought to manage differences over the future course of the conflict. They also discussed implementing a US-Israel framework agreement with Lebanon. Discussions also covered expanding the Abraham Accords and Gaza stabilization efforts. Both leaders face domestic political challenges and changing regional dynamics.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Lao Tzu: 'Truthful words are not beautiful; beautiful words are not truthful' and a philosophy that can't be lied to
Why do people claim they crossed over to Canada from the US border by mistake?
'Every possible measure must be taken': Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal says no Indian seafarer should be caught in crossfire
stories.summary: Indian shipping minister directed officials to safeguard seafarers from geopolitical conflicts. The government prioritizes the safety and welfare of Indian mariners serving on merchant vessels. Officials reviewed security situations and diplomatic mission preparedness in conflict zones. A union reported Indian sailors trapped in a Ukrainian port facing drone attacks. Mental health support and pre-departure risk awareness programs were also emphasized.

stories.title: 'I regret it': Mehbooba Mufti claims Jantar Mantar remark a slip of tongue, apologises
stories.summary: Mehbooba Mufti apologized for her Jantar Mantar remark which appeared to justify force in Kashmir. She claimed the controversial statement was a slip of tongue and a misinterpretation. The PDP president stated that her words were taken out of context by political rivals. Governing NC rejected her apology and clarification, demanding a clear response. The party also asked her to apologize for her alliance with the BJP.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Kal Penn: "Growing up, I always had two interests and two passions; one being public service and the other being…" - a reminder that you don't have to fit into one identity
stories.summary: Kal Penn pursued both public service and acting, defying conventional career paths. He left a popular television show for a White House position, demonstrating his commitment. This dual pursuit highlights how varied interests can strengthen one's overall capabilities. Penn's journey shows that personal identity is richer than a single job title. Embracing curiosity and multiple passions opens unexpected and rewarding opportunities.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Army duo hurt in Uri accidental blast
stories.summary: Two Army jawans sustained injuries from an accidental blast near the Line of Control. The incident occurred in the Kamalkote area of Uri sector on Tuesday. Both injured soldiers were promptly transported to the Army Base Hospital in Badamibagh. Medical officials confirmed that both soldiers are currently in stable condition. There is no immediate threat to the lives of the injured personnel.

stories.title: ‘It hurts to remember’: Blind since 14, J&K pellet survivor searches for tomorrow
stories.summary: Insha Mushtaq lost her sight to pellet guns during 2016 Kashmir unrest. She now pursues education and a government job despite her visual impairment. Recent protests in Delhi have reopened old wounds for her. Pellet guns, introduced as non-lethal, caused hundreds of eye injuries in Kashmir. Her story highlights the lasting impact of these weapons on individuals.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Bus with Amarnath pilgrims slips into gorge, 39 hurt
stories.summary: Thirty-nine Amarnath pilgrims were injured when their bus fell into a gorge. The bus skidded off the road in Ganiwan, Ganderbal district, on Tuesday morning. A house broke the fall, preventing a more severe tragedy for the pilgrims. Injured devotees were moved to SKIMS in Soura for medical treatment. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha assured best possible care and safe return arrangements.

stories.title: 'Corruption on Earth': Iran indicts Trump over Khamenei killing, faces death penalty
'Don't praise me': Punjabi man stops van, rushes to save autistic boy from being hit at busy Surrey traffic
CBI files chargesheet against 13 accused in NEET-UG paper leak case; hearing tomorrow
After SC order, West Bengal govt says no action against NEET protesters, except those with criminal records
stories.summary: West Bengal will not take coercive action against students protesting the NEET paper leak. This relief excludes individuals with prior criminal records, aligning with Supreme Court directives. Several BJP-led states, including Bihar and Assam, have already withdrawn cases against protesters. Maharashtra's chief minister also ordered the withdrawal of cases against student demonstrators. The Cockroach Janta Party awaits further action on their demands.

stories.title: Law on delayed birth registration to be more stringent; govt says birth certificate gives one legal identity
Rescued After 30 Days Adrift: Solo sailor Kai Sato survives on scraps; container ship pulls him to safety
stories.summary: A California man survived thirty days adrift at sea after his sailboat lost its mast. Kai Sato was found nearly nine hundred miles from Hawaii by a container ship crew. He improvised repairs and collected condensation for water while surviving on limited food. The rescue operation took about an hour and a half to complete successfully. Sato expressed deep gratitude to the ship's crew for saving his life.

stories.title: Rare Andean Bear reappears in Bolivia; camera captures it wading into Parapeti river
stories.summary: A rare Andean bear has been captured on camera near the headwaters of Bolivia's Parapetí River, giving conservationists hope that the vulnerable species continues to use the protected forest. Experts say the sighting also highlights the link between wildlife conservation and protecting vital water sources.

stories.title: Remains of five infants found in French couple's home; partner made discovery
Arizona man secretly cut holes through Tucson's street curbs to steal stormwater
The US buried 85,000 cubic metres of nuclear waste beneath a Pacific island
American gambler spent $90 million buying 54,000 acres of logged Florida land
British swam Antarctica's freezing sea and helped protect 1.55 million square kilometres
Once known as the 'Sea of Death', China's Taklamakan Desert is turning greener with drone technology
Singapore built a floating solar farm in the sea, but thousands of barnacles turned it into an engineering challenge that could sink its 13,000 solar panels
stories.summary: Singapore uses floating solar farms to overcome land scarcity for renewable energy goals. Marine organisms like barnacles attach to pontoons, adding significant weight and reducing buoyancy. This biofouling accelerates corrosion and can damage electrical components of the solar arrays. Maintaining these offshore solar plants requires constant maintenance and inspections.

stories.title: 17-year-old proposes hybrid nuclear system to cut Antarctic CO₂ emissions by 3,254 tons
stories.summary: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power. The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions. It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions. This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.

stories.title: Divers once believed the Great Blue Hole was bottomless; then explorers discovered human remains deep inside
